The authors propose an LLM-based question-answering evaluation protocol that directly verifies whether salient conceptual meaning is preserved across translations. This alignment metric prevents models from scoring highly purely through language model fluency.

entry.title: Differentiable Interval Bottlenecks for Interpretable Anomaly Detection in Numerical Data

author.name: Lamine Diop, Marc Plantevit

entry.summary: DIFFINT introduces a differentiable interval bottleneck for autoencoders that constrains latent representations of numerical data into soft, human-interpretable hyper-rectangles. This allows the model to retain end-to-end differentiable feature extraction while directly explaining anomaly scores through explicit, readable numerical interval boundaries. The method matches the accuracy of black-box autoencoders while providing transparent diagnostic explanations.

entry.title: CORE: Improving Compositional Reasoning in MLLM Embedding via Reranker Distillation

author.name: Tingyu Song, Mingxin Li, Yanzhao Zhang, Dingkun Long, Chu Liu, Pengjun Xie, Yilun Zhao, Shu Wu

entry.summary: CORE addresses compositionality failures in multimodal embedding models, where models fail to distinguish between identical concepts with different attribute bindings. The method distills fine-grained relational understanding from a cross-attentive reranker into a dual-encoder embedding model using a specialized listwise ranking objective. This significantly enhances compositional retrieval accuracy without incurring the inference latency of full cross-attention.

entry.title: Distilling deep optical flow stereo methods to retrieve dense three-dimensional wind fields

author.name: Thomas J. Vandal, Dong L. Wu, James L. Carr, Derek J. Posselt, Elise Penn, Tristan Ballard, August Posch, Kate Duffy

entry.summary: This work applies deep optical flow distillation to retrieve dense three-dimensional atmospheric motion vectors directly from satellite stereo imagery. By replacing iterative window matching with distilled optical flow networks, the approach eliminates reliance on numerical weather prediction models and resolves height assignment ambiguities. This improves computational efficiency and spatial density for operational meteorological data assimilation.

entry.title: Latent Energy Action Planning with World Models

author.name: Phu Pham, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: Latent Energy Action Planning (LEAP) improves model-predictive control in latent world models by formulating trajectory planning as an energy minimization problem. By combining terminal latent goal alignment with state energy terms and optimizing via quasi-Newton solvers, the method ensures that decoded actions faithfully achieve desired target states. This mitigates common drifting and hallucination errors during long-horizon latent trajectory planning.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Robustness Risks in PII Detection Systems

author.name: Adeel Zafar, Slawomir Nowaczyk

entry.summary: This work uncovers severe robustness vulnerabilities in deployed Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection systems under natural distribution shifts. Benchmarking encoder-based NER, rule-based systems, and LLM classifiers across informal, noisy, and unstructured inputs, the authors show that real-world noise induces severe detection failures. This exposes substantial privacy and compliance risks in enterprise data protection pipelines.

entry.title: Projected Riemannian Gradient Descent for the Bures-Wasserstein Barycenter: Dimension-Independent Linear Convergence at Unit Step Size

author.name: A. Afham

entry.summary: This work analyzes the Bures-Wasserstein barycenter computation across positive definite matrices and introduces a Projected Riemannian Gradient Descent algorithm with dimension-independent linear convergence at unit step size. This resolves a known theoretical dichotomy in optimal transport, where existing convergence rates either scaled exponentially with matrix dimension or required vanishingly small step sizes. The algorithm accelerates computations across quantum information and optimal transport.

entry.title: FrOGS: Discrete Neural Sampler for Independent Alloy Configurations Across Chemical Conditions

author.name: Kyucheol Min, Elyssa Hofgard, Tess Smidt

entry.summary: The authors introduce FrOGS, a hybrid discrete neural sampler combining autoregressive models with continuous-time Markov chains to simulate alloy configurations across varied chemical conditions. The unified training objective avoids the mode-seeking bias of reverse KL divergence and yields absolute free-energy estimates without requiring auxiliary thermodynamic integration. This provides a scalable alternative to traditional Markov chain Monte Carlo in computational metallurgy.

entry.title: Occupancy-based Quantile Risk Control

author.name: Zihao Shi, Huajun Xi, Bingyi Jing, Hongxin Wei

entry.summary: The authors introduce Occupancy-based Quantile Risk Control (OQRC), a calibration method that provides exact finite-sample bounds for quantile risk measures. By partitioning the loss space using ordered calibration errors into a finite-occupancy problem, the method avoids the excessive conservatism of prior conformal techniques. It enables tight statistical risk certification across non-monotonic loss functions in critical ML deployments.

entry.title: Where Does Harness-Optimization Value Live? Localized Gains and the Budget-Splitting Trap in Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Michael Nguyen, Wei Chen Tan, Nurul Aisyah Hassan, Arvind Raman, Li Hua Lim, Ahmad Faiz Razak

entry.summary: The authors introduce HARNESSEVO to analyze how prompt scaffolding evolution affects frozen LLM agent performance by decomposing the harness into role, strategy, format, and reflection components. Through systematic ablation under fixed compute budgets, they show that performance gains concentrate overwhelmingly in task strategies, while joint evolution across all slots suffers from budget splitting. This provides clear architectural principles for optimizing agent scaffolding.

entry.title: Large Language Models in Resolving Contextual Knowledge Conflicts

author.name: Xinye Yang, Zhenyang Liu, Ruisi Li, Yuanyuan Lei

entry.summary: This paper presents ContextConflict, a benchmark evaluating how LLMs handle contradictions arising entirely within provided input contexts rather than against parametric memory. The authors categorize six conflict types, including temporal, inferential, and granularity clashes, and show that frontier models struggle significantly with internal context coherence. The findings provide crucial insights into failure modes of long-context and retrieval-augmented reasoning systems.

entry.title: FPCO-Dialog: A Multi-Turn False-Premise Benchmark for Correction and Cooperation in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jiayuan Ma, Yuqi Lu, Weiyang Guo, Chenrui Wang, Junyi Shu, Xuebo Liu, Min Zhang, Jing Li

entry.summary: FPCO-Dialog is a benchmark containing over 10,000 multi-turn interaction turns evaluating how vision-language models respond when users introduce persistent false visual premises. The authors discover that frontier commercial and open VLMs frequently capitulate to user misconceptions over extended dialogue turns rather than maintaining visual truth. This highlights a significant sycophancy and grounding challenge in multi-turn interactive multimodal systems.

entry.title: Lngram v2: Latent N-Gram Memory with Interpretable Discrete Representations

author.name: Yunao Zheng, Bin Wen, Xiaojie Wang

entry.summary: Lngram v2 expands latent discrete n-gram memory architectures by decoupling memory routing from backbone transformer width and introducing a context-aware grouped-query attention readout. These innovations eliminate previous capacity limits, enabling models to look up static patterns with discrete memory addresses rather than consuming parameter-heavy dense compute. The architecture improves both efficiency and interpretability across vision-language and NLP tasks.

entry.title: VisCAD: A Foundation Model Suite with Multimodal Industrial CAD Intelligence

author.name: JoyIndustrial VisCAD Team, Linxin Cai, Qiuhe Hong, Zhichao Huang, Guanlin Li, Hongsen Liu, Ziqi Liu, Yichen Long, Luya Wang, Yuchen Wang, Wenxiang Wu, Huimu Yu, Ning Zhang

entry.summary: VisCAD presents a foundation model suite tailored for automated industrial CAD generation, capable of converting multimodal design intents into executable DSL programs for both individual parts and complex assemblies. The model bridges the gap between narrow CAD tools and general-purpose VLMs by maintaining parametric constraints and physical mating kinematics. The suite demonstrates superior performance on complex factory-automation assemblies.

entry.title: Laplacian Frequency Hierarchies for Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting Training

author.name: Yixiong Yang, Sisheng Zhang, Qingsong Yan, Shaohuai Shi, Qiang Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Laplacian Frequency Hierarchies to accelerate 3D Gaussian Splatting by decomposing training into coarse-to-fine frequency stages. Low-frequency Gaussian fields are frozen and archived once optimized, allowing subsequent primitives to focus solely on high-frequency geometric residuals without carrying full computational overhead. This substantially decreases active primitive counts and GPU memory requirements during training while preserving rendering quality.

entry.title: Preprocessing Failure and Adversarial Detection in Depthwise-Separable Edge Vision Systems

author.name: Jannatul Masruk Mukta, Rifa Sanjida, Adrita Rahman Tory, Md. Saifur Rahman, Khondokar Fida Hasan

entry.summary: This study demonstrates that common input-preprocessing defenses against adversarial perturbations fail systematically when deployed on depthwise-separable CNN architectures. While effective on residual backbones, these defenses offer negligible protection on edge-optimized networks, highlighting a critical blind spot in mobile vision security.

entry.title: ToPO: Token-Conditioned Preference Routing for Attention-Based Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Juntao Xu, Shihong Li, Hoi Fan Au, Ning Zhu

entry.summary: ToPO introduces token-conditioned preference routing to improve direct preference optimization for latent diffusion models. By routing preference gradients through branchwise residual contrasts and cross-attention tokens, it aligns generative outputs with local user preferences rather than applying coarse global image scores.

entry.title: Persistent Identity Preservation in Generative Image Models: A Benchmark and Evaluation System

author.name: Mengwei Ren, Xuaner Zhang, Zhihao Xia

entry.summary: This paper presents a systematic benchmark evaluating persistent identity preservation across generative image paradigms, analyzing input-context prompting, fine-tuned LoRA adapters, and persistent identity layers. The study measures identity drift and fidelity across variable poses, expressions, and multi-subject compositions.

entry.title: Predictive Zonotope Reduction: Precise Runtime Monitoring under Uncertainty

author.name: Vladimir Krsmanovic, Florian Kohn, Bernd Finkbeiner, Milan Simovic

entry.summary: Predictive Zonotope Reduction presents an adaptive reduction algorithm for runtime safety verification of autonomous systems under sensor uncertainty. By dynamically choosing reduction operators based on instantaneous state geometries, the system minimizes over-approximation error when verifying temporal logic safety bounds.

entry.title: GIFT: Guided Intermediate Feature Training via Action-Oriented Structural Supervision for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yupeng Zheng, Xiang Li, Songen Gu, Yuhang Zheng, Shuai Tian, Weize Li, Linbo Wang, Chaoyue Li, Qichao Zhang, Haoran Li, Zhongpu Xia, Ya-Qin Zhang, Shuicheng Yan, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: This paper introduces GIFT, a representation learning framework that tackles the action-sufficiency gap where foundation visual models retain control-irrelevant details while omitting physical structure. GIFT provides intermediate feature supervision tailored to geometric constraints, entity affordances, and goal grounding. This structural guidance yields substantial performance improvements in downstream robotic manipulation policies.

entry.title: DNative-Twin: Decision Graphs and Digital Twins for Reconstructable Agentic Decisions

author.name: Junjie Pang, Zhenzhen Xie, Haoke Han, Ying He, Jing Wang, Gang Liu

entry.summary: The authors present DNative-Twin, a graph-native digital twin framework designed to record, audit, and replay agentic decision trajectories in enterprise workflows. By linking observed states, tool interactions, and organizational authorizations into a typed trajectory graph, the system allows deterministic replay and counterfactual testing of autonomous decisions. It offers a practical foundation for regulatory compliance and auditability in automated operations.

entry.title: SVG-Score: Human-Aligned Evaluation of Text-to-SVG Generation

author.name: Marco Cipriano, Leonardo Zini, Alexandra Schild, Valentin Teutschbein, Afsana Mimi, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi, Gerard de Melo

entry.summary: The authors present SVG-Score, an evaluation metric tailored for text-to-Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) generation that aligns closely with human visual judgments. They show that standard raster metrics like CLIPScore fail to detect typical vector defects such as color errors, object miscounts, and improper coordinate paths. SVG-Score provides a robust, human-aligned protocol for benchmarking vector graphic synthesis.

entry.title: TruncGradGS: Improved 3D Gaussian Splatting via Truncated Gradient Updates

author.name: Theo Morales, Nhat-Quynh Le-Pham, Robin Atkins, Binh-Son Hua

entry.summary: TruncGradGS introduces a piecewise truncated gradient formulation to address gradient vanishing during 3D Gaussian Splatting optimization. By ensuring that distant primitives receive meaningful gradient updates, it improves optimization stability and makes reconstruction significantly less sensitive to initial point cloud quality. The method delivers superior novel view synthesis and faster convergence across challenging scenes.

entry.title: ToolDF: Tool-Integrated Reasoning for Mixed-Authenticity Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Taewoo Kim, Young Han Lee, Nam In Park, Chanwoo Kim

entry.summary: ToolDF introduces an audio large language model framework for detecting mixed-authenticity audio deepfakes containing both genuine and synthesized components. Acting as an agentic orchestrator, the model analyzes acoustic scenes, selectively invokes source separation, and routes isolated components to specialized forensic tools to localize manipulations. This provides fine-grained, interpretable deepfake detection rather than brittle clip-level binary classification.

entry.title: Local Updates, Global Learning (LUGL): Playing Games with non-incremental Learners

author.name: David Milec, Spyridon Samothrakis, Michael Fairbank, Dennis J. N. J. Soemers

entry.summary: LUGL introduces a framework that allows non-incremental tabular algorithms like LightGBM to be trained in online self-play reinforcement learning regimes. By decoupling environment trajectory collection from global tree fitting, it enables gradient-boosted decision trees to operate in non-stationary RL settings without catastrophic forgetting. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on discrete, tabular board and card games compared to deep neural networks.

entry.title: Masked Autoregressive Speech Enhancement with Continuous Neural Audio Codec Representations

author.name: Yoto Fujita, Simon Leglaive, Laurent Girin

entry.summary: MARSE introduces a masked autoregressive speech enhancement framework that performs iterative decoding directly over continuous latent representations from neural audio codecs. The empirical findings reveal that continuous acoustic latents preserve higher speech intelligibility and naturalness than quantized discrete codec tokens in noisy conditions. The approach provides an effective paradigm for generative speech restoration without codebook degradation.

entry.title: SENTINEL-RL: Offloading Topological Reasoning from LLM Agents in the Security Operations Center

author.name: Uday Vallabhaneni, Cassie L. Cagwin, David J. Wild

entry.summary: SENTINEL-RL presents an architecture for autonomous Security Operations Center (SOC) agents that separates complex enterprise graph reasoning from natural language decision-making. By leveraging a heterogeneous graph attention network and PPO to summarize large authentication topologies into constrained action sets, the LLM is freed from graph hallucinations. This makes agentic cyber-incident containment reliable at large enterprise scale.

entry.title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing

author.name: Adheesh Sunil Juvekar, Onkar Kishor Susladkar, Kiet A. Nguyen, Muntasir Wahed, Nabeel Bashir, Xiaona Zhou, Tianjiao Yu, Vedant Shah, Ismini Lourentzou

entry.summary: EditVid is a unified, training-free video editing framework that integrates sparse causal memory, correspondence token injection, and soft latent blending. The method supports diverse manipulation paradigms, including attribute modification, style transfer, and subject replacement, while maintaining temporal coherence and identity preservation. It achieves substantial state-of-the-art gains over existing training-free video editing baselines.

entry.title: Frontier LLMs are effective batch optimizers: Assessing reasoning models in continuous and discrete settings

author.name: Frank Hu, Shriram Chennakesavalu, David Graff

entry.summary: The authors benchmark frontier reasoning language models as zero-shot batch optimizers across continuous and discrete search spaces. The findings indicate that while reasoning models exhibit strong semantic heuristics in rich, structured domains, they remain fragile and uncompetitive compared to classical numerical optimizers on purely mathematical functions. This establishes realistic operational boundaries for using LLMs as general-purpose optimization agents.

entry.title: Guide, Not Bind: Why Defeasible Priors Fail in Augmented Lagrangian Causal Discovery

author.name: Sairam Sundararaman, Sara Girdhar, Manit Narasimha Murthy, Samrudh N, Bhaskarjyoti Das

entry.summary: This paper investigates why soft expert priors enforced via Augmented Lagrangian methods fail in differentiable causal discovery. The authors prove that penalty-ramping schedules suppress correctly identified edges before data-adaptive mechanisms can override erroneous expert constraints, establishing necessary mathematical conditions for defeasible constraints. This clarifies longstanding optimization instability in continuous DAG structure learning.

entry.title: Pushing the (Decision) Boundaries: Dynamically Calibrating Differentially Private Noise to Explainability in Federated Learning

author.name: Michael Khavkin, Kichang Lee, Jaeho Jin, JeongGil Ko, Eran Toch

entry.summary: XCal-FL is a federated learning framework that dynamically calibrates Differential Privacy (DP) noise based on real-time model explainability and logit confidence during training. By calibrating noise injection to feature attribution quality, the method preserves explanation fidelity in safety-critical domains such as clinical image diagnostics without compromising formal privacy guarantees. This bridges the tension between patient confidentiality and trustworthy clinical interpretability.

entry.title: Prospective Coding Improves Learning in Deep Continuous-Time Recurrent Networks

author.name: Shivang Rawat, Mirko Morello, Flaviano Morone, David J. Heeger

entry.summary: This work proposes Recursive Quadrature Filters (RQFs), biologically grounded complex-valued temporal filters framed as diagonal state-space models. By augmenting continuous-time recurrent networks with prospective coding, the architecture predicts incoming inputs to mitigate temporal signal delays and vanishing top-down gradients. This improves long-range temporal integration across deep continuous-time recurrent networks.

entry.title: A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neural Network Realizations

author.name: Ruiyang Hong, Hrad Ghoukasian, Anastasis Kratsios

entry.summary: The authors derive a closed-form two-stage formula for non-parametric Lipschitz regression on metric spaces that features zero optimization error. They establish uniform high-probability error bounds and prove that this estimator can be implemented exactly by sparse deep neural networks. This bridges classical metric non-parametric estimation with the expressive capabilities of deep network architectures.

entry.title: Who Speaks for the Pruned? Visual Token Pruning as Coverage Optimization

author.name: Qingchan Zhu, Weihang You, Hanqi Jiang, Changdi Yang, Tianming Liu, Geng Yuan

entry.summary: This work proposes CoverPruner, a training-free token pruning technique for vision-language models that frames pruning as representational coverage maximization. Instead of greedily preserving high-scoring tokens, it ensures that every discarded visual token has a close semantic surrogate among the retained subset in projector space. This preserves critical visual evidence and boosts VLM inference efficiency across varied image reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Learning Informative Prior with Infinite-Dimensional Continuous Normalizing Flow for Bayesian Inverse Problem

author.name: Yang Zhao, Junxiong Jia, Tao Zhou

entry.summary: The authors propose an infinite-dimensional continuous normalizing flow model based on neural ODEs in Hilbert spaces to learn expressive prior distributions for PDE inverse problems. They establish the mathematical well-posedness of the continuous measure transformation and present training strategies for both paired and unpaired data. This enables mesh-independent Bayesian inversion in high-dimensional functional spaces.

entry.title: R$^{2}$Adapter: A Routing and Rewriting Adapter for Efficient Hybrid RAG

author.name: Yucan Guo, Miao Su, Saiping Guan, Long Bai, Zhongni Hou, Zixuan Li, Xiaolong Jin, Jiafeng Guo, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: This paper introduces R2Adapter, a lightweight plug-in adapter that dynamically routes queries between standard text retrieval and multi-hop graph retrieval while simultaneously rewriting query formulations. By bypassing expensive LLM reasoning calls for routing, it eliminates latency overheads in hybrid retrieval pipelines. Experiments show superior retrieval accuracy and significantly reduced inference latency compared to heuristic hybrid RAG systems.

entry.title: PACE: Towards Surfacing Hidden Conflicts in User Requests

author.name: Yoojin Kim, Jihyoung Jang, Hyounghun Kim

entry.summary: PACE establishes a benchmark to evaluate whether personalized AI assistants can recognize implicit situational constraints and refuse user requests that conflict with background context. Moving beyond surface safety filters, the dataset tests a model ability to cross-reference latent facts stored in an egocentric knowledge base before executing actions. The work establishes a vital benchmark for contextual safety and boundary-aware agentic systems.

entry.title: A Circuit for Plural Reference: How LLMs Represent and Retrieve Singular and Plural Entities

author.name: Anh Danh, Rick Nouwen, Massimo Poesio

entry.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability and causal intervention methods, this study isolates the attention circuit responsible for resolving singular and plural pronominal coreference in LLMs. The authors trace the specific attention heads that encode entity multiplicity, bind antecedents into sets, and route information to downstream pronoun prediction layers. This provides clear algorithmic insights into how transformer architectures handle grammatical number and entity grouping.

entry.title: RuleMem: Active Rule Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents

author.name: Xingyuan Zeng, Zuohan Wu, Quanming Yao, Yue Wang, Wei Liu, Libin Zheng, Jiuke Wang, Jian Yin

entry.summary: RuleMem proposes an active memory system that induces reusable Horn-clause logical rules from historical conversational dialogue to guide multi-turn reasoning and retrieval. Rather than passively storing unstructured episodic facts, the system evaluates induced rules using a Rule Perplexity Consistency metric to bridge temporal semantic gaps. This improves consistency and multi-hop reasoning over extended agent-user interactions.

entry.title: What Do CAE Simulation Agents Really Need Beyond a Generic Harness?

author.name: Jiasheng Shi, Tianhan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks LLM agents on configuring complex computer-aided engineering solvers, comparing specialized multi-agent architectures against a standardized execution harness. The findings reveal that complex multi-agent reflection and specialized prompts add little value over a simple single-agent harness equipped with robust execution feedback and error logs. The study calls for simplifying agent frameworks in computational physics and engineering.

entry.title: RealCADBench: Benchmarking Parametric CAD Modeling from Industrial Design Intents

author.name: JoyIndustrial VisCAD Team, Linxin Cai, Qiuhe Hong, Zhichao Huang, Guanlin Li, Zongzhen Li, Hongsen Liu, Yichen Long, Wei Wang, Yuchen Wang, Dongyue Yang, Huimu Yu, Xianwen Zhong

entry.summary: RealCADBench is an extensive industrial benchmark spanning over 12,000 tasks across 19 factory-automation domains that assesses CAD generation from engineering drawings, text, and photos into executable FreeCAD programs. By evaluating both discrete part modeling and multi-part physical assemblies, it establishes a realistic industrial standard for CAD generation. The benchmark highlights huge performance gaps between commercial frontier models and specialized design automation.

entry.title: PointGT: Simultaneous Geometry and Texture Editing for Point-Based Representations

author.name: Yanshu Zhang, George Shramko, Pratul P. Srinivasan, Ke Li

entry.summary: PointGT introduces a point-based 3D neural representation that enables concurrent geometric deformation and high-resolution texture editing, surmounting the rigid topological limitations of Gaussian splats and volumetric fields. By pairing a deformable point cloud with learned UV texture mappings, users can interactively sculpt and recolor complex 3D assets while preserving photorealistic multi-view consistency. The technique provides a powerful asset manipulation pipeline for creative 3D workflows.

entry.title: Auditing Patient Privacy in Medical Generative Models: Scalable Memorization Detection with DeepSSIM++

author.name: Antonio Scardace, Francesco Guarnera, Sebastiano Battiato, Daniele Rav\`i

entry.summary: DeepSSIM++ presents a self-supervised perceptual similarity metric tailored for scalable patient privacy auditing in medical generative models. By combining multi-scale feature aggregation with anatomy-preserving augmentations, it detects exact and near-verbatim training image memorization far better than generic metrics.

entry.title: Fill My Mirror: Geometry-Constrained Mirror Inpainting

author.name: Ofek Basson, Shimon Vainer, Yacov Hel-Or, Ohad Fried

entry.summary: Fill My Mirror addresses realistic reflection synthesis by using estimated 3D scene geometry to project visible elements into reflective surfaces prior to generative inpainting. A dual-mask diffusion strategy completes occluded reflections while preserving strict perspective and optical consistency.

entry.title: Axonal delay dispersion decides whether a neuron detects an event or a sequence, and predicts cortical column diameter

author.name: Cheng Bi, Jipeng Sun

entry.summary: This theoretical neurobiology study demonstrates how axonal conduction delay dispersion and dendritic coincidence detection determine whether individual cortical neurons detect simultaneous bursts or ordered sequences. The analytical model establishes a quantitative link between spike timing synchrony and the physical diameter of cortical columns.

entry.title: Real-Time Shape Control of Multi-Segment Soft Robotic Arms Using Koopman Operators with Global and Local Observables

author.name: Jiahe Wang, Eron Ristich, Sultan Haidar Ali, Eric weissman, Lei Zhang, Wanxin Jin, Yi Ren, Jiefeng Sun

entry.summary: The paper implements real-time shape control for continuous multi-segment soft robotic arms using Koopman operator theory formulated over both local and global observables. This formulation linearizes nonlinear continuum deformations, segment coupling, and inertial forces, enabling accurate posture tracking in constrained environments.

entry.title: NeoRed: A Knowledge-Logic-Alignment Multimodal Large Language Model for Neonatal Respiratory Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Yinan Liu, Hongtai Xia, Haoran Xu, Jiankang Hong, Jingkuan Song, Ye Luo

entry.summary: This paper presents NeoRed, a multimodal large language model designed specifically for neonatal respiratory disease diagnosis and report generation from chest radiographs and clinical data. It mitigates the clinical domain gap caused by adult-skewed training distributions through tailored clinical datasets and knowledge-logic alignment. Experimental results show enhanced diagnostic accuracy and report quality compared to general medical foundation models.

entry.title: Common-Witness Certificates and Sharp Feature Bounds for Counterfactual Image Auditing

author.name: Usef Faghihi, Amir Saki

entry.summary: The authors develop a mathematical auditing framework using common witness grades and nerve complexes to detect local-to-global inconsistencies in counterfactual image generation. The method generates finite incompatibility certificates to verify whether regionally plausible image manipulations fit a single globally coherent causal explanation. It provides rigorous mathematical bounds for auditing bias, manipulation, and causal consistency in generative vision models.

entry.title: Exploring the Potential of Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data

author.name: Xiangyang Miao, Kelu Yao, Yekai Huang, Xiaogang Xu, Junxiao Xue, Minjun Shen, Chenghui Lv, Shanji Liu, Yaying Chen, Chao Li

entry.summary: OmniRSCLIP extends contrastive vision-language pre-training to multi-source remote sensing data, integrating synthetic aperture radar, multispectral, and hyperspectral imaging without breaking RGB visual priors. It introduces Spectral-Spatial Basis Decomposition to project heterogeneous sensor channels into a unified embedding space compatible with pretrained CLIP backbones. This improves cross-modal retrieval and zero-shot earth observation classification.

entry.title: LongCounsel-8: A Benchmark Suite for Longitudinal Depression Tracking from Multi-Session Counseling Dialogues

author.name: Jiayi Li, Zhaomin Wu, Bingsheng He

entry.summary: LongCounsel-8 introduces a benchmark suite for tracking longitudinal depressive symptom changes across multi-session counseling dialogues. Grounded in standardized clinical progression patterns, it evaluates whether conversational agents can assess symptom severity trajectories over time without leaking target labels. This provides a rigorous foundation for developing and testing long-horizon mental health support agents.

entry.title: Test-time adaptation for speech enhancement with an autoregressive speech prior

author.name: Sofiene Kammoun, Simon Leglaive, Xavier Alameda-Pineda, Timo Gerkmann

entry.summary: This paper proposes a single-utterance test-time adaptation method for speech enhancement that adapts pretrained models to unseen noise conditions without labeled data. The adaptation objective minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence between enhanced speech outputs and an autoregressive clean-speech prior extracted from neural audio codec latents. The approach yields consistent speech quality improvements under severe acoustic domain mismatch.

entry.title: ENEAS: Embedding-guided Neural Ensemble for Adaptive Segmentation

author.name: Javier del Pino (SperidLabs), Salvador Rodr\'iguez (SperidLabs), Alejandro Garabito (SperidLabs), Javier \'Alvarez (SperidLabs), Chema Garabito (SperidLabs)

entry.summary: ENEAS introduces an embedding-guided neural ensemble for text-promptable object tracking and segmentation, overcoming common foundation model failures such as spatial fragmentation and visual hallucination during object exits. By enforcing semantic continuity constraints, it maintains robust instance boundaries and handles open-concept discovery across complex video sequences. The framework improves segmentation stability without requiring retraining of foundation backbones.

entry.title: RATL: Learning from Retrieved Residuals for Robust Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yuchen He, Yueyang Cang, Zhiyuan Ning, Ningyu Wang, Li Shi

entry.summary: RATL applies retrieval-augmented generation concepts to multivariate time-series forecasting by retrieving and learning from historical forecast residuals rather than raw target values. By querying past error patterns to dynamically adjust current predictions, the framework improves robustness against non-stationary distribution shifts. The plug-in method consistently boosts accuracy across multiple benchmark forecasting models.

entry.title: Adaptive Vision-Language Grasping via Composable Foundation Priors and Generalizable Grasp Synthesis

author.name: Sixu Yan, Shikang Wang, Binhua Huang, Xuanlai Tang, Guohua Fan, Fan Huang, Haoxuan Li, Yongkang Li, Yuhan Li, Bencheng Liao, Zeyu Zhang, Wenyu Liu, Hangxin Liu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: AdaRoboVLG proposes a modular vision-language grasping framework that decouples semantic task comprehension from physical grasp candidate synthesis. By relying on a generalized base policy grounded in physical kinematics and force-closure constraints, foundation model visual priors can be integrated modularly. This allows robotic manipulators to generalize across novel objects and diverse robot hand morphologies without retraining physical policies.

entry.title: ESPO: Error-Structured Prompt Optimization via Diagnose, Diversify, and Stabilize

author.name: Lihao Liu, Peng Tang, Kunwar Yashraj Singh, Shabnam Ghadar

entry.summary: This paper introduces ESPO (Error-Structured Prompt Optimization) to resolve the prompt bloat and instability seen in evolutionary prompt search methods. By structuring the optimization pipeline into error diagnosis clustering, diversified candidate proposal, and bootstrap stability selection, the method generates compact yet more effective system prompts. Benchmarks across seven NLP tasks show notable accuracy gains alongside concise prompt outputs.

entry.title: Learnable composition for neural operators

author.name: Zituo Chen, Baiming Zhang, Sili Deng

entry.summary: LatentDDM introduces a learnable domain decomposition method for neural operators to reduce adaptation costs when deploying surrogates to large physical geometries. A neural operator is pretrained exclusively on small local subdomains and subsequently frozen, requiring only a lightweight composition module to be trained for global domain coupling. This eliminates the necessity of generating costly full-scale high-fidelity simulations during model adaptation.

entry.title: The Gradient Does Not See Rank: Rank-Indifference in Matrix-CODI on ProsQA

author.name: Samuel Larson (Pebble ML)

entry.summary: This paper investigates latent continuous chain-of-thought models (Matrix-CODI) and shows that truncating intermediate reasoning state matrices to low rank causes almost no performance degradation. The authors reveal that standard gradient descent optimization exhibits rank-indifference, failing to utilize matrix capacity for parallel superposition of reasoning paths. This challenges prevailing theoretical assumptions regarding representational dimensionality in latent reasoning models.

entry.title: RobustSeiz: An Open-Source Framework for Benchmarking the Robustness of EEG Seizure Detection Models

author.name: Mohammad Mohammadi, Alireza Zarei

entry.summary: RobustSeiz provides an open-source benchmarking framework for assessing the robustness of EEG seizure detection architectures under controlled clinical distribution shifts. Standardizing four clinical scalp-EEG datasets into BIDS-EEG formatting, the benchmark stress-tests models against sensor noise, physiological artifacts, and adversarial perturbations. This establishes reproducible clinical safety evaluation criteria prior to real-world medical deployment.

entry.title: Robust PAC Learning of Concurrent Stochastic Games

author.name: Angel Y. He, David Parker

entry.summary: The authors establish the first PAC learning framework for general-sum concurrent stochastic games under transition uncertainty. The framework maintains confidence sets over transition kernels and introduces a Nash margin characterization that either computes an approximate social-welfare optimal Nash equilibrium or outputs a sound certificate that no equilibrium exists. This provides rigorous formal guarantees for multi-agent reinforcement learning in uncertain dynamic systems.

entry.title: RACE-AIMC: Selective Inference for Heterogeneous Analog In-Memory Accelerators at the Edge

author.name: Osama Yousuf, Martin Lueker-Boden

entry.summary: The authors introduce RACE-AIMC, a certified selective inference framework designed for heterogeneous analog in-memory computing (AIMC) edge accelerators. To handle hardware variability, programming inaccuracies, and cell degradation across physical chips, the framework selectively defers uncertain inferences while bounding overall risk. This enables energy-efficient analog edge inference while providing formal statistical performance guarantees.

entry.title: Generative Nested Sampling of Atomistic Thermodynamic Landscapes

author.name: Alessandro Coretti, Nico Unglert, Sebastian Falkner, Georg K. H. Madsen, Christoph Dellago

entry.summary: This paper investigates the adaptation of continuous normalizing flows to nested sampling in atomistic thermodynamic landscapes. The authors show that discrete permutational symmetries and hard-core atomic collision walls create unique topological barriers absent in astrophysics applications. By incorporating permutation invariance and barrier-aware mappings, their generative nested sampler successfully resolves complex molecular phase equilibria.

entry.title: Introducing SINFONIA: Symplectic, slimplectic and Magnusian (Neural) Flows for Orbital Numerical Integration and Acceleration

author.name: Lidia J. Gomes Da Silva

entry.summary: This work presents SINFONIA, a family of neural flow architectures—incorporating symplectic, slimplectic, and Magnusian invariants—for orbital numerical integration in gravitational wave modeling. By preserving geometric Hamiltonian structures and dissipative dynamics, the neural flows integrate compact binary inspirals over long horizons without accumulating secular phase drift. This provides accelerated waveform generation for astrophysics analysis.

entry.title: ALRA: Adaptive Local Relational Alignment for Logit-Based Pre-training Distillation of Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Quang Hoang Trung, Quang Huu Hieu, Nguyen Van Hoang Phuc, Vo Nguyen Le Duy

entry.summary: The authors introduce ALRA (Adaptive Local Relational Alignment), a logit-based distillation framework for autoregressive language models that focuses distillation losses on dynamically selected token subsets. By combining student proposal tokens with top teacher candidates, ALRA prevents long-tail vocabulary noise from degrading training while maintaining relative probability rankings. This accelerates student pre-training distillation while improving downstream benchmark scores.

entry.title: The Analyst in the Prompt: Role, Retrieval, and Memory Biases in LLM Financial Analysis

author.name: Ahmed Asaad, Amr Mohamed, Yang Zhang, Omneya Abdelsalam

entry.summary: Using thousands of SEC filings across twelve LLMs, this study investigates how persona prompts, user profiles, and persistent memory induce bias in financial document interpretation. The results demonstrate that prompt-assigned personas lead to divergent financial conclusions from identical evidence due to biased interpretive framing rather than skewed retrieval. This exposes critical reliability risks in personalizing LLM agents for high-stakes financial advisory roles.

entry.title: CROCODIL: Cross-Model Code Editing with LLMs

author.name: Linghan Zhong, Aditya Thimmaiah, Jayanth Srinivasa, Milos Gligoric, Junyi Jessy Li

entry.summary: CROCODIL investigates cross-model code editing, analyzing how LLMs behave when modifying foreign code written by different AI assistants with contrasting styles. The authors discover that models systematically over-edit and rewrite stylistic components of foreign code rather than making minimal required modifications. The benchmark highlights an important practical challenge for collaborative software engineering workflows where multiple AI coding agents interact.

entry.title: ProgResViT: Progressive Resolution and Width for Adaptive Vision Transformers

author.name: Ali Hojjat, Janek Haberer, Olaf Landsiedel

entry.summary: ProgResViT introduces an input-adaptive Vision Transformer that performs progressive multi-round inference, dynamically adjusting both spatial resolution and subnetwork width based on classification difficulty. Harder images are escalated to higher-resolution, wider subnetworks while sharing representations across stages via soft gating, substantially reducing average inference latency without sacrificing top-1 accuracy. This provides an effective dynamic compute strategy for vision backbones.

entry.title: P-CORE: Self-Supervised Surface Consistency for Point-Based Neural Editing

author.name: Yanshu Zhang, Shichong Peng, Mehran Aghabozorgi, Alireza Moazeni, Ke Li

entry.summary: P-CORE proposes a self-supervised training strategy to prevent surface tearing, holes, and topological breakdowns when applying large non-rigid deformations to point-based 3D neural representations. By synthesizing random synthetic deformations during training and enforcing multi-view photometric and geometric consistency, the model learns robust deformation dynamics without requiring paired ground-truth deformed scans. The method markedly improves the visual stability of animated neural assets.

entry.title: Preserving Knowledge across Space and Time for Continual Video Deepfake Detection

author.name: Taehoon Kim, Jongwook Choi, Heejae Jo, Byungmin Park, Jongwon Choi

entry.summary: This paper presents Modality-Specific Frequency Distillation to detect video deepfakes continually as new generative models emerge. By isolating spatial, temporal, and joint spatiotemporal artifacts across frequency subbands, the method preserves historical detection capability while adapting to unseen manipulation signatures.

entry.title: Stabilizing Camera-Controlled Novel View Synthesis at Inference Time

author.name: Prajwal Singh, Arjun Badola, Seema Kumari, Hajime Nagahara, Shanmuganathan Raman

entry.summary: This empirical study investigates why training-free novel view synthesis from single images frequently destabilizes over wide camera trajectories. The authors show that decomposing motions into small autoregressive steps below twenty degrees is the predominant factor preventing error accumulation in video diffusion backbones.

entry.title: SPARK: Input-Conditioned Sparse Activation Modulation for Frozen DiT-based Super-Resolution

author.name: Federico Putamorsi, Leonardo Zini, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi

entry.summary: SPARK demonstrates that a small set of dominant channels in Diffusion Transformer backbones strongly dictates image reconstruction quality during super-resolution. By dynamically modulating these sparse activations using input conditions, the framework achieves parameter-efficient adaptation on frozen models.

entry.title: TokenMatch: 3D Mesh Correspondence Transformer with Curvature-Guided Tokenisation

author.name: Adeela Islam, Zorah L\"ahner, Vittorio Murino, Vladislav Golyanik

entry.summary: TokenMatch develops a feed-forward transformer architecture for non-isometric 3D mesh correspondence using curvature-guided surface tokenization. The system accurately matches partial, highly deformed 3D geometries without requiring template priors, iterative functional maps, or high-latency optimization.

entry.title: Toward Unified Robot Learning: Bridging Representation, Vision-Language-Action, and World Models

author.name: Shaunak A. Mehta, Ananya Hazarika, Haochen Zhang, Fan Yang, Ryo Moriyama, Wenkai Li, Yash Patel, Kanata Suzuki

entry.summary: This survey provides a unified conceptual framework organizing modern robot learning along three interconnected pillars: representation learning, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and generative world models. It diagnoses the persistent fragmentation among these subfields, which causes embodied agents to struggle with long-horizon reasoning and unstructured real-world deployment. The paper outlines key integration strategies needed to achieve generalist embodied systems.

entry.title: Frontier AI Shops Should Be Filtering and Generating AI Discourse During Pretraining

author.name: hillz

entry.summary: This proposal argues that frontier AI developers should actively scrub existential risk discourse, sci-fi tropes, and rogue-AI narratives from pretraining corpora while synthetically generating examples of pro-social, collaborative behavior. Grounded in research on persona adoption, the author contends that situational awareness causes models to mirror prevalent fictional archetypes of deceitful or rebellious machines. Filtering these narratives removes harmful priors that post-training safety techniques often fail to suppress.

entry.title: Dude: A Dual-Detection Multi-Agent System for Paper-Code Discrepancy Detection

author.name: Weijie Liu, Running Zhao, Wenhao Yuan, Jinfeng Xu, Zhanfeng Xu, Xiaoxi Zhang, Edith Cheuk-Han Ngai

entry.summary: The paper presents Dude, a dual-detection multi-agent architecture designed to verify consistency between scientific papers and their corresponding code repositories. By implementing a granularity-aligned negotiation protocol, the system resolves discrepancies between high-level paper descriptions and low-level code implementations. This reduces false positives and improves recall in automated scientific reproducibility audits.

entry.title: Govern the Model, Not Only the Data: Storage, Circulation, and Learning in Creative AI

author.name: Phoenix Perry, George Simms, Elizabeth Wilson, Yasmine Boudiaf, Nick Bryan-Kinns, Tega Brain, R. Luke DuBois, Alix Rule, Rachel Meade Smith, Kelani Nichole, Atharva Pravin Pawar, Rebecca Fiebrink

entry.summary: This paper critiques the view that federated learning inherently resolves data exploitation in creative AI, demonstrating that distributed training still leaves model ownership and utility concentrated among conveners. The authors propose an alternative governance framework spanning storage, circulation, and learning, grounded in artist-led data trusts and consent protocols. It emphasizes model governance as essential to protecting creator agency in generative systems.

entry.title: StrixAE: An Intelligent Agent for Audio Enhancement under Complex Distortion Coupling in Real-World Scenarios

author.name: Chenglin Wu, Junjie Wu, Jinhang Chen, Mingyang Chen, Zixu Lin, Jiabian Chen, Xinghao Ding, Xiaotong Tu

entry.summary: StrixAE presents an audio enhancement agent powered by a multimodal LLM controller that dynamically orchestrates specialized speech enhancement and personalization tools. Trained with chain-of-thought fine-tuning and perceptual reinforcement learning, the agent untangles coupled acoustic distortions like reverberation, noise, and clipping in real-world audio. It achieves adaptive, personalized speech enhancement across diverse environmental scenarios.

entry.title: Privacy, Robustness, and Fairness Trade-offs in Federated Intrusion Detection: Geometric Indistinguishability at the Aggregation Interface

author.name: Adrita Rahman Tory, ABM Shawkat Ali, Md Abu Layek, Khondokar Fida Hasan

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the systemic tensions between differential privacy, Byzantine robustness, and minority attack fairness in federated network intrusion detection. The authors formalize the concept of geometric indistinguishability, showing that privacy noise and Byzantine filtering mechanisms inadvertently suppress rare but critical attack categories. This work demonstrates that security, privacy, and fairness cannot be treated as independently composable properties in federated learning.

entry.title: The Psychological Costs of Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Software Engineering

author.name: Adam Alami, Elda Paja, Abhishek Tiwari

entry.summary: This empirical study examines the psychological and organizational costs of adopting generative AI tools within software engineering teams. The authors identify emerging workplace strains, including developer anxiety, identity erosion, deskilling, and disrupted team collaboration norms when automated generation replaces creative problem-solving. It argues that software organizations must address sociotechnical dynamics rather than focusing solely on productivity metrics.

entry.title: Translation as a Decision Space: A Multi-Agent Perspective on Low-Resource Dialect Generation

author.name: Hasan Alkhder, Mohammad Abboush, Igor Tchappi, Ahmet Zengin, Amro Najjar

entry.summary: The authors propose reframing machine translation for low-resource dialects as a multi-agent decision space where different agents explore distinct stylistic and dialectal pathways. By treating translation divergence as an informative signal rather than error, the framework captures cultural nuances and dialectal authenticity better than single-output systems. The approach demonstrates improved stylistic fidelity on low-resource Arabic dialect generation.

entry.title: No-Regret Bayesian Optimization with Finite-Library Input-Warped Kernels

author.name: Edvin Ketabati Augustinsson, Robert A. Bridges

entry.summary: FLIWBO introduces a theoretical framework for Bayesian optimization that guarantees no-regret convergence under input-warped Gaussian process kernels. Unlike conventional GP-UCB proofs that require static covariance structures, this work permits dynamic selection from a finite library of smooth warping functions. This formalizes convergence guarantees for black-box optimization in domains with complex, non-stationary response landscapes.

entry.title: Portable Causal Fairness Across Synthetic Data Generator Families

author.name: Steven Golob, Sikha Pentyala, Martine De Cock

entry.summary: This study tests the portability of causal fairness interventions across nine distinct synthetic data generator families, including GANs, marginal models, and diffusion frameworks under differential privacy. The authors show that fairness guarantees enforced via causal factorizations transfer robustly across diverse architectural families and privacy noise regimes. This demonstrates the viability of provable causal fairness for regulatory synthetic data publishing.

entry.title: From Zero to Hero: An Open LLM Ecosystem for Armenian

author.name: Erik Arakelyan, Khatun Avetisyan, Meri Davtyan, Heghine Grigoryan, Nane Khachatryan, Hayk Shahsuvaryan, Henrik Sergoyan, Vahan Martirosyan

entry.summary: This paper introduces an open language modeling ecosystem for Armenian, releasing the ArmWeb corpus and the ArmSTEM bilingual reasoning dataset. By performing continued pretraining on the existing Gemma-4-E4B base model, the authors release arm-gemma-e4b alongside full training recipes and evaluation splits. This provides a reproducible, high-quality open-weights foundation model for a previously underserved language.

entry.title: Federated Causal Discovery via Regression-Directed Cumulants

author.name: Pablo Torrijos, Fabio Stella, Jos\'e A. G\'amez, Jos\'e M. Puerta

entry.summary: This paper proposes a federated causal discovery algorithm for linear non-Gaussian acyclic models (LiNGAM) by exploiting regression-directed higher-order cumulant tensors. Because cumulant tensors sum additively across independent client partitions, causal orderings can be discovered without centralizing raw data, ensuring compliance with privacy regulations such as GDPR. This extends non-Gaussian causal discovery to privacy-constrained decentralized settings.

entry.title: Unifying Conformal Language Tasks with In-Context Ensembles

author.name: Xiao Shi Huang, Chen-Yuan Lin, Bruce Kuwahara, Kin Kwan Leung, Jesse C. Cresswell

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Conformal Relevance framework, which utilizes in-context learning curation and ensembling to automate score function design in conformal language tasks. By eliminating hand-crafted prompt engineering, it provides distribution-free statistical guarantees on information coverage while maximizing conciseness in document extraction and question answering. Experiments demonstrate consistent coverage calibration across diverse LLM backbones.

entry.title: CRAW: Codec Robust Audio Watermarking

author.name: David Chernin, Ethan Fetaya

entry.summary: This paper presents CRAW (Codec Robust Audio Watermarking), an imperceptible watermarking framework designed to survive neural audio codecs and denoisers. By simulating neural re-synthesis artifacts and compression dynamics during watermark insertion, the scheme maintains high detection accuracy without degrading acoustic quality. This provides a robust provenance defense against the unauthorized redistribution of deepfake and synthetic speech.

entry.title: Efficient Constant Optimization for Symbolic Regression with GPU-Accelerated Tree-Based Genetic Programming

author.name: Hao Mao, Xu Tony Liu, Shuai Lu, Peng Zhao, Wenzheng Jiang, Yuntian Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents a GPU-accelerated Levenberg-Marquardt optimizer for numerical constant tuning in tree-based genetic programming for symbolic regression. By leveraging reverse-mode automatic differentiation over heterogeneous tree populations in batched CUDA kernels, it makes constant optimization cost independent of constant counts. This removes a long-standing computational bottleneck in symbolic regression pipelines.

entry.title: Parameterised graph theory for tensor networks: entanglement rerouting, structural simplification, and agnostic tomography

author.name: Matthias C. Caro, Natalie McHugh, Sergii Strelchuk

entry.summary: This paper applies parameterized graph theory to characterize the complexity of tensor network representations and quantum state learning. The authors show that cutwidth and tree-cutwidth bound the bond dimension overhead required to convert arbitrary tensor networks into matrix product states or tree tensor networks. These structural parameters yield explicit sample and computational complexity bounds for agnostic quantum state tomography.

entry.title: Decoupling Turn-Taking from Semantics: A Decoupled Data Approach for Finite-State-Machine-Based Full-Duplex Dialogue

author.name: Yihang Li, Chenhui Chu

entry.summary: This paper presents a decoupled data framework for full-duplex spoken dialogue that models acoustic turn-taking using real human conversations while managing conversational semantics through agent text dialogues. By integrating this split into a Neural Finite State Machine, the system avoids unnatural turn-taking timing caused by synthetic training data. This enables more fluid, low-latency, and interruption-capable real-time voice agents.

entry.title: Evaluating Criterion-Conditioned Behaviour of Large Language Models in Content Moderation

author.name: Danting Zhang, Bei Peng, Robert Loftin

entry.summary: The authors introduce DECO, a benchmark framework that disaggregates composite safety benchmarks into independent, fine-grained moderation criteria to test whether LLMs can apply specific rules in isolation. Pairwise comparisons across models reveal that high aggregate benchmark scores frequently conceal failures to disentangle distinct content violations. This work demonstrates the need for modular, criterion-specific evaluation in automated content moderation.

entry.title: SLIDEFORGE: An LLM Agent for Controllable Editing of Slides as Structured Artifacts

author.name: Haozhen Zheng, Fulin Wang, Tianhu Xiong, Yingjie Yu, Shengyi Qian, Hanchao Yu, Alex Schwing, Klara Nahrstedt, Mingyuan Wu

entry.summary: SLIDEFORGE is an agentic framework that represents presentation decks via an executable Deck State Graph, linking raw visual components with native PowerPoint object hierarchies. By treating slides as structured, editable code artifacts rather than flat raster images, the agent allows users to perform fine-grained style, layout, and content edits while maintaining visual formatting. The system significantly advances AI-assisted document and presentation design.

entry.title: Beyond Small Patches: Black-Box Detection and Purification of Diverse Backdoor Triggers

author.name: Ahmed Abdelnaby, Mohamed Elmahallawy

entry.summary: TRIM provides a black-box defense against diverse visual backdoor attacks by identifying and purifying manipulated image regions at inference time without requiring access to model weights or clean training distributions. By analyzing prediction sensitivity to regional masks, the framework neutralizes both localized patch triggers and distributed image-wide perturbations. It offers a practical defense for deployed computer vision APIs vulnerable to poisoning.

entry.title: When Depth Hurts: Reliability-Aware Geometry Distillation for Depth-Free RGB-D Salient Object Detection

author.name: Xuehao Wang, Jiaxin Hua, Runmei Li, Zhenyu Wu, Chenglizhao Chen, Ke Gu, Aimin Hao

entry.summary: Recognizing that noisy sensor depth can degrade RGB-D salient object detection, this paper introduces a reliability-aware geometry distillation method that utilizes Depth Anything V2 solely as a training-time teacher. The framework transfers spatial attention, relative geometry, and boundary cues into an RGB-only model, eliminating runtime dependence on defective physical depth sensors. The resulting system outperforms conventional RGB-D detectors while running purely on standard monocular images.

entry.title: Neural-Collapse-guided Task-Free Continual Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xiaotong Kong, Chaoyang Song, Ziai Zhou, Jinxia Zhang, Kanjian Zhang, Haikun Wei

entry.summary: NC-TFAD tackles industrial visual anomaly detection across non-stationary streaming data without predefined task boundaries by projecting feature representations onto an Equiangular Tight Frame simplex guided by Neural Collapse theory. This fixed geometric scaffold prevents catastrophic forgetting and stabilizes normal visual prototypes as manufacturing environments drift. The paper demonstrates reliable continual anomaly detection under realistic, unbounded factory shifts.

entry.title: When Do Frozen VLMs Respond to Image-Free Object-Token Edits? An Answer-Key-Free Protocol and What It Reveals

author.name: Wonbin Son, Gyumun Choi, Junil Seo, Seungmin Rho, Mi Young Lee, Hyungjoon Kim

entry.summary: This work analyzes whether frozen vision-language models can reliably respond to hypothetical scene interventions performed directly on object tokens rather than re-rendering input pixels. It establishes an annotation-free auditing protocol to demonstrate that token edits require explicit instruction rather than standard visual question answering pretraining to succeed.

entry.title: Rethinking 3D Noise: Learning 3D-Aware Video Priors via Optimization-Free Morphological Perturbations

author.name: Onat \c{S}ahin, Mohammad Altillawi, George Eskandar, Carlos Carbone, Ziyuan Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents 3D Morphological Perturbations, an optimization-free data augmentation technique that perturbs explicit 3D Gaussian primitives directly. Treating Gaussians like 3D pixels allows models to learn 3D-aware video priors under sparse-view conditions without requiring expensive per-scene neural reconstructions.

entry.title: BooM-VVT: Boosting Mask-Free Video Virtual Try-On with Image-Level Pseudo Data

author.name: Wei Zhang, Xin Li, Peishu Shi, Jialin Gao, Xuekang Peng, Zhichao Lian, Yeying Jin

entry.summary: BooM-VVT presents a mask-free video virtual try-on framework trained on image-level synthetic pseudo-data paired with sparse keyframe propagation. By avoiding reliance on explicit garment boundary masks, the method eliminates boundary distortion artifacts during complex body movements and severe occlusions.

entry.title: Cat-Belling Problems

author.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky

entry.summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky analyzes cat-belling problems in AI alignment—proposals that appear clever but fundamentally depend on solving an equally difficult, unverified prerequisite. He warns against schemes that assume an advanced system can safely be delegated the task of superalignment, comparing them to flawed engineering concepts that violate core physical constraints. The essay argues that scalable safety requires confronting irreducible verification and control barriers directly.

entry.title: AutoGraphForge: Towards Automated Graph Theory Discovery

author.name: J\'an Pastorek

entry.summary: The paper presents AutoGraphForge, an automated conjecturing, refuting, and proving pipeline for graph theory. Using counterexample-guided candidate generation alongside linear-programming novelty filters, the system tests mathematical conjectures against a library of over 340,000 graphs. It demonstrates progress toward autonomous mathematical discovery systems operating over combinatorial structures.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for Energy Optimization in Data Centers

author.name: Mohammed Basharath Ullah, Summaiya Unnisa Begum, Mohammed Nadeem Ullah

entry.summary: This review paper analyzes 63 studies on AI-driven data center energy optimization, exposing widespread methodological flaws such as exclusive reliance on simulation and omission of water withdrawal and embodied carbon. The authors show that reported savings across distinct technique families overlap almost entirely, indicating that real-world efficiency gains remain unproven. It advocates for rigorous physical hardware validation in sustainable computing research.

entry.title: Adapting to Evolving Requirements: Agentic AI for Retail Supply Chain Operations

author.name: Lei Zheng, Liping Yang, Zihao Li, Guodong Lyu, Chaik Ming Koh, Chung-Piaw Teo

entry.summary: This work introduces a graph-constrained agentic framework to automate requirement-driven adaptations in retail supply chain pipelines. Specialized domain agents propose admissible module reformulations while a central planner evaluates downstream impacts across coupled operational stages. The approach enables flexible, automated adjustments to shifting logistical and inventory constraints.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Multi-LLM Federated Inference for Cognitive Diagnosis

author.name: Yagna Manasa Boyapati, Chong Yu, Tianyu Jiang, Justin Zhan

entry.summary: The authors propose a privacy-preserving federated inference architecture that allows heterogeneous commercial LLMs (such as LLaMA-3.3-70B, GPT-4o-mini, and Claude-3-Haiku) to collaborate on cognitive diagnostic tasks. By injecting epsilon-local differential privacy noise into local outputs and using residual-based aggregation, the framework avoids exposing proprietary weights or student records. It demonstrates that federated diagnostic accuracy can be maintained under formal privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Spectral Convergence of Random Feature Method in Multiple Dimensions

author.name: Pingbing Ming, Hao Yu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves the spectral convergence of random feature methods for multidimensional targets across Sobolev, Gevrey, and ultra-analytic function spaces. The authors prove that a single sampled random feature space can simultaneously achieve spectral approximation rates across multiple interpolation error norms. The work expands the mathematical understanding of kernel approximation and random feature scaling in high dimensions.

entry.title: The Civilization Framework: Sovereign-Anchored Communication Between Personal Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Guangjun Liu

entry.summary: The Civilization Framework proposes a sovereign-anchored communication architecture for personal multi-agent systems using persistent ledgers and the Embassy Protocol. By anchoring system authority in persistent ledgers rather than transient agent instances, it ensures that an agent's authority is bound strictly to verifiable memory credentials. This protocol prevents contextual information loss and authority escalation during cross-system agent communications.

entry.title: How Far Can Synthetic Data Take Thai OCR?

author.name: Kunat Pipatanakul

entry.summary: This study analyzes the factors that enable synthetic training data to transfer effectively to real-world Thai optical character recognition (OCR). The author demonstrates that typographical diversity, structural layouts, and human handwriting glyphs are critical for transfer, while non-text background realism has minimal effect. These insights lead to Wayu-Paxa-OCR-Zero, a robust Thai OCR model trained entirely without real-world manual labels.

entry.title: Enhancing Financial Question Answering: A Novel Benchmark Dataset of Banks' financial statements

author.name: Arianna Miola, Bruno Spaccavento, Lorenzo Silotto, Marco Bianchetti, Luca Cagliero

entry.summary: FinRAG-QA is a financial question-answering benchmark comprising 999 practitioner-curated questions grounded in over 200 annual and regulatory reports from 24 major US and European banks. The dataset targets complex cross-institutional comparisons and dense numerical reasoning over documents averaging 198,000 words. It establishes a rigorous evaluation standard for retrieval-augmented generation systems operating in the banking sector.

entry.title: RARF: Region-Aware Rectified Flows for 3D Brain MRI Inpainting

author.name: Tomas Guija-Valiente, Blanca Rodriguez-Gonzalez, Norberto Malpica, Angel Torrado-Carvajal

entry.summary: RARF introduces a region-aware rectified flow framework for 3D brain MRI inpainting and tissue reconstruction in neuroimaging. By restricting the flow interpolation strictly to the pathological void while conditioning on patient-specific context, it achieves anatomically coherent generative tissue completion. The method demonstrates strong inpainting performance on benchmark brain lesion challenges.

entry.title: Mesh-Native Physics-Informed Graph Surrogates for TCAD-in-the-Loop Design Space Exploration

author.name: Leonid Popryho, Ayoub Sadeghi, Inna Partin-Vaisband

entry.summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed graph attention network surrogate that operates directly on 3D tetrahedral TCAD meshes for FinFET semiconductor design. By predicting nodal electrostatic potentials and quasi-Fermi levels, the model adheres to governing drift-diffusion physics while bypassing slow numerical differential equation solvers. This accelerates multi-objective device exploration in chip design by orders of magnitude.

entry.title: Learning from Scarce Labels: Multi-View Echocardiography for Ejection Fraction Prediction

author.name: Zhiyuan Gao, Dominic Yurk, Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa

entry.summary: This work introduces a semi-supervised pipeline to predict left ventricular ejection fraction from parasternal long-axis (PLAX) echocardiography views, overcoming clinical data scarcity. By matching unstructured clinical notes with video timestamps and using automated proxy labeling, the authors assemble a dataset of 25,000 videos. The resulting model achieves diagnostic error rates competitive with standard apical four-chamber clinical benchmarks.

entry.title: VoxReason: Listener-Free Evaluation of Source-Grounded Speech Planning Before Synthesis

author.name: Mengzhe Geng

entry.summary: This paper presents VoxReason, a listener-free evaluation framework that audits whether speech planning choices (such as prosody, affect, and pauses) are properly grounded in source text before synthesis. The system forces models to generate explicit speaking plans with source citations, allowing deterministic verification of delivery intent. This prevents conversational and expressive TTS models from hallucinating inappropriate emotional or narrative stances.

entry.title: Bounded Personas Match Retrieval on Classification but Not Regression for a Frozen Agent

author.name: JaeHa Yoon, Minjun Park, Seoyeon Kim, Jiwoo Lee, Hyunwoo Choi, Dohyun Kang

entry.summary: This paper introduces PersonaLink to distill user interaction histories into compact, bounded natural-language personas for frozen language agents. Evaluating the approach against full retrieval-augmented history, the authors find that compact personas match retrieval accuracy on discrete classification tasks but fall behind on continuous regression and ranking. This establishes concrete boundaries for when lightweight persona distillation can replace expensive retrieval context.

entry.title: RL-ADA: A World-Feedback Framework for Adversarially Robust Enterprise Dialogue Agents

author.name: Ram Narayanan, Harshit Rajgarhia, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: RL-ADA proposes an adversarial co-evolutionary framework pairing a 3B support agent with a 7B adversarial customer agent trained via reinforcement learning on outcome-based world feedback. This replaces manual dialogue annotation by aligning conversational policies directly with task success and operational consequences. It offers enterprise conversational agents greater resilience against evasive or difficult customer interactions.

entry.title: How Perturbations Propagate: A Multi-Level Analysis of Robustness in Large Language Models

author.name: Dun Li Chan, Emily Liu, Niyathi Allu, Christian Hoang

entry.summary: This research analyzes how naturalistic and synthetic input noise propagates through LLMs across three distinct tiers: final token predictions, internal representation geometry, and individual attention heads. The authors demonstrate that internal geometric distortion reveals model vulnerability long before degradation appears in observable textual outputs. This multi-level lens provides deeper mechanistic diagnostics for assessing neural network robustness.

entry.title: A Reverse Sign Language Dictionary: Open-Vocabulary Sign Recognition from Continuous Signing via Video Captioning and Description Retrieval

author.name: Santiago Poveda-Guti\'errez, Hideki Nakayama, Mayumi Bono

entry.summary: The authors develop a reverse sign language dictionary that avoids closed-set gloss classification by generating procedural linguistic descriptions of sign gestures using an open-weight VLM and matching them via text retrieval. Evaluated on Japanese Sign Language dialogue, this open-vocabulary framework decouples recognition from rigid gloss inventories. It offers an adaptable pathway for translating unstandardized or continuous sign language into text.

entry.title: Exemplar: Classical Priors Complement Frozen Features for Few-Shot Microscopy Segmentation at Native Resolution

author.name: Michal Pr\r{u}\v{s}ek, Adam Novoz\'amsk\'y, Filip \v{S}roubek

entry.summary: Exemplar demonstrates that fusing frozen self-supervised foundation features with classical image processing filters allows for native-resolution, few-shot segmentation across diverse biomedical microscopy datasets. Bypassing heavy fine-tuning, the lightweight fusion head fits masks from minimal examples while avoiding resolution downsampling artifacts. The approach provides an efficient solution for clinical microscopy annotation where labeled data is scarce.

entry.title: SafeRestore: Detector-Relative Risk Certificates for Selective Industrial Image Restoration

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: SafeRestore introduces detector-relative risk certificates for industrial image restoration pipelines prior to automated defect inspection. It calculates exact finite-sample binomial bounds to ensure that restoration filters neither erase subtle defect cues nor trigger excessive false alarms.

entry.title: Tree-Structured Vector Quantization For Efficient And Progressive Image Compression

author.name: Xinkun Wang, Tianyi Xu, Qingyu Luo, Mingming Ma, Changzhe Jiao, Fu Li, Yi Niu

entry.summary: Tree-VQ proposes a progressive learned image compression architecture that structures discrete codebook vectors within hierarchical binary trees. Every prefix along a latent token tree path forms a decodable representation, allowing continuous rate adaptation and progressive streaming without multiple models.

entry.title: Observation-Conditioned Latent Energy Priors for Sparse Implicit Neural Shape Completion

author.name: Paul B\"uschl, Ezequiel de la Rosa, Julia Wolleb, Julian McGinnis, C\'esar Nombela-Arrieta, Bjoern Menze

entry.summary: The paper proposes observation-conditioned latent energy priors to prevent test-time geometric drift in implicit neural shape completion models. When optimizing continuous representations from sparse off-grid point clouds, the residual energy prior penalizes shapes that fit sparse points but deviate from plausible categorical geometry.

entry.title: Efficient Semantic Understanding from Digital Foveation

author.name: Caterina Caccavella, Vittorio Fra, Andreas Ziegler, Giulia D'Angelo, Yulia Sandamirskaya

entry.summary: Inspired by biological active vision, this paper introduces a digital foveation framework that concentrates high-resolution computation exclusively on salient image fixations. Combined with low-resolution contextual pooling, the approach achieves nearly 96% of dense segmentation accuracy while dramatically cutting computational operations.

entry.title: Robot Aware Computational Design of Object Specific Passive Grippers for Additive Manufacturing

author.name: Abdullah Yahya Abdullah Omaisan, Ibrahim Sheikh Mohamed

entry.summary: This work introduces an automated computational pipeline that synthesizes custom, unactuated passive grippers tailored to specific target objects and robot manipulator kinematics. By integrating 3D surface contact analysis, inverse kinematics, and topology optimization, it generates 3D-printable end-effectors requiring zero motor actuators.

entry.title: MulDP: Multimodal Diffusion Policy for Autonomous Quadruped Parkour Navigation across Complex Terrains

author.name: Kangmai Hu, Yueqi Zhang, Peng Zhai, Xiaoyi Wei, Jiabin Hu, Zhixiang Liu, Quancheng Qian, Lihua Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MulDP, a multimodal diffusion policy enabling autonomous parkour navigation for quadrupedal robots traversing complex obstacles without human operator steering. The policy fuses visual observations, proprioception, and goal conditions to synthesize smooth, anticipatory velocity commands that tightly link perception with low-level execution. This eliminates the traditional reliance on human teleoperation for high-level agile quadruped maneuvers.

entry.title: MasterControl Seventeen Every Time

author.name: MasterControl AI Lab

entry.summary: The paper investigates a governed enterprise analytics framework where language models are restricted to interpreting user intent, leaving data operations to deterministic, pre-approved execution policies. Experiments across 440 runs show that runtime planning by open 8B models fails enterprise evidence and consistency contracts, whereas deterministic policy execution guarantees replayable results. It provides a grounded argument against unconstrained runtime agent execution in enterprise settings.

entry.title: TabScope: Question-Adaptive Scope Selection for Table Question Answering

author.name: Yuxiang Wang, Junhao Gan, Jianzhong Qi

entry.summary: TabScope introduces an adaptive scope-selection mechanism for table question answering that dynamically toggles between localized sub-table reasoning and full-table context. By identifying whether a user query requires localized cell lookup or broad table synthesis, it decomposes oversized tables to prevent context degradation in language models. This dual-mode approach improves answer accuracy on large, heterogeneous tabular datasets.

entry.title: Building and Evaluating Fixed-Voice Thai TTS from Synthetic Speech

author.name: Kunat Pipatanakul, Potsawee Manakul, Warit Sirichotedumrong, Sittipong Sripaisarnmongkol, Pakorn Nathong, Phatrasek Jirabovonvisut

entry.summary: This work explores distilling compact fixed-voice text-to-speech models for low-resource Thai using entirely synthetic speech generated by a large voice-cloning teacher. The authors analyze pipeline filtering strategies to handle Thai-specific challenges, including ambiguous word boundaries, tonal contours, and English code-switching. The study provides practical guidelines for training lightweight on-device speech models from short reference recordings without human audio datasets.

entry.title: Seeing Before Synthesizing: VLM-Guided Transition Event Discovery for Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning

author.name: Ye-Chan Kim, Seunghee Choi, SeungJu Cha, Si-Woo Kim, Hwiseon Kim, Hyungee Kim, Dong-Jin Kim

entry.summary: Seeing Before Synthesizing (SBS) is a weakly-supervised dense video captioning framework that discovers transition events using vision-language model guidance. Instead of blindly filling inter-event gaps with hallucinated text, SBS detects visual transitions from semantic variations in frame-level narratives before generating aligned captions. This improves temporal localization and visual-linguistic grounding in uncurated long-form video understanding.

entry.title: TRACE: Spatiotemporal Contact Memory Graph Network Simulator for Granular Dynamics

author.name: Changjian Zhou, Negin Yousefpour, Jie Qi, Junfeng Fang, Guillermo A. Narsilio, Hans Petter Jostad

entry.summary: TRACE is a learned graph-network simulator for granular dynamics that maintains temporal interaction history directly along dynamically changing contact edges. By coupling persistent edge memory with an attention-based recurrent graph update, it avoids information loss when particle contacts break and reform. This allows accurate simulation of complex granular phenomena, including force chains and shear band formations.

entry.title: Resolution-Aware Experimental Design under Partial Identifiability

author.name: Sofianos Panagiotis Fotias

entry.summary: This theoretical paper introduces Resolution-Aware Experimental Design (RAED) to address experimental selection under partial identifiability where nuisance parameters obscure structural meaning. The author proves that standard information-gain objectives can select experiments with arbitrarily poor structural resolution, and formulates an alternative criterion controlling false exclusion. This provides sound statistical guarantees for active scientific discovery.

entry.title: OSR: Output Space Redistribution for Adaptive Label Removal in Classification Models

author.name: Minyi Peng, Darian Gunamardi, Ivan Tjuawinata, Yongsen Zheng, Kwok-Yan Lam
