entry.title: The Approximation Rank of Softmax Attention: Sharp Geometric Laws and Robust Interaction Dimension

author.name: Yuhe Sui, Jianing Zhang

entry.summary: A theoretical study deriving worst-case rank complexity laws for softmax attention approximation, showing rank scales with support geometry (spherical vs ball) and an r/2 interaction-dimension law for fixed heads. This provides sharp mathematical grounding for when attention matrices are intrinsically low-rank, relevant to efficient attention design.

entry.title: Real-time virtual circuits for plasma shape control via neural network emulators: experimental demonstration on MAST Upgrade

author.name: Nicola C. Amorisco, Kamran Pentland, Adriano Agnello, George K. Holt, Alasdair Ross, Matthew J. Marshall, Edward Jones, Graham J. McArdle, Charles Vincent, Timothy Nunn, Martin Kochan, Pedro Cavestany, Aran Garrod, Stanislas Pamela, James Buchanan

entry.summary: Reports the first experimental deployment of real-time virtual circuits for tokamak plasma shape control on MAST Upgrade, replacing offline lookup tables with neural-network-emulator-updated VCs while retaining the existing control architecture and interpretability.

entry.title: From the Loss Landscape to Diverse Feature Learning in Neural Networks

author.name: David Aram Yunis

entry.summary: Revisits the provable-auditable privacy gap of DP-SGD, synthesizing the tension between theoretical upper bounds and empirical auditing lower bounds and charting where the pessimistic auditing outlook may or may not hold. Strong author group in privacy (Kamath, Tian).

entry.title: Locked at the Entrance, Open Inside: Where RLVR Narrows the Solution Space

author.name: Qiancheng Zhou, Ruizhe Li

entry.summary: Disentangles access from execution in RLVR-induced solution-space narrowing using the exhaustively enumerable Countdown task, finding solution coverage falls up to 67% and that loss occurs at entrance families (the policy cannot initiate valid solution modes) rather than mid-computation. Sheds light on why RLVR hurts pass@k.

entry.title: Where Induction Runs Out: Description-Length Difficulty and the Memorisation Gap in Integer-Sequence Benchmarks

author.name: Sabilashan Ganeshan

entry.summary: Uses an exactly computable MDL learner over P-recursive recurrences to analyze what OEIS-based integer-sequence benchmarks measure about language model mathematical reasoning. Shows benchmark difficulty is predicted by parameter count and reveals a memorisation gap between induction and inference.

entry.title: Preference Elicitation for Policy Optimization and Application to Aligning Heart Transplantation with Human Values

author.name: Itai Zilberstein, Ioannis Anagnostides, Zachary W Sollie, Arman Kilic, Tuomas Sandholm

entry.summary: The authors design a preference-elicitation algorithm for linear utilities that learns attribute weights via cutting planes from pairwise outcome comparisons, then applies it to optimize organ allocation policy for heart transplantation. Shifting elicitation from decision-level to outcome-level preferences avoids conflating means with ends.

entry.title: Adversarial Calibration Attack on Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Liangkai Liu, Qingzhao Zhang, Kang G. Shin

entry.summary: The authors identify online camera-LiDAR calibration as a novel attack surface for autonomous vehicles and present Adversarial Calibration Attack (ACA), the first physical attack targeting calibration updates. Corrupted calibration persists across fusion operations, propagating errors from perception to planning and control.

entry.title: The Illusion of Replacement: Rethinking Specialized Machine Learning Models in the Foundation Model Era

author.name: Kiyan Rezaee

entry.summary: A review of 159 papers from 2016-2026 examining whether language-based foundation models can replace specialized ML architectures for structured data across nine modalities. It introduces eight representational regimes and finds language-mediated models competitive only in specific settings like few-shot prediction and symbolic tasks, arguing that preserving structural computation matters beyond task accuracy.

entry.title: AdaVLA: Adaptive Step Flow Matching for Training-free Acceleration of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Sunghwan Han, Youngtae Han, Youngmin Yi

entry.summary: Proposes AdaVLA, a training-free acceleration method for flow-matching vision-language-action models that adaptively reduces the cost of the iterative ODE solver rather than the VLM backbone, targeting on-device robotics deployment where fine-tuning or training data access is unavailable.

entry.title: Content Exploration Beyond the Feed: Creator Supply and the Shared Corpus

author.name: Yuanyuan Shen, Yiren Yan, Wenjie Li, Chunhui Zhu

entry.summary: Analyzes four experiments on a major short-video platform showing that production-side exploration budgets raise creator output (8.55% more videos posted, 7.10% more active creators) while viewer-side ablations trade off views (up 1.74%) against other engagement, filling a gap where published budget objectives omit creator response.

entry.title: Benchmark Contamination: A Taxonomy Organized by Defeated Mitigation

author.name: Johanna Angulo, V\'ictor Yeste, Hector Espinos-Morato

entry.summary: Proposes a taxonomy of benchmark contamination organized by which mitigation each contamination type defeats - direct, derivative, temporal, distributional, and acquired - arguing that leaderboards make capability and leakage observationally equivalent and that a private held-out test set alone closes only the first threat.

entry.title: $\mathcal{N}_0$-Foundation: Towards the Age of Tactile Intelligence

author.name: NeoteAI Team, Fudan TEAI Team

entry.summary: Presents N0-Foundation, an end-to-end paradigm for tactile-enabled embodied manipulation including a vision-based tactile sensor, tactile UMI infrastructure, and NeoData - over 30,000 hours of synchronized visuo-tactile demonstrations across six embodiments and 450 tasks - plus tactile representation learning and standardized evaluation.

entry.title: CoVA-SFT: A Large-Scale Dataset for Chain of Visual Abstractions

author.name: Tsung-Han Wu, Heekyung Lee, Anya Ji, Haoming Chen, Trevor Darrell, Joseph E. Gonzalez, David M. Chan

entry.summary: Presents CoVA-SFT, a 51.9K-sample structured corpus with over 222K multimodal reasoning steps teaching models to maintain internal visual workspaces during textual reasoning, plus the companion CoVA-Bench. Extends chain-of-thought training beyond text-only serialization of visual problems.

entry.title: Pad\=artha: Ontology-Grounded Fine-Grained NER Benchmark for Classical Sanskrit

author.name: Sujoy Sarkar, Pretam Ray, Paramhans Shah, Manoj Balaji Jagadeeshan, Akash Gairola, Arjuna S R, Pawan Goyal

entry.summary: Introduces Terminal-Bench-LILT, 300 native-speaker-authored agentic coding tasks in ten languages targeting non-English-specific issues like internationalization, encoding, and cultural conventions. Best of six frontier models reaches only 63.1% pass rate, with many tasks unsolved by any model.

entry.title: The Emergent Symbolic Structure of Artificial Neural Networks

author.name: R. Thomas McCoy, Paul Soulos, Tal Linzen, Paul Smolensky

entry.summary: Argues that neural networks implicitly realize symbolic structure, showing that Tensor Product Representations can explain how continuous-vector systems capture compositional structure, connecting interpretation methods and cognitive-science-style symbolic hypotheses.

entry.title: You Know What I Mean: A Benchmark for Agentic Conversational Reference Grounding

author.name: Karen Fuchs, Uri Katz, Yoav Goldberg

entry.summary: A2Agent trains repository-level code localization agents with action-aware reinforcement learning that rewards both discovery and commitment of gold code regions per turn, plus an action-level advantage estimation grouping turns with shared exploration context. It improves average F1 over state-of-the-art by addressing sparse trajectory-level credit assignment.

entry.title: SwarmBench: Can Large Language Models Act as Agent Swarm Orchestrators?

author.name: Jinshan Gao, Zhuoran Jin, Tianyi Men, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: SwarmBench benchmarks whether LLMs can act as orchestrators of dynamically reconfiguring agent swarms, evaluating accuracy, efficiency, cost, and process quality. Results show large gaps between models in orchestration capability beyond final task accuracy.

entry.title: Will the User Ever Know? Covert Indirect Prompt Injection on Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Yunseok Lee, Yunji Kim, Woojin Lee

entry.summary: Decomposes indirect prompt injection Attack Success Rate into covert (no trace in the agent's final response) and overt (user-visible) success rates, better reflecting user risk from tool-using agents. This reframing matters because covert injections are far more dangerous in practice. Directly relevant to AI security measurement.

entry.title: TAKE 85: Testing Audiovisual filmmaKer's intEnt across 85 Hours of Film

author.name: Kaishuu Shinozaki-Conefrey, Olivier Pascaud, Robin Courant, Xi Wang, Dimitris Samaras, Vicky Kalogeiton

entry.summary: TAKE 85 is the first benchmark for directorial-intent understanding in film, with 398 films (85 hours) and expert-verified QA pairs spanning visual and audio intent, plus controlled modality ablations. Reveals a large gap between what current MLLMs perceive and why creative choices are made.

entry.title: From Intent to Evidence: Policy-Steered Multi-Strategy Retrieval for Long-Video Agents

author.name: Can Zhang, Baofeng Zhang, Xiaotian Han, Junyuan Shang, Yuchen Ding, Shuohuan Wang, Dianhai Yu, Ruirui Li

entry.summary: VESTA is a training-free long-video agent that routes each question to a focused, recall, or contrastive evidence-acquisition policy over a shared visual-speech index within an acquire-verify-consolidate loop. It addresses the limitation that existing video agents use one uniform retrieval behavior regardless of question type.

entry.title: SMG: Semantic Motion Graph for Monocular Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Haozheng Yu, Xinyu Yang, Rundong Luo, Jennifer J. Sun, Bharath Hariharan

entry.summary: SMG models dynamic Gaussian Splatting motion as low-rank semantic motion, exploiting the prior that spatially close and semantically related regions share consistent dynamics to regularize under-constrained regions in monocular video. It reduces overfitting to training views and improves handling of occlusion and complex motion.

entry.title: STEP: A Modular Silent Trial Engine for Operational Evaluation of Digital Pathology AI in Routine Workflow

author.name: Gabriele Campanella, Matthew Croken, Olga Lukatskaya, Jane Houldsworth, Ricky Kwan, Peter Sch\"uffler, Chad Vanderbilt

entry.summary: STEP is a reusable software platform from Memorial Sloan Kettering for orchestrating prospective silent trials of computational pathology AI across heterogeneous laboratory information systems and digital pathology infrastructure. Silent trials bridge retrospective validation and clinical deployment without influencing patient care.

entry.title: DREAM: Deployment-Time Demonstration Generation via Real-to-Sim for Scalable Policy Adaptation

author.name: Makoto Sato, Tatsuya Matsushima, Yutaka Matsuo, Yusuke Iwasawa

entry.summary: DREAM generates fine-tuning demonstrations for pretrained VLA models at deployment time without human teleoperation: it reconstructs the captured workspace, uses an LLM to translate instructions into symbolic goals, and applies task-and-motion planning to synthesize action-labeled data. This addresses the costly per-workspace demonstration bottleneck.

entry.title: DriftingVLA: Native One-Step Vision-Language-Action Generation via Per-Dimension Temporal Drifting

author.name: Yuxuan Gao, Shiqi Zhang, Yedong Shen, Yifan Duan, Wenhao Yu, Xin Zhang, Siyuan Cao, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: DriftingVLA achieves native one-step generation of complete action chunks via a distribution-drifting objective, replacing iterative flow integration that inflates latency in flow-based VLA models. Per-Dimension Temporal Drifting accounts for distinct control semantics across action dimensions, enabling real-time robot control with a single action-expert forward pass.

entry.title: Sampling-based Certified Planning with Graphs of Convex Sets

author.name: Peng Xie, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: Reports the first quantification of the gap between probabilistic collision-free guarantees of convex region generators and planner correctness in graphs-of-convex-sets planning: on a 14-DOF bimanual library, 3.2 percent of interface samples were in collision, causing a 62 percent answer error with trajectories driving arms through shelves reported as successes. Repair strategies such as stricter contracts and sums-of-squares certified regions are evaluated.

entry.title: Probing Perceptual Priors of MLLMs via Gibbs Sampling with Interpretable Generative Controls

author.name: Manuel Cherep, Pattie Maes, Nikhil Singh

entry.summary: Proposes probing what multimodal LLMs implicitly expect in their inputs by using Gibbs sampling with interpretable generative controls to reconstruct the prior distribution over stimuli, rather than holding inputs fixed as mechanistic or behavioral probes do. This reframes a slice of interpretability as recovering the models expected input distribution. A genuinely novel methodological angle from an experienced MIT group.

entry.title: Agents in the Large: Perception-Centered Architecture for Persistent Agents

author.name: Shihan Dou, Haoxiang Jia, Shichun Liu, Feng Chen, Chenhao Huang, Yujiong Shen, Shaofan Liu, Jiayi Chen, Jiahang Lin, Honglin Guo, Qianyu He, Minghao Guo, Ziyi Ye, Pluto Zhou, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: Proposes a Perception-Centered Architecture for Persistent Agents (PCAP), a framework for language agents that provide long-lived, open-ended assistance rather than solving bounded tasks. It characterizes persistent agents, organizes existing work, and sketches architectural principles centered on perception.

entry.title: Low-Resource Preference Adaptation of LLMs via Activation-Based Label Propagation

author.name: Alessio Galatolo, Meriem Beloucif

entry.summary: Investigates how LLMs encode preference information in intermediate activations, finding chosen and rejected responses form distinct clusters that alignment strengthens for canonical preferences but erases for different target preferences. Exploits this for low-resource preference adaptation via activation-based label propagation.

entry.title: HSRM: Hidden-State Reward Models for Test-Time Verification

author.name: Xianzhi Li, Xiaodan Zhu

entry.summary: HSRM is a lightweight hidden-state reward model that verifies candidate mathematical reasoning solutions by reading the generator's internal representations directly, avoiding expensive text-based re-verification at test time. Builds on prior evidence that LLMs internally encode correctness signals. Potentially significant for efficient test-time compute.

entry.title: Think, Look, and Revise: Inconsistency-Aware Visual Self-Correction in MLLMs

author.name: Yu Cheng, Arushi Goel, Hakan Bilen

entry.summary: ReVISE equips multimodal LLMs with verification and dynamic error recovery for tool-augmented reasoning, using curated data supervising reflective behavior and a reinforcement learning stage. Models learn to validate tool-derived evidence, reformulate queries on mismatch, and fall back to intrinsic grounding when tools are unreliable. Directly addresses the unverified-tool-output gap in agentic MLLMs.

entry.title: Rating the Raters: Rasch Measurement Theory for LLM Evaluation

author.name: Pratik S. Sachdeva, Nathan Boudol

entry.summary: Applies Rasch measurement theory from psychometrics to LLM evaluation, treating benchmarks, LLM judges, and human raters as separable facets of a common measurement problem, with diagnostics that expose miscalibrated items and rater bias. A case study shows how the decomposition clarifies what evaluation scores actually measure. Offers a principled statistical upgrade over naive aggregate metrics for both benchmark scoring and judge-based assessment.

entry.title: Quantization-Triggered Backdoors in Language Models: Cross-Quantizer Transferability and the Validation--Deployment Gap

author.name: Jacopo Dardini, Claudio Stanzione, Giordano Col\`o, Giuseppe Fenza

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a validation-deployment gap in LLM quantization: because quantization is a many-to-one mapping, full-precision certification does not guarantee behavioral equivalence in the deployed model. It introduces Quantization Behavioral Equivalence Classes, proves membership does not imply equivalence, and demonstrates a three-stage adversarial pipeline for quantization-triggered backdoors. A significant security blind spot for edge deployment workflows.

entry.title: ContextLeak: Exfiltrating LLM Agent Context via Malicious Tools

author.name: Yuqi Jia, Ruiqi Wang, Patrick Li, Yuepeng Hu, Peinian Li, Neil Gong

entry.summary: ContextLeak is a malicious-tool attack on LLM agents that induces the agent to pass its runtime context, including user prompts, trajectories, and tool lists, as tool arguments exfiltrated to attacker endpoints, targeting the previously unexplored second condition of the exfiltration chain. It completes the picture of context-theft attack requirements beyond tool selection and transmission. Significant security implications as agent tool ecosystems grow.

entry.title: Blog: Survey of Optimizers

author.name: Ruoran Xu

entry.summary: A survey organizing 2025-2026 neural network optimizers along four axes: temporal estimation, update geometry, horizon management, and representation/systems, connecting Muon, Shampoo, SOAP, schedule-free training, and memory-efficient methods. Captures the post-Adam-variant design space.

entry.title: On the Recoverability of Private Information Unlearning in Large Language Models

author.name: Shicheng Hu, Runzhi Tian, Ziqiao Wang, Yongyi Mao

entry.summary: Builds a white-box auditing framework with synthetic private data to test whether LLM unlearning methods truly erase rather than hide memorized information, finding a simple inverse-greedy decoding can recover claimed-forgotten content across five evaluated methods.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Detection of Rare Disease-Associated Cell Subsets via Secure Multi-Party Computation

author.name: \c{S}. Selcan Magara, Esther Havemann, Debora Jutz, Ali Burak \"Unal, Mete Akg\"un

entry.summary: This paper builds a secure multi-party computation (MPC) framework enabling institutions to jointly train and run CellCnn models for detecting rare disease-associated cell subsets in single-cell data without sharing sensitive patient records. It could unlock multi-institutional cohorts for rare-subset discovery under privacy regulations.

entry.title: The Hallucination Signal Is a Mean Shift: Why Simple Probes Suffice

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Jaehyung Seo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: The authors show the hallucination-detection signal in LLM hidden states is overwhelmingly a single mean-shift component, and removing that direction collapses detection to chance. Simple L2-regularized logistic regression bounds or beats twelve more complex probe architectures, explaining apparent probe sophistication as covariance-estimation difficulty.

entry.title: Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventions

author.name: Haijie Xu, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: Studies causal representation learning in a fragmented multi-client setting where each client intervenes on only a subset of shared latent variables, showing that marginalization induces bidirected edges that break standard node-wise assumptions. The method recovers the global latent causal order by assembling client-specific structural fragments.

entry.title: Hyper-Fold: Exploring the Expressive Limit of Sequence-Geometry Learning for Proteins via Hypergraph Modeling

author.name: Yifan Feng, Guanjie Cheng, Shihui Ying, Shaoyi Du, Yue Gao

entry.summary: Shows that the complete bilinear operator over content-geometry outer products is the expressive ceiling for protein sequence-geometry layers, and that mainstream geometric GNN additive message passing is provably blind to content-geometry binding. Proposes Hyper-Fold, a rank-K separable hypergraph convolutional backbone approaching this ceiling at message-passing cost.

entry.title: LoGo: Token-Level Dynamic Local-Global Attention

author.name: Yuqi Pan, Zheng Li, Bohao Tang, Zhen Qin, Guoqi Li

entry.summary: Proposes LoGo, a token-level dynamic local-global attention mechanism that allocates attention budget per token based on contextual demand, coupling local and global branches within each layer to address the inefficiency of static local-global hybrids as context lengths scale.

entry.title: Do large language models scrutinise what they review? A multimodal audit of scoring calibration, error detection, and author-identity effects

author.name: Emad Alharbi

entry.summary: Audits two multimodal LLMs (Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Pixtral-Large-124B) as ICLR peer reviewers, testing author-identity blinding, prestige manipulation, figure access, and detection of 145 inserted errors. Reveals how review quality and bias susceptibility interact in LLM-based reviewing.

entry.title: Causal Interventions Reveal Typologically Organized Syntactic Mechanisms in Multilingual Language Models

author.name: Sasha Boguraev, Toshiki Nakai, Kyle Mahowald, Julius Steuer

entry.summary: Uses causal interventions from mechanistic interpretability to show cross-lingual transfer of syntactic mechanisms in multilingual LMs across subject-verb agreement, pronoun gender agreement, and filler-gap extraction. Provides empirical support that typologically similar structures are processed by similar internal mechanisms.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Reasoning Models Varies with Where and How Preference Cues Are Delivered

author.name: Aryo Pradipta Gema, Neel Rajani, Rohit Saxena, Wai-Chung Kwan, Pasquale Minervini

entry.summary: Introduces CLAIMPROBE, a claim-level audit decomposing deep-research reports to measure hallucination, misattribution, citation hygiene, and fact recall against retrieved evidence, plus CLAIMWRITER, a hierarchical claim-based writer reducing failures across three DR frameworks. Shows rubric scores can stay stable while factual failures go undetected.

entry.title: The Depth Flow of Token Representations Is Nonlinear and Does Not Descend Its Own Density

author.name: Alexandre Quemy

entry.summary: Fits the layer-by-layer flow of token representations in Pythia models as a discrete Langevin model and finds the dynamics are nonlinear (quadratic drift beats linear maps) and do not descend the model's own density. Provides a dynamical-systems characterization of how representations move through layers.

entry.title: GUIDE: Guiding Internal Evidence with Language Instructions

author.name: Soyeon Caren Han, Hyunsuk Chung, Jinwoo Kim, Seungyeon Ji, Kyungreem Han

entry.summary: GUIDE controls which internal multimodal evidence pathways models use via language instructions, combining grouped parameter-efficient adaptation with instruction-conditioned gating. It also introduces a pathway-level evaluation framework measuring reliance sensitivity and modulation dynamics.

entry.title: Calibrating Small Language Models for Claim Check-Worthiness Detection

author.name: Pratuat Amatya, Venktesh Viswanathan, Vinay Setty

entry.summary: Proposes NN-PPI, a pointwise extension of Prediction-Powered Inference that calibrates small language model predictions for claim check-worthiness at inference time without retraining. Gains of 12-33.8% weighted F1 bring SLMs on par with much larger LLMs in a real fact-checking pipeline.

entry.title: Improving Information Extraction with Learned Queries

author.name: Omar Sharif, Soroush Vosoughi, Nikhil Singh

entry.summary: This paper shows that the queries used to elicit information matter as much as the extraction model: improving question design alone raises performance by 18.6 F1 points across four clinical benchmarks and five LLMs, more than using larger models. It introduces LoQ for document-specific question sets and FeedQ for feedback-driven question optimization, and shows optimized questions can train lightweight extractors. A practical reframing of where extraction quality comes from.

entry.title: Ignorance or Incompetence? Constructing Knowledge-Gated, Verifiable Tasks for LLM Agents

author.name: Hanlin Tian, Minhao Li, Yu Mi, Sihan Zhu, Zhao Yang, Yuxiang Wang, Hongquan Zhu, Qiufei Hu

entry.summary: Introduces a knowledge-gated task-construction protocol for LLM agents that separates task instructions from private-convention artifacts, making benchmark contamination and leakage testable via provenance, leak audits, and executable witnesses. Frontier agents pass 68% with the artifact and 0% without, cleanly demonstrating task dependence. Addresses a real flaw in current agent benchmarks.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling for Video Diffusion Models via Diagnosis-Guided Candidate Recycling

author.name: Hangzhou He, Lunhao Duan, Shanshan Zhao, Kaiwen Li, Qing-Guo Chen, Weihua Luo, Yanye Lu

entry.summary: GEARS introduces test-time scaling for video diffusion that recycles low-scoring candidate samples via guided editing instead of discarding them, salvaging the motion, layout, and appearance structure already encoded. This avoids the waste of generate-and-discard noise-search paradigms and improves lightweight generators without training. Authored with Alibaba-affiliated researchers.

entry.title: A Calibration Audit of Confidence in Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Nanxing Nick Deng, Qing Cheng, Niclas Zeller, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Audits per-pixel confidence emitted by seven feed-forward 3D reconstruction backbones across thirteen datasets, scoring rank correlation, calibration level, across-range behavior, and interval coverage. Finds confidence ranks error well but predicted uncertainty is off by a median factor of 2.4 when read outside training conditions. Important caution for downstream systems consuming these confidence signals.

entry.title: FaceSnap: Real-Time Personalized Lightstage Facial Performance Capture

author.name: Rukhshanda Hussain, No\'e Artru, Emeline Got, Luiz Gustavo Hafemann, Alexandre Messier, Brandon Dearlove, Rafael M. O. Cruz, Abdallah Dib, Eric Granger

entry.summary: FaceSnap is an end-to-end lightstage facial capture system where a one-time multi-view personalization enables real-time monocular capture, jointly estimating geometry and dynamic 4K texture at 83 fps. It substantially reduces the cost of production-quality digital human capture.

entry.title: Evaluating the Safety of Deep Learning-Based Brain MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Dat Tat Mai, Thai Viet Pham, Thu Nguyen Thi Dang, James Jin Kang

entry.summary: A PRISMA-based systematic review of 263 studies finds that only a small fraction evaluate the safety of deep learning brain MRI reconstruction against lesion erasure or false tissue synthesis, failure modes that pixel-averaged metrics like PSNR and SSIM miss. It exposes a serious blind spot in a clinically sensitive domain.

entry.title: RoboPhys-3D: A Comprehensive Embodied World Model Evaluation via 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Tianyi Wang, Jiazhou Chen, Yiming Xu, Xiangyu Li, Tianyi Zeng, Chih-Hsien Chou, Ning Lu, Liang Peng, Junfeng Jiao, Christian Claudel

entry.summary: RoboPhys-3D is a 3D-grounded benchmark for embodied world models built on RoboTwin 2.0, covering 50 manipulation tasks with 5,000 episodes and 25,000 multi-view videos, processing generated and ground-truth rollouts through the same 3D reconstruction pipeline to separate reconstruction error from generation error. It tests whether generated rollouts preserve scene state.

entry.title: EviAnchor: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models via Regional Visual Evidence Compensation

author.name: Sihang Jia, Shuliang Liu, Songbo Yang, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: EviAnchor mitigates hallucinations in large vision-language models via a training-free inference framework that anchors regional visual evidence in decoder layers, countering the observed attenuation of visual influence in later layers. Regional Evidence Anchor slots aggregate dense visual tokens into spatially structured representations.

entry.title: Frontier vision-language models have overtaken young adults at detecting AI-generated portraits -- but not their calibration

author.name: Sunwhi Kim (Hwasung Medi-Science University, Dept. of Bio-Healthcare), Sunyul Kim (Yonsei University, Graduate School of Engineering, Dept. of Artificial Intelligence), Meounggun Jo (Hoseo University), Jini Tae (Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology, School of Humanities and Social Sciences)

entry.summary: This study benchmarks 19 vision-language models on detecting AI-generated identity-matched portraits, finding that four July-2026 releases broke the ceiling: GPT-5.6-Sol reached 92.8 percent balanced accuracy, above young adults, and Claude-Fable-5 detected every AI image, while calibration remained poor. It tracks the closing human-machine gap on deepfake detection.

entry.title: CometVLA: Co-Training on an Embodied Data Pyramid towards Physical Understanding

author.name: Hanwen Wan, Dafeng Chi, Linbo Zhai, Tianao Shen, Yuzheng Zhuang, Tianle Zhang, Peidong Liu, Liang Lin, Xiaoqiang Ji

entry.summary: CometVLA co-trains on an embodied data pyramid comprising CometData, a physical VQA corpus strictly aligned with robot action domains, and CometBench, a corresponding benchmark, using Global Action Prior tokens as a learnable bottleneck to inject physical commonsense into action generation. Targets brittleness in manipulation requiring physical understanding.

entry.title: SUN: Persistent Programs For Language-Grounded Control-to-Learning-to-Real Policies

author.name: Weiqi Wang, Zhi Li, Yudong Lei, David Martinez, Xiaofeng Gao, Yuxin Jiang, Chenfanfu Jiang, Yingnian Wu, Demetri Terzopoulos, Ran Gong

entry.summary: SUN Programs are typed executables in which geometric and contact relations are defined once and compiled into aligned MPC costs, satisfaction predicates, RL rewards, guards, and diagnostics; the Kuafu system uses large vision-language models to synthesize them from language and scene semantics, unifying model-based control and learning in long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: TimesFM-3: A zero-shot foundation model for multivariate forecasting

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google research blog announcing TimesFM-3, a zero-shot foundation model for multivariate time-series forecasting, positioned within their data management research stack.

entry.title: LCoT-GV: Graph Attention Networks for Verifying Long Reasoning Chains in Large Language Models

author.name: B\'er\'enice Jaulmes, Mehwish Alam

entry.summary: LCoT-GV represents long chains-of-thought as reasoning graphs with nodes for steps and edges for semantic/logical relations, then trains a graph attention network to verify chain correctness. It includes a new graph-oriented verification dataset built from QA reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Personas Differ from Native-Language Generation: Language Pathways Shape LLM Interpersonal Advice

author.name: Jinhee Won, Xinlan Emily Hu

entry.summary: Tests whether native-speaker persona prompting reproduces the outputs of generating advice in the target language and translating back, using 600 interpersonal advice questions across 13 languages and 8 LLMs. Finds the two are not interchangeable, showing personas differ systematically from native-language generation.

entry.title: Beyond the Payload: How User Invocation Shapes Coding Agent Vulnerability to Repository Poisoning

author.name: Fukang Zhu, Binbin Zhao, Ruixiao Lin, Ping He, Tianyu Du, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: Introduces CIPR, a benchmark of 1,920 instances in 20 poisoned repositories showing that user-side choices (task delegation, phrasing, supplied skills/rules, called Prompt-Level Configurations) systematically shape coding-agent vulnerability to repository poisoning. Shifts attention from attacker-side to user-side risk factors. Practical for securing agentic software engineering.

entry.title: Speculative Probing: LLM Monitoring at Speculative-Decoding Cost

author.name: Collin Zhang, Tingwei Zhang, Vitaly Shmatikov

entry.summary: Repurposes the speculative-decoding machinery already present in modern LLM inference stacks for real-time classification and safety monitoring at near-speculative-decoding cost, escaping the trade-off between fast but context-blind hidden-state probes and accurate but expensive dedicated judge models. Clever systems-level reuse with safety, filtering, and behavioral-monitoring applications. Strong practical potential.

entry.title: EvoUndo: Recoverability-Constrained Self-Evolution for LLM Agent Harnesses

author.name: Tanmay Sah, Dolly Sah, Harshul Jain, Tanya Sah

entry.summary: EvoUndo studies a safety-critical property of self-evolving LLM agents: whether their own prompt, tool, and harness modifications can be reliably reversed across counterfactual states. Across 600 one-shot self-evolution tasks, 197 capability-improving mutations failed recoverability verification, and conventional repair strategies recovered none of them. It introduces verification tooling for a risk that current agent frameworks largely ignore.

entry.title: A Survey on Rubric-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Language Models

author.name: Zifei Shan, Fangning Shao

entry.summary: This survey organizes rubric-guided reinforcement learning for language models under a Bayesian framework treating constitutions as priors over evaluation criteria and rubrics as conditional instantiations. It maps how structured, interpretable criteria can replace opaque scalar rewards in RLHF for reward design, feedback generation, and policy optimization. Timely given the shift from scalar reward models toward rubric- and principle-based rewards.

entry.title: FedEHR-Agents: Federated Agentic Optimization for Automated EHR Modeling

author.name: Jun Bai, Ruilin Wang, Yue Li

entry.summary: DAMP is the first study of post-training quantization of recurrent states in gated-delta (GDN) and Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) based language models, which replace KV caches with fixed-size recurrent states stored in FP32. It shows uniform INT8/FP8 quantization degrades accuracy and proposes decay-aware mixed-precision quantization instead. Directly relevant to the memory and latency costs of the new linear-attention model families.

entry.title: Deriving Scaling Laws for OpenEuroLLM Models: Learning Rate, Batch Size and Loss

author.name: Niccol\`o Ajroldi, Diana Alexandra Onutu, Haider Al-Tahan, J\"org Franke, Sampo Pyysalo, Jenia Jitsev, Aaron Klein

entry.summary: Introduces performative privacy, formalizing the intuition that privacy loss reduces future data participation and thus long-term utility. Analyzes a repeated mean-estimation model where agents leave after leaks, characterizing the noise-participation trade-off in differential privacy.

entry.title: Video Generative Models as Geometry Learner

author.name: Haosen Yang, Jifei Song, Zhensong Zhang, Xiatian Zhu, Jiankang Deng

entry.summary: Repurposes pretrained video generative models as a unified, data-efficient framework for depth and surface normal estimation, formulating geometry estimation as next-frames prediction that exploits correlations between geometric targets.

entry.title: SemKV: Semantic Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization Guided by the Quality Cliff for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Daeha Lee, Do-Hyung Kim, Jae-Hong Kim

entry.summary: Shows under a multi-seed statistical protocol that uniform KV cache quantization has a sharp quality cliff (statistically indistinguishable from FP16 down to ~2.3 bits, collapsing below), which reframes mixed-precision KV quantization: above the cliff importance indicators are interchangeable. Transfers across models.

entry.title: When Do Larger Batches Help Scale LLM Reinforcement Learning?

author.name: Ziniu Li, Jinbo Wang, Guanhua Huang, Feiyuan Zhang, Pengbo Li, Alex Chen

entry.summary: Analyzes when larger batches help LLM RL by separating algorithmic from systems effects: at equal cumulative samples with retuned hyperparameters, a batch-size-invariant family emerges, so wall-clock gains hinge on throughput rather than statistical benefits. Directly relevant to RLVR infrastructure decisions.

entry.title: On the Plasticity Collapse in Continual Machine Unlearning

author.name: Yingdan Shi, Xiang Xu, Kaize Ding, Alfred O. Hero, Ren Wang

entry.summary: Identifies plasticity collapse in continual machine unlearning: sequential unlearning requests accumulate geometric constraints in parameter space, creating saturated subspaces that progressively impair future forgetting. Provides theoretical analysis plus empirical demonstration of the effect.

entry.title: Higher-Dimensional Rotary Position Embedding

author.name: Yixing Li, Ruobing Xie, Yudong Zhang, Yushi Bai, Samm Sun, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes HD-RoPE, extending rotary position embeddings from independent 2D rotations to higher-dimensional rotations with a Paley-I orthogonal basis for dense, isotropic phase mixing, while preserving relative-position closure and enabling length extrapolation.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Qwen3-27B for C-to-Rust Code Translation: A Three-Stage Curriculum of Pretraining, Debugging-Aware SFT, and Task-Specific SFT

author.name: Pu Zhao, Changdi Yang, Yixiao Chen, Yi Gao, Yifan Cao, Haochen Zeng, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune Qwen3-27B with a three-stage curriculum (continued pretraining, debugging-aware SFT, and task-specific SFT) to specialize it for translating C code into safe, idiomatic Rust. This targets a high-value security problem, since automated C-to-Rust translation can eliminate entire classes of memory-safety vulnerabilities in legacy systems.

entry.title: The information geometry of product-reference discrete diffusion: Interaction growth complexity and optimal scheduling

author.name: Martin J. Wainwright

entry.summary: Martin Wainwright analyzes product-reference discrete diffusion through an information-geometric lens, introducing interaction growth complexity (IGC) as a path-based data-geometry measure that exactly characterizes KL discretization error. The framework yields optimal stepsize schedules and iteration-complexity results for epsilon-accurate sampling.

entry.title: APIFlow-Bench: Measuring Whether Agents Survive Long, Dependent API Workflows

author.name: Zelin Wan, Arash Nourian, Xiaoxiao Li, Nihar Nandan, Kamalakannan Nandagopal

entry.summary: Introduces APIFlow-Bench, an auditable benchmark for long-horizon, dependent REST-API workflows that decomposes agent performance into seven engineering capabilities and requires answers supported by actual call paths. It uses adversarial audits and zero-LLM self-tests to verify graders and solvability.

entry.title: Learning Simple Test-Time Environments for LLM Web Agents

author.name: Junxuan Li, Zijun Liu, Ziyi Huang, Peng Li, Yuzhou Liu, Ming Yan, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Test-Time Environment Decomposition (TTED), a label-free method letting LLM web agents decompose complex real-world webpage observations into simple sub-modules via trial steps and adapt their behavior from experience during inference, improving robustness when transferring from curated environments.

entry.title: When Safety Speaks a Language: A Mechanistic Analysis of Safety-Language Identity Entanglement in LLMs

author.name: Apoorva Upadhyaya, Sandipan Sikdar

entry.summary: Presents a mechanistic analysis of multilingual safety alignment using sparse autoencoder features across three instruction-tuned LLMs and eight languages, finding safety features are architecture-dependent and geometrically entangled with language identity. Explains why safety degrades unevenly across languages.

entry.title: Looking Again: Measuring Sycophancy in the Reasoning Chains of Multimodal Models Under Pressure

author.name: Mahir Numayeer Islam, Gakuto Okuyama, Nikolaus Siauw, Shivank Garg, Madhur Panwar, Vasu Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark measuring sycophancy in large multimodal reasoning models, pairing four visually grounded datasets (mathematical, clinical, temporal, demographic) with five user-pressure conditions in single- and multi-turn settings. Fills a real gap since no reliable sycophancy measure existed for LMRMs.

entry.title: A Unifying Perspective on Language Model Representations: From Filler-Role Structure to Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Zhang Enyan, R. Thomas McCoy

entry.summary: Proposes Tensor Product Representations as a unifying hypothesis for language model internal structure, showing mathematically and empirically that TPRs unify additive analogies, linear probing, sparse autoencoders, and activation patching. Connects classic filler-role binding theory to modern mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: A Hub of Short Rows Inflates Intrinsic Dimension Estimation of Token Embeddings

author.name: Alexandre Quemy

entry.summary: Shows that a hub of short rows near the origin of token embedding tables systematically biases nearest-neighbor intrinsic dimension estimators like TwoNN, inflating measured dimensionality. After removing the hub, measured ID collapses to a narrow range across eleven models from GPT-2 to recent large models.

entry.title: MURANO: Design, Run, and Reproduce Mechanistic Interpretability Experiments as Composable Pipelines

author.name: Alireza Bayat Makou, Emirhan B\"oge, Phu Gia Hoang, Federico Tiblias, Jingcheng Niu, Subhabrata Dutta, Richard Eckart de Castilho, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: MURANO is an open-source framework representing mechanistic interpretability operations (loading, recording, attribution, intervention, evaluation) as composable pipeline steps with typed artifacts. It improves reproducibility and interoperability across existing interpretability libraries.

entry.title: You Shouldn't Have Asked: A Pragmatics-Inspired Taxonomy for Evaluating LLM Refusals

author.name: Ruoxuan Li, Pinqiao Wang, Sheng Li, Cameron Robert Jones

entry.summary: Proposes the first pragmatics-grounded taxonomy of LLM refusals, treating refusals as face-threatening acts, and applies it to 16 LLMs across 14 harm categories. Finds substantial variation in how appropriately models refuse across contexts.

entry.title: Faithfulness Is Not Free: Auditing Offline KV-Cache Quantization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Atta Ul Asad, Ahsan Bilal, Muhammad Ali, Muhammad Haseeb, Dean F. Hougen

entry.summary: This paper audits whether offline KV-cache quantization in retrieval-augmented generation damages faithfulness, not just accuracy, evaluating Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct under INT8 and INT4 on RGB and HotpotQA. It finds INT8 is near-lossless while INT4 degrades both metrics, with faithfulness eroding even when answers remain superficially correct. The distinction between grounded and merely correct answers is a useful reframing for compressed RAG deployments.

entry.title: Every Token Leaves a Ripple in the Stream of Thought: Eliciting Model-Internal Token Saliency for Chain-of-Thought Compression

author.name: Tianyi Zhao, Yinhan He, Wendy Zheng, Chen Chen

entry.summary: MIST elicits token saliency for chain-of-thought compression from model-internal signals, measuring the ripple each reasoning token leaves in the residual stream as the answer forms. This avoids external scorers or heuristic signals indirectly tied to answer computation. The approach targets cheaper inference by pruning CoT traces for model adaptation.

entry.title: S3Gym: Can LLMs Turn Self-Testing and Self-Judging into Self-Improvement?

author.name: Jiajun Shi, Siyuan Tao, Yuhao Wu, Zexuan Wang, Jingyuan Zhang, Jiaheng Liu, Xinping Lei, Xinrong Zhang, Siyuan Fang, Zhewen Tan, Tianle Cai, Junhao Fang, Jiameng Huang, Yueyang Wang, Jinkai Liu, Yuxuan Zhang, Jian Yang, Zhoujun Li, Shen Yan, Wenhao Huang, Ge Zhang

entry.summary: S3Gym is an interactive benchmark evaluating whether LLM agents can turn self-testing and self-judging into self-improvement, instantiated in seven text-based games with executable environment verifiers. It separates permissive exploration from strict held-out evaluation, addressing whether agents can actively test behavior and improve future decisions rather than acting as fixed policies. This targets a capability most agent benchmarks do not measure.

entry.title: EvoSkill Injection: Red-Teaming Autonomous Skill Generation and Evolution in Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Doyun Kim, Chanwoo Kim, Sugyeong Eo, Yeo-Chan Yoon, Chanjun Park

entry.summary: Defines EvoSkill Injection, a threat model where malicious capabilities are generated, stored, and reused as legitimate skills in self-evolving LLM agents, and proposes SARGE, a red-teaming framework to test skill-generation pipelines. Opens a new attack surface beyond direct prompt injection. Timely as agentic skill libraries proliferate.

entry.title: GenFirst: Generation Before Reconstruction for Stable End-to-End Latent Generative Modeling

author.name: Guangting Zheng, Yiyuan Zhang, Tao Yang, Yunpeng Chen, Rui Zhu, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: GenFirst studies stable end-to-end training of latent generative models, identifying that the KL entropy term is essential for preventing latent collapse and analyzing the generation-reconstruction conflict. The proposed generation-first ordering of objectives stabilizes joint VAE-plus-generator training. Addresses a foundational architectural question in latent generative modeling.

entry.title: Robust retinal biometrics for patient identity verification and retrieval across age and imaging devices

author.name: Jose D. Vargas-Quiros, Dennis Bontempi, Jeroen Vermeulen, Bart Liefers, Sven Bergmann, Caroline C. W. Klaver

entry.summary: A retinal biometric system for patient identity verification and retrieval trains a ConvNeXtV2 metric-learning encoder on 227,004 fundus images from 21,851 patient-eyes in the Rotterdam Study, validated externally on UK Biobank and AREDS across devices and up to 32.6 years of follow-up. It addresses real patient-record integrity problems in medicine.

entry.title: BLARM: Animating 3D Objects from Video via Blending Latent Rigid Motion Primitives

author.name: Pradyumn Goyal, Yizhak Ben-Shabat, Hsueh-Ti Derek Liu, Haomiao Jiang, Snehasish Mukherjee, Kyle Spence, Mark Stauber, Evangelos Kalogerakis, Yunze Zeng

entry.summary: BLARM animates a static 3D mesh to follow a monocular video using a compact set of learned time-varying rigid motion components blended via time-invariant skinning weights, requiring no rigs, cages, or annotations. A factorized spatial-temporal attention decoder conditions deformation latents on video features.

entry.title: RoboGesture: Real-Time Semantic-aligned Co-Speech Gestures Generation for Humanoid Interaction

author.name: Zifan Wang, Ziang Ren, Pengyang Shi, Zirui Wang, Chenghuai Lin, Tianze Wang, Zekun Qi, Liangliang Zhao, He Wang, Li Yi

entry.summary: RoboGesture is a robot-centric framework for real-time semantic co-speech gestures on humanoid robots, co-designing a 300-category gesture dataset, automated synthesis of collision-safe data, and control to overcome modality eclipse and sim-to-real safety gaps. It powers a complete human-humanoid interaction loop.

entry.title: Doc-REFRAG: Rethinking Multimodal Document Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Ruofan Hu, Shengyang Xu, Minjie Hong, Xiaoda Yang, Sashuai Zhou, Ke Lei, Tao Jin, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: Doc-REFRAG tackles multimodal RAG over multi-image documents with DocLongRAG, a 343K QA-pair dataset averaging 37.4 retrieved images per question, and a question-guided framework that compresses visual tokens into coarser representations to cut compute from irrelevant visual content. It targets realistic document QA workloads.

entry.title: A Degradation-Tolerance Benchmark for Camera-Only End-to-End Driving

author.name: Haohua Que, Handong Yao

entry.summary: DriveDegrade is a benchmark injecting sixteen corruption families at five severities into camera-only end-to-end driving policies, evaluating open-loop planning on nuScenes and NAVSIM plus a CARLA closed-loop anchor to measure how much degradation a policy tolerates before driving breaks. It finds mild degradation barely affects planning.

entry.title: Behavior-Skill: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Chunyun Ma, Lun Luo, Xingjian Luo, Xiexing Feng, Hang Zhang, Wei Liu, Feng Qiao, Yaonan Wang, Huimin Lu, Xieyuanli Chen

entry.summary: Behavior-Skill is a fine-grained benchmark for long-horizon VLA evaluation containing 235,492 skill instances from 10,000 demonstrations across 50 household tasks and 34 skill categories, pairing skill instructions with observation-action segments and restorable intermediate states to expose intermediate failures hidden by task-level metrics.

entry.title: Zeva: In-Context Causal Learning for Generalizable Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Fu Chen, Xin Ding, Bingjia Huang, Xiangyu Li, Mingju Wang, Jiawei He, Kun Li, Wei Sun, Yunxin Liu, Hao Wu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: Zeva enables in-context causal learning from a robot's own physical interaction experience during deployment with the policy model frozen: a Causal Interaction Extractor encodes executed actions and induced state changes into causal signals stored in dual-timescale memory and retrieved to inform subsequent actions.

entry.title: prefilling an emergently misaligned model with reasoning traces that produced misaligned answers increases misalignment rates by ~8% but reasoning traces that produce misaligned answers aren't detectable through text monitoring

author.name: nesiacel

entry.summary: Independent experiment prefilling an emergently misaligned model with chain-of-thought traces that produced misaligned versus aligned answers, finding misaligned prefilling raises misalignment rates by roughly 8 percent while misaligned reasoning traces are not detectable via text monitoring. Follows up a prior CoT-monitoring study with released code and data.

entry.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models

author.name: Naoto Usuyama, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Tristan Naumann

entry.summary: Microsoft introduces GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, distilled, dramatically more efficient versions of its pathology foundation models, enabling whole-slide analysis and tumor microenvironment modeling across larger patient cohorts toward population-scale discovery. Released as open research models explicitly not validated for clinical use.

entry.title: LLM-Augmented Causal Discovery: Probabilistic Fusion of Edge Existence and Orientation

author.name: Neville K. Kitson, Anthony Constantinou

entry.summary: Introduces Probabilistic Dependency Graphs, an edge representation carrying distributions over directed, undirected, and absent states, to fuse broad but unreliable LLM causal knowledge with Bayesian network structure learning. Across 26 benchmark networks, ensembles of three structure-learning algorithms and three frontier LLMs, a simple 50/50 fusion improves F1 over either source alone in 22 of 26 cases. A clean, well-evaluated recipe for combining data-driven and model-encoded causal knowledge.

entry.title: AI Alignment through a Game-theoretic Lens: A Survey

author.name: Yanan Cai, Zhongrui Zhao, Zhigang Lu, Ickjai Lee, Wei Emma Zhang, Minhui Xue, Yihong Zhang, Shuchao Pang, Wei Xiang

entry.summary: Surveys AI alignment through a game-theoretic lens, organizing recent work around preference diversity, alignment priority, and temporal dynamics, and identifying where current methods fall short for context-dependent, non-transitive, multi-party preferences in high-risk deployments. A timely synthesis as multi-agent deployment grows. A useful map for researchers rather than new results.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Theory-of-Mind-Grounded Friction for Epistemic Alignment

author.name: Yifan Zhu, Kyeongmin Rim, James Pustejovsky

entry.summary: Operationalizes Theory-of-Mind inference as a control signal within Frictive Policy Optimization, computing epistemic friction from four-part belief structures at each referring expression. This separates surface coordination from true epistemic alignment in dialogue, capturing silent divergence.

entry.title: Generalization over Memorization: Generalization-Aware Diffusion Adaptation for Single-Image Multi-View Synthesis

author.name: Jie Li, Xingchen Zou, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: GoM is the winning solution to the ACM Multimedia 2026 Grand Challenge on single-image multi-view synthesis, ranking first among 293 teams under severe constraints (40 training scenes, one forward pass per view, no geometry or post-processing). Key insight: shared train/validation scenes made memorization masquerade as view control, so they introduce scene-disjoint validation and generalization-aware adaptation. The diagnosis of memorization-vs-generalization in model selection is broadly instructive.

entry.title: RealSWE: A Compositional Evaluation of Coding Agents under Realistic User Requests

author.name: Gyuhyeong Kim, Hyojung Gwon, Jeonghyeon Kim, Kyuhong Shim, Sunjae Lee

entry.summary: Quantifies the gap between SWE-bench-style tasks and real user requests, finding that casual, minimally contextualized problem-statement-only prompts account for 88 percent of real prompts but just 7 percent of benchmark problems, and builds RealSWE, a compositional evaluation of coding agents under such realistic requests. Exposes how current benchmark scores may overstate deployment readiness. Directly relevant to the coding-agent ecosystem.

entry.title: HyQuant: Hybrid-Precision Quantization for LLM Attention

author.name: Jiatong Ding, Bingxin Xing, Yu Zhang, Dian Ding, Xiaodong Yi, Xianbin Ouyang, Feihu Zhou, Kun Zhang, Zhenyu Guo, Hao Pan, Guangtao Xue, Yiming Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes HyQuant, a hybrid-precision quantization framework for LLM attention that keeps a small set of vertical-line tokens and local-window states in high precision, selected by lightweight criteria, while low-bit quantizing the remainder, improving the accuracy-efficiency balance over smoothing-only outlier handling. Attention quantization remains a core inference cost problem. Credible authorship including Kun Zhang and a targeted efficiency win.

entry.title: The Illusion of $\textit{What If}$: Evaluating the Breakdown of Counterfactual Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Yucheng Wang, Yuetian Du, Zhengyi Liu, Rongyu Zhang, Bing Zhao, Boyu Yang, Ming Kong, Lin Qu, Hu Wei, Jie Liu, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: Presents WhatIfBench, 220 open-domain, open-form, long-horizon what-if questions across STEM, humanities-social science, and hybrid scenarios, plus PRISM, an evaluator that converts free-form responses into response-derived semantic causal graphs to score counterfactual reasoning beyond fixed-variable settings. Current models reportedly show substantial breakdown. A well-constructed diagnostic pair for an underexplored capability.

entry.title: Prove2Me: An Open Collaborative Platform for Scaling Math Formalization

author.name: Shuze Chen, Kunal Marwaha, Xiaoyang Lu, Henry Yuen, Tianyi Peng

entry.summary: Prove2Me is an open collaborative platform for scaling formal math formalization in Lean 4, exploiting AI coding agents so that users can contribute machine-checked proofs via natural language. It enables internet-scale human-plus-AI mathematical collaboration with correctness guaranteed by the proof assistant. This could significantly expand participation in formalization projects.

entry.title: When Linguistic and Internal Confidence Diverge in Large Language Models

author.name: Hefan Zhang, Bingquan Zhang, Ming Cheng, Saeed Hassanpour, Weicheng Ma, Soroush Vosoughi

entry.summary: A broad study across 30 models finding that linguistic (verbalized) confidence in LLMs frequently diverges from logits-based and semantic-entropy uncertainty, with instruction-tuned models often over-reporting confidence. Important for trusting self-reported confidence in deployed systems.

entry.title: Conformal Uncertainty Quantification Guarantees for Neural Operators

author.name: Tom Stent, Nicolas Boull\'e

entry.summary: Develops a split conformal framework providing distribution-free pointwise coverage bands for neural operator outputs on function spaces, with proven marginal coverage guarantees for measurable residual fields. Brings principled UQ to PDE surrogate models.

entry.title: The Halt Vector: Internalizing a Causal Steering Intervention for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Dylan Jayabahu, Tinuade Adeleke

entry.summary: Proposes the halt vector, internalizing a difference-of-means steering direction into model weights so reasoning models stop thinking once their answer probability settles, cutting excess chain-of-thought without global length penalties. Careful treatment of off-axis corruption during weight installation.

entry.title: Flow-JEPA: Flow Matching for Robust Latent Dynamics in JEPA World Models

author.name: Yanchen Huo, Ziying Song, Yadan Luo

entry.summary: Flow-JEPA replaces the deterministic autoregressive predictor in JEPA world models with a conditional flow-matching dynamics model that jointly generates future latent sequences, improving robustness to perturbations and error accumulation for reconstruction-free latent world modeling.

entry.title: MedCache: Efficient and Temporally Valid Memory for Longitudinal Clinical Agents

author.name: Hei Ting (Una), Chan, Chenwei Wu, Xueshen Liu, Boyuan Zheng, Liyue Shen, Jiasi Chen, Z. Morley Mao

entry.summary: Introduces MedCache, a benchmark and systematic study of memory design (curation, organization, retrieval, reasoning) for longitudinal clinical agents over multi-visit, multi-specialty patient records. Finds temporal validity matters more than retaining more history.

entry.title: DASC: Decay-Aware State Compression for Hybrid Linear-Attention Serving

author.name: Yanqi Yu, Pingwei Sun, Jianchao Tan, Tao Zhang, Yuchen Xie, Xunliang Cai, Yao Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DASC, decay-aware state compression for serving hybrid linear-attention models such as Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention, exploiting the observation that different heads and channels retain prefix information over different retention horizons. This reduces checkpoint memory and evictions in prefix-reuse serving. Timely as hybrid linear-attention architectures scale in open-weight models.

entry.title: Confounding Masquerading as Improvement: A Systematic Evaluation of Offline Reinforcement Learning for Stroke Antithrombotic Treatment in a 129,000-Patient Registry

author.name: Kihun Rhee

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates offline RL for stroke antithrombotic treatment across five algorithm families and 14 reward designs in a 129,000-patient registry, identifying reward-embedded confounding where proxy terminal rewards encode baseline severity rather than treatment efficacy. Apparent policy improvements of +0.0069 to +0.0101 are almost entirely attributable to confounding. A crucial cautionary study for clinical offline RL.

entry.title: Learning Where Outcomes Change:Credit-Addressable Reasoning for Multimodal Geometry

author.name: Jiani Guo, Junjie Wang, Jie Wu, Pengxiang Zhao, Dongdong Zhang, Shaohan Huang, Yujiu Yang, Furu Wei

entry.summary: Introduces credit-addressable reasoning for multimodal geometry, instantiating it as Code-CoT, which represents visual relations as line-addressable executable code, and CE-GRPO, which assigns credit at event boundaries rather than distributing a terminal reward across the whole response. From an MSRAsia-affiliated team including Furu Wei, it directly targets the credit assignment problem in trajectory-level RL for VLMs. A promising refinement of RL post-training for reasoning.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling for Scientific Equation Discovery

author.name: Haowei Lin, Hubert Lim, Xiangyu Wang, Letian Huang, Di He

entry.summary: The paper studies test-time scaling for open-ended scientific equation discovery, unifying Best-of-N, refinement, tree search, and evolution under a compute-allocation view. On LLM-SRBench it finds search width is the dominant factor, extending TTS analysis beyond closed-ended math and coding tasks.

entry.title: TACS: Trajectory-Aware Candidate Selection for LLM Jailbreak Suffix Optimization

author.name: Shiliang Xiao

entry.summary: Shows that greedy loss-based candidate selection is a hidden bottleneck and form of reward hacking in gradient-based jailbreak suffix optimization, proposing a trajectory-aware selection framework (TACS) that augments per-step evaluation with trajectory information to improve downstream jailbreak outcomes.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Functional Vectors for Emotion Detection in Large Language Models

author.name: Jieying Xue, Phuong Minh Nguyen, Minh Le Nguyen, Shogo Okada

entry.summary: Investigates whether function vectors - latent task directions injected from in-context demonstrations - can transfer across languages, using multilingual multi-label emotion recognition as a semantically challenging benchmark under standard and structured ICL settings.

entry.title: A Unified Perspective on Conformal Prediction and Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization for Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Kehan Long, Yiqi Zhao, Pol Mestres, Lars Lindemann, Nikolay Atanasov, Jorge Cort\'es

entry.summary: Unifies conformal prediction and Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization by viewing both as finite-sample quantile estimators of test scores, deriving transferable guarantees between the two frameworks. Relevant to reliable decision-making under distribution shift in control and automation.

entry.title: Recognition-Refusal Misalignment in LLMs: Why Models Answer Structurally Unanswerable Questions

author.name: Yucheng Du, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: Shows that across instruction-tuned models from 1.7B to 70B, a single linear direction in hidden states separates answerable from structurally impossible math and code prompts, yet this recognition direction is nearly orthogonal to the canonical safety-refusal direction. Explains refusal failures as routing misalignment rather than missing recognition.

entry.title: AI Can Be Easily Persuaded in Clinical Decision Making

author.name: Jiayuan Zhu, Jiazhen Pan, Fenglin Liu, Minhao Hu, Junde Wu

entry.summary: Shows through controlled experiments that AI clinical decision systems are easily swayed by professional authority, institutional affiliation, claimed past performance, multiple physician endorsements, and repeated pressure, with senior-clinician sources shifting about 10% more cases. Highlights a serious robustness gap for high-stakes medical AI.

entry.title: DVBench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Understanding Dynamic Charts and Narratives in Data Videos

author.name: Bomiao Wang, Zekai Shao, Jiexiang Lan, Xiaoliang Fu, Xingchen Zeng, Siming Chen

entry.summary: Introduces DVBench, a benchmark of 300 real-world data videos and 1,000 human-verified QA pairs for evaluating how multimodal LLMs understand dynamic charts combined with narration. Evaluations of nine MLLMs show Gemini-3.1-Pro performs best overall, with Kimi-k2.5 the strongest open-source model.

entry.title: Seeing the Unseen: Visual Similarity for Pixel Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Ran Zhang, Miryam de Lhoneux, Wessel Poelman

entry.summary: Studies continued pre-training of pixel-based language models for low-resource languages, using Tibetan as a case study and introducing four rendering-level metrics of visual script similarity. Finds that orthographic similarity to related Brahmic scripts drives cross-lingual transfer.

entry.title: WildSEEK: Evaluating Language Models for Information-Seeking

author.name: Tanise Ceron, Joachim Baumann, Elisa Bassignana, Berat Cabuk, Dirk Hovy, Debora Nozza

entry.summary: WildSEEK provides 3k manually annotated real-user information-seeking queries and an evaluation framework for LLM responses, with risk-sensitive domain annotations (health, finance) and factoid versus analytical query distinctions. It aims to capture in-the-wild complexity missing from synthetic evaluations.

entry.title: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?

author.name: Yuhao Wu, Jingyuan Zhang, Jiajun Shi, Yuxuan Zhang, Xinping Lei, Junting Zhou, Zexuan Wang, Yuchen Wu, Huan Zhou, Duo Wang, Yinzhu Piao, Yongchang Peng, Yunfeng Shi, Jin Chen, Zuo Wang, Jinkai Liu, Jiaheng Liu, Wenxuan Zhang, Shen Yan, Wenhao Huang, Ge Zhang

entry.summary: ASPIRE is a benchmark for vague-goal-driven self-evolution: the agent receives only a natural-language capability goal with downstream evaluation tasks hidden, and must operationalize the goal by choosing data, update methods, and constructing training procedures. This contrasts with standard self-evolution work that presumes human-specified tasks and metrics. It probes a more realistic and open-ended form of autonomous learning.

entry.title: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing

author.name: Adrians Skapars, Edoardo Manino

entry.summary: BLOOM-WILT is a full automated auditing pipeline that elicits natural multi-turn instances of rare behaviors using logit tilting and an auditor model that revises its conversational strategy across rounds, requiring no training or white-box access beyond next-token distributions. Improves sample efficiency of automated LLM auditing. Relevant to scalable oversight and red-teaming.

entry.title: Text-Guided Diffusion-Based Adversarial Attacks on Chest X-Ray Images

author.name: Basudha Pal, Arjun Narayanan, Neha Ajith, Vikas R Bhat, Muhammad Umair

entry.summary: Proposes text-guided diffusion-based adversarial attacks on chest X-ray classification, optimizing learnable text conditioning to produce plausible radiographic variation rather than constrained pixel perturbations. Demonstrates vulnerabilities in multi-disease models where attacks can flip several overlapping diagnostic predictions. Important safety evidence for clinical AI deployment.

entry.title: LightNav-0: Eliciting VLM Spatial Intelligence for Generalist Embodied Navigation

author.name: Shaoan Wang, Aocheng Luo, Fei Huang, Jingyi Xu, Xiaoyang Wang, Yueyu Wang, Qianli Ma, Fan Yang, Ran Mei, Jia Wei, Jiangpeng Hu, Xuhao Liu, Hongming Chen, Yuanbin Shao, Yiyang Lin, Ziliang Li, Liang Pan, Xinhang Liu, Yuntao Ma, Tingxiang Fan

entry.summary: LightNav-0 is a compact generalist embodied navigation model that elicits spatial intelligence from a pretrained VLM and aligns it with navigation control without task-specific prediction heads, representing diverse goals in a unified interface across tasks, environments, and embodiments.

entry.title: Scaffolding Foundation Models into Physical-World Agents Pushes the Frontier of Long-Horizon Navigation

author.name: Zixing Lei, Gengze Zhou, Xiong-Hui Chen, Jiazhao Zhang, Yiyang Huang, Hang Yin, Haoqi Yuan, Qi Wu, Weixin Li, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: NavMCP is an agentic scaffolding framework coupling a VLM reasoning agent with a navigation foundation model executor for long-horizon exploration: the VLM decides what evidence to seek and when to stop, while the NFM grounds each sub-goal into reliable closed-loop navigation, addressing the complementary weaknesses of both model classes.

entry.title: Thinking Costs Tokens: When More Structure is Worth the Price

author.name: Thomas Nolasque, John Grey, Calista Pham, Ankit Vani

entry.summary: Measures whether token-budget thresholds exist below which structured inference (planning, verification, repair) hurts performance and above which it helps, comparing a single-call monolith against a verified search architecture on financial QA tasks across 14 budget tiers using GPT-5.4 mini, an established frontier small model released months earlier. The study spans roughly 28,000 evaluation cells. Directly relevant to the economics of reasoning-time compute.

entry.title: GRACE:Gradient-guided Coreset Selection for LLM Unlearning

author.name: Praveen Bushipaka, Andrea D'Angelo, Lucia Passaro, Tommaso Cucinotta

entry.summary: GRACE addresses a realistic weakness in LLM unlearning: forget and retain sets usually must be inferred from just a few seed examples of undesired behavior. It computes a forget direction from gradients and uses orthogonal matching pursuit to build compact forget and retain coresets. This makes unlearning more applicable to practical, heterogeneous-corpus settings.

entry.title: Trajectory-Level Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tianxiang Pan, Baitao Gong, Mo Guang, Hongwei Yong, Tianpeng Jiang, Yaqian Li, Zheng Cao, Kaiwen Long

entry.summary: This paper develops trajectory-level speculative decoding for diffusion language models, which unlike autoregressive models must speculate over multi-token denoising trajectories with explicit unmasking orders. It constructs draft trajectories via confidence-stratified tree exploration and verifies them with blockwise parallel evaluation, addressing the throughput collapse of current dLLM decoding. An important efficiency advance for an emerging model class.

entry.title: Quanta Perception as Probabilistic Events

author.name: Varun Sundar, Pavan Thodima, Sacha Jungerman, Mohit Gupta

entry.summary: This paper introduces probabilistic events, a computational primitive for quanta (single-photon) perception that represents photon streams by the posterior over time since the last intensity change, enabling real-time processing where raw streams exceed compute budgets. It addresses sensitivity-dynamic-range trade-offs in extreme-environment perception for robotics. A novel sensing-compute interface with potential for nighttime and high-speed navigation.

entry.title: Semantic Watermarking with Order-Robust Detection over Sub-sentence Units

author.name: Abdulrahman Diaa, Jonathan Petit, Florian Kerschbaum

entry.summary: This paper introduces an adaptive embedding displacement attack (EDA) against semantic watermarks, using a public paraphraser and surrogate encoder to reword, reorder, and resegment text under one objective without access to the generator or key. At a 5 percent false-positive rate it substantially degrades detection, exposing a weakness in meaning-tied watermarking schemes. Important adversarial evidence for the watermarking research community.

entry.title: CARDINAL Predicts Cardiovascular Risk From Non-contrast Cardiac CT

author.name: Roy Gabriel, Nattakorn Kittisut, Jamshid Hassanpour, Michael Galarnyk, Abanoub Abdelmalak, Marly van Assen, Carlo N. De Cecco, Arshed Quyyumi, Ali Adibi

entry.summary: CARDINAL learns compact representations from routine non-contrast cardiac CT for major adverse cardiovascular event prediction, evaluated in 17,659 patients against AHA pooled cohort equations, PREVENT, coronary artery calcium, and other baselines across 1 to 10 year horizons. It moves CT risk assessment beyond a handful of handcrafted biomarkers. A large-scale, clinically grounded deep learning result with real deployment potential.

entry.title: OpenStamp: A Watermark for Open-Source Language Models

author.name: Miroojin Bakshi, Saksham Rastogi, Danish Pruthi

entry.summary: OpenStamp embeds watermarking logic directly into an open-source language model's weights by modifying only the unembedding layer, since users with white-box access can simply disable sampling-based watermarks during inference. Experiments across two models show comparable performance to sampling methods while surviving user-side tampering. It addresses the fundamental applicability gap of LLM watermarking for open models.

entry.title: VISTA: Verifier-Informed Student-to-Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Zewen Ding, Zezhong Wu, Zhou Tao, Shida Wang, Shizhuo Hou, YongXiang Hua, Haoyu Cao, Linli Xu

entry.summary: VISTA extends on-policy self-distillation by letting a verifier update the privileged teacher when its distribution misaligns with valid student reasoning, addressing one-way supervision failures. Targets improved reasoning training efficiency.

entry.title: How Proper Scoring Rules Shape LLM Forecasting

author.name: Benjamin Turtel, Paul Wilczewski, Kris Skotheim, Ville A. Satop\"a\"a, Philip E. Tetlock

entry.summary: Evaluates five proper scoring rules as training objectives for LLM forecasters on resolved real-world events, finding that although theory predicts identical incentives, the choice of rule systematically shapes calibration, bias, information, and noise profiles. Includes Tetlock among authors.

entry.title: Curvature Cryptanalysis of Smooth Transformer Feed-Forward Networks

author.name: Munawar Hasan, Apostol Vassilev

entry.summary: Shows that smooth two-layer transformer FFNs with GELU/SiLU activations expose a second-order (Hessian-based) model extraction channel under chosen-input raw-output access, formalizing identifiability conditions and reducing query cost via structural decomposition. NIST-affiliated security analysis.

entry.title: The Safety Relay in Roleplay Jailbreaks: A Component-Resolved Causal Analysis of Harm Recognition and Refusal

author.name: Md Mokarram Chowdhury, Ernie Chang, Yang Li

entry.summary: Uses mechanistic interpretability to analyze roleplay jailbreaks, tracing hidden-state contrasts across two benchmarks, three model families, and four wrappers to isolate which wrapper components, persona, scenario, task, reverse refusal behavior. It identifies a safety relay mechanism that turns compliance on. Substantive safety research with causal, component-resolved methodology.

entry.title: Evaluating Tiny Recursive Models Across Training for Code Generation

author.name: Anjani Sirivella, Aanisha Newaz, Glaucia Melo

entry.summary: Evaluates a ~28M-parameter Tiny Recursive Model for code generation across training, testing whether teacher-forced advantages survive free-running generation. The study addresses an open evaluation-methodology question for recursive-depth architectures trained with next-token loss.

entry.title: RouteSparse: Input-Conditional Pattern Routing for Budgeted Long-Context Prefilling

author.name: Chao Zhang, Yifan Ji, Ziyan Zhang, Kai Song, Fei Lin

entry.summary: Introduces RouteSparse, which routes each attention head and prompt segment among a library of GPU-efficient sparse patterns for long-context prefilling, with a latency-aware router and an attention-output error certificate. Improves on MInference's fixed per-head pattern assumption.

entry.title: R$^2$A: Learning Persona Policies Through Persona Representation Learning and Runtime Alignment

author.name: Mohan Zhang, Chengsong You, Xiaoyu Cao, Zhen Sun, Xiaohan Jia, Junwei Zhou, Yongchao Chen

entry.summary: Presents a Persona Selection-Realization framework that decomposes persona-conditioned behavior into selection and realization components, identifying gaps where static persona prompting falls short of an ideal policy. R2A learns persona policies in two stages using structured representations and runtime alignment.

entry.title: Error-Type-Aware Loss Reweighting for Robust Named Entity Recognition with Noisy LLM Labels

author.name: Elena Merdjanovska, Jonas Golde, Alan Akbik

entry.summary: Shows that fine-tuning NER models on LLM-annotated data ignores heterogeneous annotation noise, and that existing noise-robust losses are not transferable to sequence labeling. Proposes error-type-aware loss reweighting that treats missing mentions and type errors differently.

entry.title: Evidence-Bounded Mental Health Reasoning from Heterogeneous Speech Protocols

author.name: Chengyuan Gao, Jiang Wu, Tao Lu, Jiayan Guo, Mingkun Xu, Tianyi Zang, Shangyang Li

entry.summary: The authors reformulate multimodal mental health screening as evidence-bounded reasoning, arguing that heterogeneous speech protocols (free interviews vs fixed reading tasks) carry different evidentiary validity that uniform reasoning violates. They introduce the Evidence Package Benchmark with 1,870 packages and show even long chain-of-thought LLMs overclaim support. This connects clinical protocol heterogeneity with hallucination control.

entry.title: PaperGym: Rubric-Centered Evolution for Research-Plan Generation

author.name: Yuhan Wang, Zhengxi Lu, Yuchen Yan, Kaitao Song, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: PaperGym turns research papers into training environments for research-plan generation, using rubrics derived from method and experiment sections as critics while synthesizing questions from goals and background to prevent reward-by-paraphrase. It addresses the absence of verifiable reward environments for research planning, a decisive capability for AI scientists. The framework also avoids compressing rubrics into a single scalar per rollout.

entry.title: How Identity and Opinion Shape Political Sycophancy in LLMs

author.name: Li-Ni Fu, Chang-Chih Meng, Chien-Hua Chen, Hen-Hsen Huang, I-Chen Wu

entry.summary: The paper disentangles two triggers of political sycophancy in LLMs: opinion alignment with explicit narratives versus identity-based stereotyping from demographic labels, using 450 manually checked political dilemmas to evaluate 13 instruction-tuned models. It finds a dissociation between susceptibility to explicit opinion adaptation and identity-conditioned behavior. This refines a blunt safety concern into measurable components.

entry.title: NBS: No Bias Stereo

author.name: Vage Taamazyan, Zhuowen Shen, Stefan Hinterstoisser, Alberto Dall'Olio, Agastya Kalra, Aarrushi Shandilya, Xin Li, Wenping Wang, Kartik Venkataraman

entry.summary: NBS (No Bias Stereo) demonstrates that a plain end-to-end vision transformer with no architectural inductive biases, trained on massive synthetic data, achieves state-of-the-art stereo accuracy with superior runtime efficiency, challenging the belief that stereo-specific inductive biases are necessary. A notable result about data scale versus architectural priors.

entry.title: InfraOcc: An Infrastructure Occupancy Benchmark with Static-to-Dynamic Reasoning

author.name: Lei Yang, Xiaokai Bai, Boqi Li, Chunmian Lin, Li Wang, Ziying Song, Jiahuan Zhang, Enhui Ma, Haibao Yu, Jiaqi Ma, Kaicheng Yu

entry.summary: InfraOcc is the first real-world infrastructure-side semantic occupancy benchmark, with dense voxel annotations for 290 roadside multi-modal sequences and a static-dynamic decoupled annotation pipeline plus models exploiting persistent-static structure. Differentiates roadside occupancy from ego-vehicle perception.

entry.title: The Potential of Haptic Foundation Models

author.name: Jianquan Wang, Haiwei Dong, Abdulmotaleb El Saddik
