author.name: Mingwen Zhang, Jisheng Dang, Minqiang Yang, Bimei Wang, Bin Hu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multi-agent RL framework for video reasoning coupling a trainable Grounder with a frozen Verifier that assigns query-conditioned segment scores, using a group-relative policy gradient favoring trajectories that outperform within-input peers. This extends verification from inference-time reranking to training-time guidance for grounded video QA and temporal grounding. Co-author Tat-Seng Chua adds credibility.

entry.title: Rate-Coding Bundle Memory: A Unified Model of Memory and Control for Symbolic Computation in the Brain

author.name: Teun van Gils, Rowan P. Sommers, Markus Ostarek, Peter Hagoort

entry.summary: RCBM proposes a neurobiologically plausible hybrid model combining rate-coded symbols in continuous space with a bundle memory system, grounded in the Symbolic Subsystem Hypothesis. It aims to explain cognitive phenomena including one-shot learning, pattern separation, and binding, bridging connectionist and symbolic systems. The work is a theoretical contribution bridging neuroscience and cognitive architectures.

entry.title: ContextBias: Controlled Evaluation of Bias Persistence Under Context Shift in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Shaghayegh Kolli, Sina Emami, Moreno D'Inc\`a, Pouyan Nejadi, Nicu Sebe, Massimiliano Mancini, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: ContextBias is a controlled evaluation framework and benchmark (92 roles, 1,656 prompts, 66,240 generated images) testing whether role-linked stereotypical associations in text-to-image models persist under contextual shift. Evaluating four state-of-the-art models, it isolates the effect of contextual variation on visual representations of professions. The question of bias stability versus context sensitivity is a genuine open issue in generative fairness.

entry.title: Geometry of Divergence: Tracking Hidden-State Trajectories for Adaptive Multi-Turn Reasoning

author.name: Jie Liang, Zhengxin Yu, Hamid Nasiri, Peter Garraghan

entry.summary: Formulates multi-turn LLM agent reasoning as a hidden-state trajectory characterized by temporal curvature and variance slope, using these geometric signals to detect representation drift and adaptively manage context under resource constraints. Evaluated across four tasks and three LLMs. Offers a mechanistic lens on long-horizon agent reliability.

entry.title: Defending Wearable VLMs Against Private Attribute Inference

author.name: Zhimin Li, Pan Wang, Jingxian Chen, Yuantao Tang, Anthony Chen, Qian Lou, Jingtong Hu

entry.summary: Investigates privacy leakage in split VLM inference for wearable devices, where intermediate visual tokens transmitted off-device can reveal private attributes about the wearer even when final responses are benign, and proposes defenses for this joint privacy-utility problem. Addresses an underexplored leakage surface in egocentric AI.

entry.title: Foundational feature fusion for conditional flow matching in 6D pose estimation

author.name: Amir Hamza, Davide Boscaini, Fabio Poiesi

entry.summary: FunFlow6D uses features from geometric and appearance foundation models with conditional flow matching for 6D pose estimation, removing the need for task-specific encoder training. A cross-attention fusion mechanism resolves pose ambiguities. This shows foundation-feature reuse can replace supervised encoders in a state-of-the-art pose pipeline.

entry.title: LightFuse: Relightable Interactive Gaussian Scene Reconstruction via Multi-Scan Fusion and 2D Gaussian Ray Tracing

author.name: Haonan Zhou, Gaoxiang Linghu, Youlin Jia, Hongyu Cui, Kewei Wei, Kaiyue Zhou, Bruce X. B. Yu, Gaoang Wang

entry.summary: LightFuse reconstructs relightable interactive scenes from multi-object scans using 2D Gaussians with explicit material-illumination decomposition and physically based ray-traced relighting. It fuses observations across arrangements into a shared background plus movable objects and refines geometry for consistent shadows under edits. Advances interactive scene reconstruction beyond baked lighting.

entry.title: Neural video codecs quality assessment dataset and benchmark

author.name: Nikolay Safonov, Nikita Gornostaev, Alexandra Dubonos, Dmitriy Vatolin

entry.summary: Presents a large-scale subjective dataset and benchmark for quality assessment of neural video codecs versus traditional codecs, targeting the novel temporal compression paradigms NVCs introduce. Fills an infrastructure gap as deep learning enters video compression. Valuable community resource from an established video-quality group (MSU/Vatolin).

entry.title: TRINITY: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark for Personal-Style Video Highlight Detection

author.name: Qianqian Chen, Hyun Bin Kim, Denzel Elden Wijaya, Yang Yi, Bo Liu, Yangkai Ding

entry.summary: GATE fuses reliability-gated Gaussian evidence for training-free transductive test-time adaptation of vision-language models with all parameters frozen.

entry.title: Efficient and High-Quality Depth Estimation via Pixel-Space Diffusion with Linear Attention

author.name: Bingde Liu, Wu Ran, Jinglei Zhang, Huanhuan Yuan, Chao Ma

entry.summary: Lapis combines linear attention with one-step pixel-space diffusion for efficient high-fidelity monocular depth estimation, using a coarse-to-fine hierarchy to fix structural consistency issues of naive linear attention. Targets the O(N^2) cost of scaling generative depth models.

entry.title: Dynamic Hub-and-Spoke Memory for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Xinru Jiang, Lin Zhao, Xi Xiao, Yunbei Zhang, Janet Wang, Chenrui Ma, Haolin Li, Yanzhi Wang, Yifan Gong, Octavia Camps

entry.summary: D-HSM is a training-free streaming video understanding framework that compresses distant history into an entity-centered hub-and-spoke textual memory while keeping recent frames as visual tokens, retrieving question-aware evidence on demand. Balances long-range memory with fine-grained perception.

entry.title: ImageCAS-X: a dataset and benchmark for coronary artery segmentation and centerline extraction in coronary CT angiography

author.name: Kit M. Bransby, Esther {\O}ksnebjerg, Kristoffer Kj{\ae}r, Jacob Kirkeby, Yasmin El Youssef, A\"ida Jim\'enez, Philip R. Pedersson, Martina C. de Knegt, Klaus F. Kofoed, Rasmus R. Paulsen

entry.summary: ImageCAS-X provides voxel-wise lumen annotations, centerlines, and mesh surfaces for 800 coronary CT angiography scans, plus benchmarks of established segmentation methods. Addresses a key data bottleneck for quantitative atherosclerosis analysis.

entry.title: MEOM: Multi-View Expected-OKS Maximization for Human Pose Triangulation

author.name: Ziliang Xiong, Henglin Shi, Per-Erik Forssen

entry.summary: MEOM formulates multi-view human pose triangulation as Multi-view Expected-OKS Maximization, using full 2D heatmap probability mass rather than collapsed peaks, with highest-density-region calibration for heatmap reliability. Principled fix to a known fragility of algebraic triangulation.

entry.title: Failure or Drift? Evaluating Monocular SLAM under Synthetic and Real-World Corruptions

author.name: Abhay Skaria Thomas, Shashank Agnihotri, Margret Keuper

entry.summary: Presents UFPR-PEs, a Brazilian face recognition bias-evaluation benchmark from videos of elected politicians annotated with official self-declared census race/color categories including parda, absent from US/Europe-centric schemas. Built from compressed public video preserving hard samples.

entry.title: Rad-R: A Raw-ADC Radar Dataset and Capture-Invariant SSM for Hardware-Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Mainak Mallick, Junghwan Yim, Seung-Kyum Choi

entry.summary: Rad-R introduces a raw-ADC automotive mmWave radar dataset paired with calibrated hardware faults (vibration, antenna misalignment, radome blockage) at measured severities, plus a capture-invariant state-space model for fault diagnosis. It fills a genuine data gap since radar hardware faults require physical measurement.

entry.title: Multimodal Shared Latent Representation of Narration, Microscope and iOCT Images for Phase Recognition in Vitreoretinal Surgery

author.name: Onur Izmitlioglu, Shervin Dehghani, Tarek Ghannoum, Benedikt Schworm, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: The paper builds a shared latent representation across surgical narration, microscope video, and intraoperative OCT for phase recognition in vitreoretinal surgery, using microscope views as an anchor to bridge modalities. It exploits abundant online narration as semantic supervision where synchronized intraoperative multimodal data is scarce.

entry.title: Is Deformable Image Registration Ready for Brain Metastasis Reirradiation Dose Accumulation? A Longitudinal MRI Benchmark of Registration Accuracy

author.name: Hengjie Liu, Manju Sharma, Xinyi Fu, Di Xu, Ke Sheng

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates deformable image registration methods for brain metastasis reirradiation dose accumulation on 87 manually screened longitudinal MRI lesion pairs, a controlled but clinically meaningful test case. It provides a rigorous clinical benchmark for learning-based and optimization-based DIR.

entry.title: RePair: Turning Retrieval Failures into Counterfactual Hard Pairs

author.name: Siyi Liu, Xiaorong Zhu, Enjun Du, Xinyu Zuo, Lisheng Duan, Haijin Liang, Jin Ma, Junfu Pu, Yongqi Zhang

entry.summary: RePair turns retrieval failures into counterfactual hard positives by minimally correcting the failure-causing residual of top-ranked false positives, then training CLIP-style dual encoders on these constructed pairs. It combines hard-sample mining and synthetic augmentation while conditioning hardness on actual model failures.

entry.title: Autoregressive Mosaics: Probing 2D Spatial Reasoning in Text-Only Language Models

author.name: Ashwin Nedungadi, Stefan Oehmcke, Stefan L\"udtke

entry.summary: Autoregressive Mosaics introduces AM-Bench, which separates geometry translation from open-ended 2D layout composition in text-only code-generating LLMs, finding all eight evaluated models translate specified geometry reliably but degrade on open-ended layout. It probes whether text-trained LLMs possess internal spatial representations.

entry.title: "More Is Different'' in Neural Circuits: Algebraic Emergence of Effective Theories in Canonical Recurrent Motifs of Biological Neuronal Networks

author.name: Nima Dehghani

entry.summary: This theoretical paper represents canonical neural circuit motifs (divisive normalization, winner-take-all) algebraically as finite transformation systems, analyzing transition monoids to distinguish emergent structure from inherited structure upon composition. It shows aperiodic updates can generate non-aperiodic monoids, formalizing emergence in neural motifs.

entry.title: Toward Trustworthy Robot-Assisted Sliding Palpation for Shallow Vessel Localisation with a Calibrated Digital Twin

author.name: Piotr Blaszyk, Wen Fan, Kaizhong Deng, Daniel Elson, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a robot-assisted sliding palpation framework that uses a calibrated digital twin to generate labeled tactile training data for locating shallow subsurface vessels, reducing reliance on costly real-world sensor data. Bayesian-optimization-based domain adaptation calibrates the twin against real trajectories, and a spatio-temporal GNN performs vessel classification. Relevant to safe robot-assisted venous access and vessel-aware manipulation.

entry.title: Self-Aware Active Learning Enables Continual Improvement in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Dong Hu, Chao Huang, Carman K. M. Lee, Dimitrios Kanoulas

entry.summary: SAGE is an active learning framework for autonomous driving in which a predictive world model generates fear (short-horizon risk and uncertainty) and curiosity (novelty) signals, letting agents estimate their own incompetence, seek assistance, and convert safety-critical encounters into targeted improvement. Aimed at post-training adaptation for long-tail events.

entry.title: Learning to infer and manipulate through distributed whole-arm interaction in a soft robot

author.name: Chuhan Zhang, Ebrahim Shahabi, Kseniia Khomenko, Wei Pan, Cosimo Della Santina

entry.summary: Introduces a physical intelligence framework for soft robots in which distributed whole-arm compliant interactions jointly reveal task-relevant information and organize manipulation behavior, inspired by elephants and octopuses, treating contact as an information source rather than a disturbance to reject.

entry.title: SleepWalking: Privileged Representation Shaping for End-to-End Blind Locomotion in Legged Robots

author.name: Zheng Pan, Tenghui Wang, Peilin Li, Shiyu Zhou, Hao Sun, Yan Ma, Liang Yu, Liang He

entry.summary: SleepWalking reframes partial observability in blind legged locomotion as an information-retention problem and proposes SWAQ, a one-stage end-to-end framework using next-step privileged physical reconstruction to shape internal representations that retain task-relevant information, avoiding explicit state estimators or long histories.

entry.title: Autonomously Acquiring Robot Manipulation Skills with Language-Driven Quality-Diversity

author.name: \'Emiland Garrab\'e, Mahdi Khoramshahi, St\'ephane Doncieux

entry.summary: Combines quality-diversity algorithms with LLM-driven specification so robots autonomously acquire diverse motion primitive archives from free-form natural language task descriptions, removing the need for hand-written fitness and diversity metrics while retaining zero-shot adaptability.

entry.title: A Catalogue of Corrigibility Counter Arguments

author.name: Felix Moses

entry.summary: A catalogue of counterarguments to corrigibility as an alignment target, written in the context of renewed mainstream interest following the Hugging Face incident, engaging with the CAST strategy and industry incentives around helpfulness.

entry.title: Update on Security at METR

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: METR discloses two security incidents in 2026: a stolen inference API key in March and systematic infrastructure probing with an unsuccessful access attempt in May, reporting no sensitive data accessed and detailing their subsequent security investments. No evidence found of agents hacking third parties during evaluations.

entry.title: PCFBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Product Carbon Footprint Estimation

author.name: Krishna Rao, Andrew Dumit, Shaena Ulissi, Jacob Feintzeig, P. James Joyce, Daniel Frank, Steven Watson, Jonathan Glidden, Gizem Ilayda Dinc, Travis M. Kwee

entry.summary: Introduces PCFBench, reportedly the first benchmark to decompose product carbon footprint estimation into 614 expert-labeled independently evaluable tasks spanning decomposition, retrieval, ontology matching, and numerical extraction, exposing error sources that total-emissions scoring hides and that isolated sub-task scoring misses. Targets high-stakes domain workflows where intermediate correctness matters. A useful new evaluation surface for agentic systems.

entry.title: AERA: Adaptive Evidence Residual Allocation for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Ziming Wang, Ivor Tsang, Hangwei Qian

entry.summary: Demonstrates that checkpoint-level correctness during test-time scaling evolves non-monotonically, so observable evidence strength can mislead stopping decisions, and introduces AERA, a learned sequential controller that allocates additional computation where recovery is likely rather than trusting confidence or agreement. A conceptual insight plus an adaptive-stopping method. A solid contribution to adaptive test-time compute.

entry.title: Detecting AI Impostors: How Do Middle Schoolers Identify LLM Agents in a Live Collaborative Setting?

author.name: Dan Schumacher, Pragathi Durga Rajarajan, Haven Kotara, Roman Rendon, Kosi Atupulazi, Deepti Tagare, Ismaila Temitayo Sanusi, Fred G. Martin, Anthony Rios

entry.summary: Introduces DoppelBot, a cooperative social deduction game for studying how middle schoolers detect AI impersonation by LLM agents. Repeated exposure improves detection accuracy, driven by a shift from surface cues to deeper strategies, and the game prompts reflection on privacy and impersonation.

entry.title: Retrieving Relations, Detecting Fallacies: A RAG Approach to Political Debate Analysis

author.name: Deborah Dore, Greta Damo, Elena Cabrio, Serena Villata

entry.summary: Combines retrieval-augmented generation with argumentative discourse structure to detect fallacies in political debates, retrieving both topical world knowledge and relations among arguments rather than encoding structure as static classifier features. Targets a high-stakes misinformation-adjacent task where surface text alone is insufficient. A solid applied contribution to argument mining.

entry.title: ReToolSQL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Robust Text-to-SQL

author.name: Pratik Kakkar, Chandra Dhir, Ravi Shankar, Pareekshit Reddy Gaddam, Anup Shirgaonkar

entry.summary: Combines a supervised warm-start on rejection-sampled reasoning traces with multi-turn agentic reinforcement fine-tuning over tool-use trajectories for text-to-SQL, arguing the two stages act on complementary axes of solution diversity and iterative recovery. Extends single-turn execution-feedback RL toward robust multi-turn refinement. Competent post-training work in a crowded area.

entry.title: CoRe-MoE: Compact Reusable MoE for Continual Multimodal Instruction Tuning

author.name: Runze Liu, Naibin Gu, Mingxu Ai, Yuqing Li, Peng Fu, Zheng Lin, Weiping Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes the SVD of task-specific LoRA updates in continual multimodal instruction tuning, finds substantial overlap in input and output subspaces across tasks, and proposes CoRe-MoE, which reuses shared subspace experts and learns lightweight task coordinates instead of full new LoRA experts per task, cutting parameter overhead while preserving prior knowledge. A practical efficiency contribution to continual learning. Competent and moderately novel.

entry.title: Rubric-to-Code Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Rui Jin, Jikai Chen, Yihan Chen, Hao Zhou, Demin Zhu, Kaichen Yang, Dong Wang, Linjian Mo, Chenyi Zhuang

entry.summary: Tackles the weakness of GRPO-style sequence-level rewards in interactive web-app generation by converting rubric-level functional feedback into localized token-level credit over the code regions that satisfy each requirement. A targeted credit-assignment improvement for reinforcement learning on structured artifacts. Aligned with the broader move toward fine-grained rewards in RL from verifiable signals.

entry.title: Learning from Hard Prompts: Difficulty-aware Advantage Amplification in Dynamic Sampling

author.name: Siyuan Gan, Yuhan Li, Xiran Wang, Linjian Meng, Boyan Wang, Zhen Zhao, Jing Huo, Lei Bai, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Theoretically shows that dynamic sampling in DAPO wastes hard prompts by filtering them when zero advantages yield zero gradients, asymmetrically amplifying advantage estimates, and proposes difficulty-aware advantage amplification to exploit hard-to-sample correct responses. A useful theoretical refinement of a widely used RL recipe. Incremental but well motivated.

entry.title: MAP: A Benchmark on Multimodal Accessibility Planning for Real World Places

author.name: Jason Armitage, Ioannis Tsochantaridis, Linda Mazzone, Chuqiao Yan, Srini Narayanan, Sarah Ebling

entry.summary: MAP is the first benchmark evaluating multimodal AI systems as assistants for users with accessibility requirements when planning visits to real-world places. It introduces claim verification and visual evidence retrieval assessments around point-of-interest accessibility features. It highlights a socially impactful blind spot in current multimodal evaluation.

entry.title: RetailAgent: Structured Adverse Timing in Self-Conditioned Multimodal LLM Trading Agents

author.name: Yupeng Zhang, Liuyuan Jiang, Hongyi Huang, Bingheng Li, Lisha Chen

entry.summary: RetailAgent examines whether LLM agents acting as intraday equity traders exhibit predictable directional structure, using an exposure-matched measure on long/flat decisions. It finds persistent negative timing skill across modality, horizon, state, and model family, meaning the agents systematically buy at unfavorable moments. This is a cautionary result for deploying LLM agents in financial markets.

entry.title: Logos: An Agent Harness on a Cross-Process Bus

author.name: Hanzhang Jia, Liheng Zeng, Hao Cheng, Yi Gao, Bo Ma

entry.summary: Logos generalizes a formally treated spatiotemporal-composability calculus for agent capability assembly from a single process to a cross-process bus, exploiting the statelessness of language models to keep cross-step state outside the model. This removes the single failure domain that suspends all components when the host process dies. It connects formal agent theory with systems-level fault tolerance.

entry.title: SciReC: Diagnostic Evaluation of Multimodal, Multi-Turn Relational Reasoning with Adaptive Interaction

author.name: Nilay Yilmaz, Naga Sai Abhiram Kusumba, Stella Wenxing Liu, Yezhou Yang

entry.summary: SciReC is a model-adaptive multimodal academic dialog benchmark for relational reasoning (analogical, structural, cause-effect) in multimodal LLMs, paired with DMRA, a deficit-based diagnostic framework that quantifies contributions of visual understanding, knowledge, and memory recall. It moves evaluation from aggregate scores toward component-level diagnosis. Useful for locating specific capability gaps in MLLMs.

entry.title: Select, Don't Train: The Benefits of Modular Entity Disambiguation with LLM-Based Selection

author.name: Fina Polat, Daniel Daza, Pengyu Zhang, Klim Zaporojets, Paul Groth

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies modular entity disambiguation, separating candidate retrieval from LLM-based selection instead of training dual-encoder models that must balance recall and fine-grained selection in one embedding space. It clarifies the interplay between retrieval strategies and LLM selectors and avoids costly retraining as knowledge graphs change. Practical guidance for KG construction pipelines.

entry.title: XHotpotQA: A Benchmark for Cross-Lingual Knowledge Composition in Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Iman Barati, Arash Ghafouri, Behrouz Minaei-Bidgoli

entry.summary: XHotpotQA is a controlled benchmark for cross-lingual knowledge composition in multi-hop QA where question, bridge evidence, answer evidence, and distractors have explicit language assignments, exposing failures at language boundaries that monolingually translated benchmarks hide. It provides 23k audited instances with sentence-level support supervision. Fills a real gap in multilingual reasoning evaluation.

entry.title: LitCurate: A Configuration-Driven AI-Assisted Framework for Scientific Database Construction with an Application to Lower-Mantle Equation-of-State Data

author.name: Abin Shakya, Wilson Samuels, Dominica Wilson, Gioia A. Marchi, Israa Draz, Chenxing Luo, Renata M. Wentzcovitch

entry.summary: LitCurate is an open-source, configuration-driven framework for building scientific databases from literature using LLMs within an auditable, stage-wise workflow covering discovery, extraction, and validation, demonstrated on lower-mantile equation-of-state data. It addresses keeping scientific context intact when extracting quantities from publications. Valuable reusable infrastructure for AI-assisted data curation in the physical sciences.

entry.title: From Perspective to Fisheye Depth Estimation and Open-Vocabulary Segmentation

author.name: Rit Gangopadhyay, Alex Wong

entry.summary: This paper proposes Distortion Extenders, learnable parameters modeling fisheye distortion coefficients and the latent distributional shift between fisheye and perspective images, allowing vision foundation models trained on perspective data to generalize to wide field-of-view cameras for depth estimation and open-vocabulary segmentation. A parameter-efficient adaptation to a real covariate shift problem. Relevant to robotics and surveillance optics.

entry.title: SOMTab: Set-Order Mamba for Efficient Tabular In-Context Learning

author.name: Hao Wang, Siyu Zhang, Wei Ma

entry.summary: SOMTab is a Set-Order Mamba architecture for tabular in-context learning that separates representation construction (Mamba-based state-space mixing over unordered table tokens) from query-conditioned retrieval (attention retained only at the final stage), questioning whether attention is needed throughout the pipeline. It targets the efficiency limits of attention-heavy tabular foundation models. A sensible architectural efficiency exploration.

entry.title: Nested Byte-Level Vocabularies Are Cheap to Deploy and Expensive to Share: A Pre-Registered Negative Result

author.name: Christos Koutsiaris

entry.summary: A pre-registered negative-result study showing nested byte-level BPE vocabularies allow exact weight-slicing for multi-size deployment (bit-exact logits, 66% fewer deployed weights), but the sharing benefits across vocabulary sizes do not materialize. Notable for methodological transparency with pre-registered claims and 30 trained models.

entry.title: Aero Hand Open: A Simulation-Ready Tendon-Driven Hand for Dexterous Manipulation Learning

author.name: Nan Wang, Mohit Yadav, Jonathan Wulff, Aidan Rosenbaum, Kezhou Chen, Yuvan Sharma, Xu Dong, Yiwei Tao

entry.summary: Presents Aero Hand Open, an affordable tendon-driven anthropomorphic hand released simulation-ready, addressing the difficulty of simulating underactuated cable transmissions for dexterous manipulation learning. Open hardware for the manipulation research community.

entry.title: Off-Policy Evaluation for Semantic ID Recommenders: Does the Model's Own Code Hierarchy Help?

author.name: Artem Betlei

entry.summary: Studies off-policy evaluation for generative recommenders emitting hierarchical semantic IDs, showing per-item OPE fails under near-argmax logging but marginalizing to code-prefix clusters restores estimable support, with the model's own code hierarchy serving as the action abstraction.

entry.title: PathGuide: Dynamic Classifier-Free Guidance via On-Policy Transport Alignment

author.name: Avishag Nevo, Tamir Hazan

entry.summary: PathGuide reformulates classifier-free guidance selection for flow-based generative models as an on-policy transport problem using the weak form of the continuity equation, deriving a dynamic guidance criterion with path-correctness guarantees.

entry.title: PokaiTrainer: Scaling Belief-State Search to Competitive Pok\'emon VGC

author.name: Max Yu

entry.summary: PokaiTrainer scales belief-state equilibrium search to competitive Pokemon VGC, which violates tractable-subgame assumptions (simultaneous moves, hundreds of joint actions, hidden information), via a fast Rust battle engine and factorization techniques.

entry.title: Spatial Entropy based Partitioning for Spatiotemporal Graph Unlearning

author.name: Qiming Guo, Wenbo Sun, Ye Wang, Wenlu Wang

entry.summary: Introduces IsleNet, which uses spatial-entropy-guided partitioning and virtual edges to enable exact, efficient machine unlearning on spatiotemporal graphs, motivated by GDPR/CCPA requirements. Only the affected subgraph encoder is updated instead of full retraining.

entry.title: Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion

author.name: Runyu Zhang, Jiawei Zhang, Gioele Zardini, Saurabh Amin, Asuman Ozdaglar

entry.summary: Proposes projected-gradient-guided diffusion that treats the Stein denoising operator as an approximate projection onto the data geometry, keeping gradient-guided samples on structured feasible sets. Provides analysis and a practical in-denoiser projection update.

entry.title: Which LLM for Which Work? Budgeted Model Allocation under Uncertain Evaluation

author.name: Hamed Khosravi, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Formulates budgeted LLM model allocation across recurring workloads as a multiple-choice knapsack problem and analyzes why both causal/off-policy and evaluator-validation approaches fail to estimate the needed quality table, especially under proxy-score and selection bias.

entry.title: LLMODE: Aligning ODEs with LLMs via Gated Token Injection for Irregular Spatio-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Di Zhang, Jingyang Zhang, Ziqian Wang, Chi Zhang, Yikun Ban, Ziwei Zhang, Ruijie Wang

entry.summary: Proposes LLMODE, using a frozen LLM backbone with a graph-aware ODE encoder and fixed-budget token resampling for irregular spatio-temporal forecasting, addressing temporal asynchrony and context limits token-efficiently.

entry.title: Sensitivity-Constrained Neural Operators for Data-Efficient Forward and Inverse Modeling of Partial Differential Equation Systems

author.name: Abdolmehdi Behroozi, Chaopeng Shen, Daniel Kifer, Kathryn Lawson

entry.summary: Proposes sensitivity-constrained neural operators that augment PDE surrogate training with sampled solver-derived Jacobian supervision, amortizing input-output response information across batches to improve forward and inverse reliability.

entry.title: Joint Spatiotemporal Spectral Neural Operators for Learning PDEs on Irregular Domains

author.name: Abdolmehdi Behroozi, Chaopeng Shen

entry.summary: Introduces the Graph Spectral Neural Operator, combining graph spectral decomposition with temporal Fourier transforms in a unified space-time kernel to learn PDE solution operators on irregular, non-Cartesian domains without warping or interpolation.

entry.title: When 3D Gaussian Splatting Recovers Real Surfaces

author.name: Songhe Wang, David Johnathan Miller

entry.summary: Develops a mathematical framework based on a first-hit rendering abstraction to identify when 3D Gaussian Splatting recovers true surfaces versus billboard-like overfits, proving a strict identifiability window tied to bounded angular capacity and confirming billboard failures experimentally.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Refinement for Kilometer-Scale Probabilistic Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Dohyun Park, Changhoon Song, Tengyuan Chang, Yoo-Geun Ham, Youngjoon Hong

entry.summary: Introduces exPreCast-ENS, a conditional residual diffusion framework upgrading a 4 km deterministic radar nowcaster into a 1 km probabilistic ensemble, recovering 38-47% of human-forecast skill in two 2023 Korean extreme precipitation events.

entry.title: Tail-Replay: Escaping the Curse of Linear Attention in Prefix Caching for Hybrid LLMs

author.name: Yirui Liu, Ruoling Qi, Xuaner Wu, Penghang Liu, Jian Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Tail-Replay, a prefix-caching mechanism enabling unconstrained token-level prefix reuse in hybrid LLMs that interleave full and linear attention, escaping checkpoint-aligned rollback constraints of existing recurrent-state caching.

entry.title: AutoScientist-Quant: Self-Evolving Coding Agents for Automatic Research in Quantitative Investment

author.name: Zongqian Li, Yaoyiran Li, Yaohui Guo, Ming Zhang, Nigel Collier, Eugene Ie

entry.summary: AutoScientist-Quant frames quantitative investment research as one budgeted search problem in which a controller decides when to generate, combine, pivot, or stop alpha discovery, and also automates library and model selection. It explicitly addresses test-window leakage, a common flaw in LLM-driven alpha search.

entry.title: Generation of High-Level Concepts in 3D Scene Graphs via Autoregressive Diffusion

author.name: Jose Andres Millan-Romera, Samuel Cognolato, Holger Voos, Jose Luis Sanchez-Lopez, Luciano Serafini

entry.summary: The paper presents a unified autoregressive diffusion model that jointly generates structure and node features for 3D scene graphs, producing high-level concepts like rooms and floors for robotic perception and SLAM. It removes the need for separate models or hand-crafted rules per concept class.

entry.title: Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Regularized SVGD

author.name: Sayan Banerjee, Dohyeon Kim

entry.summary: The authors prove quantitative target convergence and uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for Langevin-regularized Stein variational gradient descent, showing Stein and Langevin components dissipate relative entropy in complementary geometries. Under log-Sobolev conditions this yields exponential last-iterate convergence.

entry.title: Spectral-Embedded Operator Learning for Three-Phase Interfacial Flow: A Ternary Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes Benchmark

author.name: Muhammad Abid, Arth Sojitra, Omer San

entry.summary: Introduces a three-phase interfacial-flow benchmark (air bubble rising through water into an oil layer) built with a structure-preserving ternary Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes solver, to test whether neural operator-learning surrogates validated on single-interface problems transfer to multiphase flows. Includes 1,024 Sobol-sampled simulations for evaluation.

entry.title: FiLM-GPNet: Geometry-Aware Pseudo-Supervised Phase Restoration with Zero-Shot Generalization for Large Temporal InSAR Stacks

author.name: Getnet Demil, Muhammad Farhan Humayun, Tomi Westerlund, Jukka Heikkonen, Mourad Oussalah

entry.summary: Proposes FiLM-GPNet, a geometry-conditioned network for wrapped-phase restoration in large temporal InSAR stacks, using FiLM modulation with a 7D geometry descriptor, pseudo-supervision from Goldstein-filtered interferograms, interferometric physics regularization, and per-pixel uncertainty estimation, with zero-shot generalization across Capella Spotlight stacks.

entry.title: Neural ODE enhanced linear mixed effect models for estimating complex association patterns of time-varying covariates with the marker trajectory

author.name: Zhe Aurore Li, Quentin Clairon, C\'ecilia Samieri, Rodolphe Thi\'ebaut, M\'elanie Prague, C\'ecile Proust-Lima

entry.summary: Proposes Neural ODE-LMM, embedding a neural ODE inside linear mixed-effects models to learn time-varying covariate-outcome associations from irregular longitudinal data without pre-specifying functional forms. Aimed at epidemiology and clinical cohort analysis with uncertainty-preserving inference.

entry.title: EDGE: Engine for Deterministic Graph Evaluation through Conversation Simulation from Graph Structured DSL Configuration

author.name: Ram Kulathumani, Regunathan Radhakrishnan, Anupam Tripathi, Xiangbo Mao, Roshanak Omrani, Keshav Somani, Shwet Kamal Mishra, Shayna Lurya

entry.summary: Introduces EDGE, a formal evaluation methodology for multi-agent LLM workflows using a DSL-based planner (AgentGraph) whose directed graph is exhaustively traversed to enumerate conversational paths, enabling deterministic replay and behavioral-consistency checks. Addresses growing demand for reproducible agent evaluation.

entry.title: No Detectable Change in Side-Level WER from Prompt-Level Context: A Preregistered Ablation on a Production Oral-History Corpus

author.name: Theodore O. Cochran, Stephanie Dodson, Keith Nore

entry.summary: A preregistered, hash-frozen within-item paired ablation on a production oral-history transcription corpus finds prompt-level context does not detectably change side-level WER, contradicting earlier large gains on smaller models. A model example of rigorous, negative-result reporting in applied NLP.

entry.title: Quantifying Error Tolerance in Synthetic Data: An Atomic-level Operand vs. Operator Perturbation Study

author.name: Jiaxiang Liu, Chenhao Yuan, Shuwen Xu, Boxuan Xing, Xiusheng Huang, Yinhao Xu, Hao Liu, Wenhao Teng, Xiangwen Liao, Pengfei Cao, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces ATOM, a framework decomposing synthetic data into functional units that distinguishes benign operand perturbations from fatal operator perturbations, enabling quantitative error-tolerance analysis for synthetic data filtering. Addresses the gap between overly aggressive and overly permissive filtering strategies.

entry.title: When Patients Cut In: Extending Clinical Conversational AI Safety to Interruptions

author.name: Zachary Ellis, Spencer Hazel, Adam Brandt, Yajie Vera He, Ernest Lim, Jared Joselowitz

entry.summary: Evaluates interruption recovery in deployed clinical voice agents, adapting conversation-analytic overlap categories into three operational types and showing cascaded architectures lose clinically required content when patients interrupt. Fills a gap since clinical conversational-AI benchmarks assume patients wait their turn.

entry.title: All You Need Is Non-Commutative Words

author.name: Carla M. Quispe Flores, Stanley Salvatierra, Renan Cabrera

entry.summary: Introduces VoiceCodeBench, 300 human-recorded workplace segments with 1,482 audited structured-token targets across 26 entity types, evaluating exact recovery of identifiers, paths, and quantities in English ASR under a raw-audio-only protocol. Exposes that fluent low-WER transcripts can still corrupt values downstream systems must parse.

entry.title: MUDDLE: Measuring Understanding of Documents under Distractor and Length Effects

author.name: Jason Luo, Saibilila Abudukelimu, Judy Song, Andrew Feng, Shivank Garg, Vasu Sharma, Kevin Zhu

entry.summary: Presents MUDDLE, a controlled benchmark of 270 human-annotated questions instantiated in five conditions separating distractor similarity from context length in document QA, disentangling two effects prior work conflates.

entry.title: LLM Judges as Raters: A Pre-Registered Audit of Severity, Halo, Reliability, and Version Instability in LLM Essay Scoring on Public Corpora

author.name: Veerendra Kumar Sunkavalli

entry.summary: Treats LLM judges as raters, running a pre-registered many-facet Rasch audit of severity, halo, reliability, and version instability across 2,377 essays and 12 judges from 4 providers. Finds judge severity spans 219 points on ENEM's 0-1000 scale and version drift comparable to between-trainer differences.

entry.title: Which one is banana man? Evaluating vision-language models in multi-turn pragmatic interpretation

author.name: Alvin Wei Ming Tan, Ben Prystawski, Veronica Boyce

entry.summary: Tests humans and vision-language models on interpreting referring expressions from iterated reference games, varying context amount, order, and relevance. Humans perform consistently while models can use prior context to interpret expressions but struggle to build up the relevant context themselves.

entry.title: SUP-MIMIC: A Multi-Task Clinical Diagnosis Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs' Robustness to Contradictory Evidence

author.name: Yi Yu, Bo Wang, Chong Feng, Ge Shi, Xia Liu, Ziyi Yang, Xuewen Shi

entry.summary: Proposes SUP-MIMIC, a multi-task benchmark on MIMIC-IV testing LLM diagnostic reasoning under ambiguity (same presentation, different etiologies) and convergence (heterogeneous symptoms, same disease), including robustness to contradictory evidence.

entry.title: Agent Zero Memory: Provenance-Aware Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: Ming Wu, Pengyuan Zhu

entry.summary: Presents Agent Zero Memory, a provenance-aware long-term memory system distilling conversations, files, and sources into three parallel structures: an episodic events timeline, an entity-event knowledge graph, and a citation-locked hierarchical documentary memory.

entry.title: JPO: Juris Policy Optimization for Structured Legal Reasoning in Criminal Judgment Prediction

author.name: Zhaolu Kang, Yantao Liu, Tailong Luo, Leqi Zheng, Lei Wei, Chenghua Zhu, Junhao Gong, Jiachen Qian, Eric Hanchen Jiang, Jiaxin Liu, Yuan Wang, Hao Zhang, Zixia Wang, Rong Fu, Zheng Lin, Richeng Xuan, Zhichao Hu

entry.summary: Proposes Juris Policy Optimization (JPO), a post-training framework for Chinese criminal judgment prediction that supervises the structured reasoning chain (facts-to-statutes, statutes-to-charges, charges-to-sentencing) rather than final labels or LLM-generated rubrics.

entry.title: Language Proficiency Assessment from Eye Movements in Naturalistic Passage Reading

author.name: Shachar Frenkel, Ido Falah, Omer Shubi, Yevgeni Berzak

entry.summary: Validates and extends predicting language proficiency from eye movements during naturalistic passage reading, moving beyond single-sentence setups to new proficiency measures, models, and information-seeking reading. The approach works across all evaluated conditions, and the authors examine scoring biases.

entry.title: Annotated Surrogate Retrieval for Polish Statutory Law

author.name: Orkun Yi\u{g}it Cengiz

entry.summary: Presents a family of retrieval methods for Polish statutory law based on document surrogates (LM annotations attached at index time), spanning a cost-quality frontier from a surrogate cascade with reranking to a model-free fusion design. Evaluated against 14 baselines on Polish bar exam questions.

entry.title: Type-Balanced Contextual Learning for Incremental Named Entity Recognition

author.name: Duzhen Zhang, Yahan Yu, Xiuyi Chen, Chenxing Li, Dong Yu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a biased context problem in pseudo-labeling-based incremental named entity recognition, where contexts of old entity types shift toward new types in new sentences. It proposes type-balanced contextual learning to counteract this alongside catastrophic forgetting. The work adds a distinct failure mode to the continual-learning-for-NER literature.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Linguistic Steganography: Methods, Countermeasures, Evaluation, and Challenges

author.name: Ruiyi Yan, Chenhui Chu, Zhongliang Yang, Yugo Murawaki

entry.summary: This comprehensive survey covers linguistic steganography along four axes: 148 methods, 60 steganalysis countermeasures, 23 evaluation metrics, and 9 open challenges, identifying five paradigm shifts in the LLM era. These include moves from covertext modification to prompt-only generation and from heuristic to provable security. It is the first systematic account of LLM-era steganography.

entry.title: GeoAgent: Evaluating VLM Geolocalization Through Embodied Navigation

author.name: Arka Mukherjee, Soham Roy, Kartikeya Trivedi, Shreya Ghosh

entry.summary: GeoAgent is an agentic benchmark requiring VLMs to navigate Street View environments and gather observations through embodied navigation before submitting geolocalization predictions, arguing static image-based evaluation misrepresents the task. It is relevant to disaster response, OSINT verification, and location privacy. The setup reveals how sequential observation changes geolocalization behavior.

entry.title: Call Neighbours Yourself: Graph Walks with Destination-Conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yilun Liu, Boyu Luo, Yanran Tang, Ruihong Qiu, Zi Huang

entry.summary: CNY enables LLMs to proactively explore graph neighbourhoods during reasoning over text-attributed graphs via topology-constrained graph-walk actions, rather than reasoning over a pre-selected static neighbour set. It exposes lightweight neighbour previews and learns when to expand candidate context. This makes neighbour selection part of the reasoning process itself.

entry.title: Do LLMs Change Their Minds Like Humans? Diagnosing Human--LLM Divergence in Single-Turn Persuasion Judgments

author.name: Lin Chen, Yitong Chen, Yong Li

entry.summary: Using a naturally occurring persuasion corpus where original posters verified whether replies changed their views, this study diagnoses human-LLM divergence in single-turn persuasion judgments. LLMs show only slight agreement with humans (Cohen's kappa 0.079-0.178), agreeing on strong cues but diverging on finer ones: humans respond to novelty and assertiveness, LLMs to topical similarity and surface form. The result questions LLMs as stand-ins for human belief updating in social simulations.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient Training-Free Acceleration of Diffusion Transformers with BaryCache

author.name: Chengjie Lu, Tianchi Deng, Zhengqi He, Zhijian Gao, Huisi Wu, Xueliang Li

entry.summary: BaryCache accelerates diffusion transformers via training-free stepwise forecasting with a barycentric extrapolator, reducing redundant computation while unlike prior cache methods avoiding VRAM growth. Improves both image and video generation efficiency. Practical efficiency contribution to a widely used model family.

entry.title: Instruction Distillation: Text Instructions as Visual Examples

author.name: Hardik Jindal, Soumyabrata Pal, Sayak Ray Chowdhury

entry.summary: Proposes Instruction Distillation, where an MLLM offline generates a structured per-image identification instruction encoding distinguishing features and confusion points, replacing expensive visual in-context examples with cheaper text for large-K fine-grained classification. A practical token-efficiency idea for MLLM inference.

entry.title: FairReL: Deepfake Detection using Fairness-Aware Representation Learning

author.name: Xiaoman Lu, Jiaqi Li, Shuntian Zheng, Huiping Chen, Yu Guan

entry.summary: FairReL addresses demographic bias in deepfake detection by identifying subgroup-sensitive feature components (multi-scale spatial and fine-tuning residual features) and applying targeted rather than whole-representation fairness regularization. Important fairness dimension for a high-stakes detection task.

entry.title: GramLoop: Training-Free Gram-Gated Replay for Robust Dense Prediction

author.name: Yang Chen, Canyu Shen, Xinzhe Rao, Yuanyi Yan, Yunlu Chen, Meng Tang, Teng Long, Vincent Tao Hu

entry.summary: GramLoop improves frozen DINOv3 dense-prediction models under distribution shift by adding training-free inference-time computation inside the backbone, replaying short transformer windows gated by cosine-Gram consistency to refine features without disrupting spatial relations. Elegant weight-free robustness mechanism for foundation-model backbones.

entry.title: SGRNet: Spatially Guided Radiology Network for Structured Radiological Reporting of Head and Neck Cancer

author.name: Ayush Gupta, Vinkle Srivastav, Prateek Upadhya, Amit Gupta, Krithika Rangarajan, Nicolas Padoy

entry.summary: SGRNet reformulates head-and-neck cancer radiology report generation as anatomically grounded, structured multi-label prediction over a hierarchical clinical schema, using organ segmentations and weakly supervised spatial priors to reduce hallucination and handle missing PET imaging. A hallucination-risk-reducing approach to clinical report generation.

entry.title: OPUS-V2: Bridging the Gap between Sparse Points and Dense Voxels

author.name: Jiabao Wang, Qiang Meng, Liujiang Yan, Ke Wang, Qibin Hou, Ming-Ming Cheng

entry.summary: OPUS-V2 improves point-based occupancy prediction for self-driving by adding a lightweight point-voxel transformation module that adaptively maps sparse predictions into dense voxel space. This removes hand-crafted heuristics that previously bridged sparse points and dense occupancy. Relevant to efficient 3D perception in autonomous driving stacks.

entry.title: Ground-to-Satellite Localization in Unconstrained Image Collections for 3D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Angel Daruna, Ben Southall, Niluthpol Chowdhury Mithun, Kshitij Minhas, Nicholas Meegan, Qiao Wang, Bogdan Matei, Supun Samarasekera, Rakesh Kumar

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical cross-view localization framework that grounds ground-level images against satellite imagery using geometric constraints from SfM models, with coarse-to-fine pose hypotheses and KDE aggregation. This enables metrically accurate 3D reconstruction from unconstrained image collections without panoramas or known initial poses. Likely industrial lab work (SRI given author roster).

entry.title: 3D-MRL: Nested Multimodal 3D Representations via Matryoshka Representation Learning

author.name: M\'arcus Lobo, Vitor Matias, Jeov\'a Farias, Moacir Ponti

entry.summary: 3D-MRL applies Matryoshka Representation Learning to multimodal 3D pre-training, aligning point clouds with frozen CLIP image and text embeddings under contrastive supervision across multiple embedding dimensions. A single model then serves different computational budgets instead of requiring separate fixed-dimensional models. Practical for deploying 3D vision-language models across resource tiers.

entry.title: The Nearest Target Is the Wrong One: Target Separation in Arc2Face Identity Unlearning

author.name: Zeynel Tok

entry.summary: Shows that unlearning an identity from face-conditioned generators like Arc2Face can silently fail when the redirection target is the nearest neighbor in recognition space, auditing target-selection policies under a hard-neighbour stress test. Relevant to machine unlearning safety.

entry.title: NoisEasier: Test-Time Noise Optimization for Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Yujiang Pu, Yu Kong

entry.summary: NoisEasier is a test-time scaling framework for text-to-video generation that optimizes input noise via differentiable multi-objective rewards without modifying the base model. Avoids reward hacking and poor adaptation issues of reward-based fine-tuning.

entry.title: Centering before Pruning: Lightweight Geometry Correction for Diversity-Based Visual Token Pruning in LVLMs

author.name: Shunjie Wen, Jaeyeon Lee, Dong-Wan Choi

entry.summary: Analyzes geometry of diversity-based visual token pruning in LVLMs, showing centering features before cosine similarity reveals richer pairwise structure yet alone degrades pruning, and derives a lightweight correction. Reduces inference cost of vision-language models.

entry.title: Proximity3D: Shape from Capacitive Proximity on Sensing Manifold

author.name: Hao Chen, Chenming Wu, Chun Ping Lam, Xiangjia Chen, Guoxin Fang, Charlie C. L. Wang, Yeung Yam, Juncong Lin, Chengkai Dai

entry.summary: Proximity3D treats a curved capacitive textile as a non-planar sensing manifold, recovering object shape from capacitive proximity fields with a multi-view feedforward model. Opens a new sensing modality route for robotic near-field perception.

entry.title: SePArate: Segmenting Patterns from Defects in Wafer Manufacturing Using Weak Supervision

author.name: Dain Kwon, Changmin Shin, Sunjong Park, Kanghyun Choi, Hyeyoon Lee, Jaewon Jang, Minseok Choi, Jinho Lee

entry.summary: ATGS organizes Gaussian primitives around time-conditioned anchors with temporal windowing for long volumetric video, stabilizing long-term complex motion tracking. Targets temporal instability and artifacts in free-viewpoint video.

entry.title: SeqAlign3DVG: A Sequence-Aligned Benchmark and Voxel Reasoning Framework for 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Yi Zhang, Yi Wang, Yueting Wu, Kaiyue Yang, Yuejiao Su, Lap-Pui Chau

entry.summary: SeqAlign3DVG introduces a temporally ordered, strictly observation-aligned benchmark for image-based 3D visual grounding with ~24K human-verified samples, plus a unified voxel-based reasoning pipeline. Fixes loose text-observation alignment in prior 3D grounding benchmarks.

entry.title: VisLens: Single-Pass Interpretable Visual Search for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Jingyi He, Sanghwan Kim, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: VisLens performs single-pass fine-grained visual search in high-resolution images using the logit lens to decode hidden-state semantics, avoiding the multi-query cost of training-free methods and the opacity of RL tool-use models. Includes a lightweight tuned component.

entry.title: CORAL: A Benchmark for Structure-aware and Brain-wide Neuron Reconstruction in Light Microscopy

author.name: Zekang Yang, Jiamin Li, Zhenghua Li, Jiaqi Fan, Zengcai Guo, Xiaolin Hu

entry.summary: CORAL is the first benchmark for structure-aware, brain-wide neuron reconstruction from light microscopy, with two tasks spanning block-level and whole-brain scales on curated fMOST annotations. Tests whether local-reconstruction progress translates to whole-brain scalability.

entry.title: RealOOB: A Definition-Consistent Real-World Oriented Occlusion Boundary Benchmark

author.name: Lintao Xu, Yinghao Wang, Chenchu Rong, Xuchong Qiu, Chaohui Wang

entry.summary: RealOOB provides a definition-consistent, real-world oriented occlusion boundary benchmark with self-occlusion annotations and coverage beyond prior fragmented supervision, benchmarking modern edge detectors and depth estimators against definition-consistent OBs.

entry.title: Lucida: Parse, Generate, and Place for Composable Real-to-Sim Scene Modeling

author.name: Minghan Qin, Yuang Wang, Xiuyu Yang, Yushi Long, Yujian Zhang, Ruihuan Wang, Kai Ye, Yangang Zhang, Hang Li

entry.summary: Lucida addresses composable real-to-sim scene modeling (parse, generate, place) by redistributing precision requirements so each step consumes only what cluttered real captures reliably provide, yielding simulation-ready editable object assets for robotics.

entry.title: Vision Models Predict Urban Scene Appraisal with Limited Neural Alignment

author.name: Kaizhen Tan, Yuantao Deng

entry.summary: Using EEG from 63 adults viewing Berlin street scenes, this study separates predictive accuracy from neural alignment, testing seventeen feature spaces against representational geometry of urban scene appraisal. It shows high behavioral prediction from vision embeddings does not imply human-like scene organization.

entry.title: LISynSeg: Data-Centric Label-to-Image Synthesis for Cross-Modality Whole-Heart Segmentation

author.name: Jiacheng Wang, Ivana Isgum, Ipek Oguz

entry.summary: LISynSeg is a data-centric approach for cross-modality whole-heart segmentation that augments nnU-Net training with label-to-image synthesis, calibrating contrast and acquisition perturbations to the training cohort while holding architecture fixed. It addresses annotation heterogeneity and acquisition shifts in CT and MRI.

entry.title: MedTVL: Harnessing Vision and Language for Medical Time Series Classification

author.name: Jiexia Ye, Jia Li, Fugee Tsung

entry.summary: MedTVL is a text-guided dual-pathway architecture for medical time series classification that synergizes a convolutional temporal pathway on raw sequences with a transformer-based visual pathway, motivated by tri-modal clinical diagnosis. It extends beyond the typical bi-modal (time series plus text) setups.

entry.title: Evaluating the Effects of Inter-Observer and Model Variability on Radiological Peritoneal Cancer Index Assessment

author.name: Savvas Saragiotis, Pieter C. Gort, Lotte J. S. Fleurkens-Ewals, Anna F. van Herwijnen, Marion Tops-Welten, L. D. Kampmeijer, Joost Nederend, Fons van der Sommen

entry.summary: This study examines the metric-to-decision gap in radiological Peritoneal Cancer Index assessment, benchmarking an nnU-Net segmentation model against four experts and relating Dice/HD95/ASD improvements to clinically meaningful decision changes at the PCI 20 threshold. It quantifies inter-observer variability against model performance.

entry.title: Medical Foundation Model Features as Perceptual Loss for Brain MRI Contrast Dose Simulation

author.name: Changsheng Fang, Dayang Wang, T. Campbell Arnold, Enhao Gong, Srivathsa Pasumarthi

entry.summary: This paper tests whether features from medical foundation models (RadImageNet, SegVol, BrainIAC) outperform VGG16/ResNet50 as perceptual losses for brain MRI contrast dose simulation, evaluated across four public benchmarks. It addresses the domain mismatch of natural-image perceptual losses in medical synthesis.

entry.title: SpatialTrust: A Benchmark for Environmental Risk Recognition in Secure Authentication

author.name: Junbin Lu, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Saesha Wadhwa, Yu Ting Hsu, Jenq-Neng Hwang

entry.summary: SpatialTrust is a question-answering benchmark evaluating whether multimodal LLMs can recognize, localize, and explain environmental risks relevant to secure authentication, across five complementary abilities including indirect factor identification and explanation. It probes a security-relevant blind spot of current models.

entry.title: GarmentWeaver: Schema-Aware Structured Synthesis for Multimodal Sewing Patterns

author.name: Yinwen Lu, Weihao Luo, Yueqi Zhong

entry.summary: GarmentWeaver generates executable sewing patterns from sketches and text via a schema-aware framework that activates garment-relevant structural branches and predicts hierarchical targets, avoiding entangled flat sequence representations. It targets simulation-compatible digital garment creation.

entry.title: GAFT: Geo-Anchored Fine-Tuning for Hazard Identification from Rare Failures

author.name: Yanran Xu, Chuanhang Qiu, Yue Wang, Wenbo Wu, Zhaoxing Li

entry.summary: GAFT adapts vision foundation models with parameter-efficient LoRA tuning guided by geometry-derived priors to identify rare off-road navigation hazards (high-centering, entrapment) from limited outcome-labeled data. Geometry-anchored spatial attention alignment prevents exploitation of scenario-specific cues.

entry.title: Cognitively-Grounded On-Device Runtime Learning for Ground Robots in Unknown Physical Environments

author.name: Yihao Cai, Yanbing Mao, Christian Lebiere

entry.summary: CogRun enables safety-critical ground robots to perform cognitively-grounded runtime learning on edge devices in unknown environments, blending actor-critic reinforcement learning with instance-based learning under a rational safety agent and coordinator. It targets map-free deployment with safety guarantees.

entry.title: Coding What Matters: A Semantic-Aware Memory Interface for Energy-Efficient Perception in Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Haohua Que, Handong Yao

entry.summary: MotiMem-Omega is a semantic-aware memory-interface coder for autonomous vehicles that reduces sensor-to-memory energy cost by protecting traffic participants at high fidelity while degrading sky and background, guided by cross-dataset bit-sensitivity sweeps with safety floors for vulnerable road users. It ties memory hardware costs to perception semantics.

entry.title: A Cognitive Architecture for Shared Autonomy in AUV Operations

author.name: Niamh Ellis, Thi Tran, Ignacio Carlucho, Yvan R. Petillot

entry.summary: This paper presents a cognitive architecture combining a domain ontology with multiple role-specialized LLMs to support shared autonomy in AUV/ROV operations, grounding LLM decisions in domain knowledge across mission stages to reduce operator workload and raise situational awareness. It targets safety-critical underwater operations.

entry.title: Bridging Semantics and Physics with Constrained LLMs for Safe and Trustworthy Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Wenhao Hong, Lan Wei, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: This work bridges the language-action gap in LLM-driven kitchen manipulation by formalizing a typed contract: RGB-D observations ground a collision-aware scene model, and language decisions are constrained through schema-validated MCP tool calls rejecting physically infeasible plans. It targets safe execution under imperfect perception.

entry.title: Task-Relevant Feature-Dynamics Fidelity Enables Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer for Robotic Ultrasound Scanning

author.name: Yizhao Qian, Jiayuan Luo, Wanyi Zhu, Yameng Zhang, Max Q. -H. Meng, Yixuan Yuan, Li Liu

entry.summary: Introduces task-relevant feature-dynamics fidelity (TR-FDF), a theory and training framework for zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of robotic ultrasound scanning policies, showing that matching how task-relevant features change under probe motion matters more than single-frame realism. A contraction analysis quantifies how motion-dependent simulation mismatch reduces closed-loop stability margins.

entry.title: LARC: Lazy Adaptive Reachability Certification of Robot Manipulator Trajectories

author.name: Yu Feng, Hao Wu, Yuzhe Wang, Jianshu Zhou

entry.summary: LARC certifies robot manipulator trajectories against obstacles by lazily bisecting only intervals with inconclusive clearance tests, bounding link occupancy with midpoint capsules inflated by exact speed maxima. Evaluated on real AgileX PIPER trajectories, it provides continuous-time collision certification more efficiently than uniform partitioning.

entry.title: CanonNav: Disentangling Navigation Behavior from Camera Geometry in Cross-Platform Visual Navigation

author.name: Dong-Wook Kim, Ji-Hoon Hwang, E-In Son, Mintaek Oh, Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: CanonNav disentangles navigation behavior from platform-dependent camera geometry in cross-platform visual navigation, addressing the ill-posedness of implicitly inferring camera geometry from images and making intermediate decisions explicit beyond demonstrated trajectories.

entry.title: Generalizable Multi-Agent Planning from Signal Temporal Logic Specifications via Diffusion

author.name: Joe Eappen, Zikang Xiong, Shreyash S. Iyengar, Suresh Jagannathan

entry.summary: A diffusion-based planner for multi-agent systems that generalizes to unseen signal temporal logic specifications at deployment, addressing the scalability limits of optimization-based STL methods and the specification-overfitting of learning-based ones, including per-agent heterogeneous specifications.

entry.title: Provably Safe Decentralized Contingency MPC under State-Only Information and Limited Sensing for Nonlinear Multi-agent Systems

author.name: Max Studt, Georg Schildbach

entry.summary: Provides provably safe decentralized contingency MPC for nonlinear multi-agent systems under state-only information and limited sensing, with agent-wise fallback safe sets and a novel update mechanism reducing conservatism in local interaction handling while preserving recursive feasibility and convergence.

entry.title: The separation principle: where do beliefs and desires come from?

author.name: Fernando Rosas

entry.summary: Argues that the belief-desire picture of agency can be derived from classic optimal control and reinforcement learning theorems, suggesting beliefs and desires are properties of optimal policies rather than folk-psychological assumptions, with implications across psychology, economics, and AI.

entry.title: Implicit-bias-like patterns in reasoning models

author.name: Calvin K. Lai

entry.summary: A Nature Machine Intelligence paper by Lee and Lai showing that most large reasoning models process stereotypical information with less computational effort than counter-stereotypical information, an implicit-bias-like processing asymmetry. This provides a measurable, compute-based signature of bias in reasoning models.

entry.title: SpikeOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Autoregressive Spiking Language Models

author.name: Enqiao Lu, Xingrui Yu, Yiwei Fu, Zhenglin Wan, Pengfei Zhou, Wangbo Zhao, Muqing Jian, Xueyi Zhang, Yang You, Ivor Tsang

entry.summary: Identifies prefix-source mismatch when distilling autoregressive spiking language models from pretrained ANN teachers on fixed corpus prefixes, and adapts on-policy distillation to the spiking setting to stabilize teacher-student output alignment and internal spiking dynamics. Advances energy-efficient language modeling through ANN-to-SNN migration. An interesting niche with real potential for efficient inference.

entry.title: See, Hypothesize, Validate: Multimodal Agentic Framework for Discovering Governing PDEs

author.name: Sarang Manoj Pekhale, Amartya Roy, Rajat Sarkar, Souvik Chakraborty

entry.summary: Organizes PDE discovery as a confidence-governed hypothesis validation loop across four role-specialized agents for observation, visualization, hypothesis, and validation, aiming to overcome library constraints, noise sensitivity, and hallucination in prior sparse, symbolic, and LLM approaches. Well-designed, but it overlaps substantially with HER-PDE in this same batch, indicating a rapidly crowding subfield. Not unique, though carefully constructed.

entry.title: SABER: Stability-Aware Early Exit for LLM Reasoning via Adversarial Branch Probing

author.name: Wanli Cheng, Haiya Xiang, Juntao Li, Hongling Wang, Wenliang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SABER, a training-free early-exit method for large reasoning models that probes the stability of intermediate answers via simple adversarial semantic perturbations, avoiding both confidence-based miscalibration and costly multi-trajectory consistency checks. Targets the substantial waste of continuing to reason after answers stabilize. A practical efficiency technique with moderate novelty.

entry.title: LoopArena: Benchmarking Models as Runtime Controllers for Loop Engineering

author.name: Yi Wang, Haopeng Zhang, Chengxiang Huang, Rui Dai, Kaikui Liu, Piotr Koniusz, Xiangxiang Chu

entry.summary: Introduces LoopArena, a benchmark evaluating how well one model can act as a runtime controller guiding a separate coding agent through long-running tasks, disentangling loop-guidance quality from executor capability since a single end-to-end outcome confounds the two. Conceptualizes and measures the emerging practice of loop engineering around coding agents. Timely and distinct evaluation angle.

entry.title: Beat-Synchronous Tokenization for ECG Transformers

author.name: Ahmed Sameh, Nolan Wilson, Max Enderlein, Yogatheesan Varatharajah

entry.summary: Studies beat-synchronous tokenization for ECG transformers, comparing fixed temporal patches against three heartbeat-aligned strategies, with experiments on PTB-XL and Icentia11k after different pretraining schemes. Resampled beat tokens achieve the best results, showing that physiological structure in tokenization matters. A clean, actionable finding for medical signal modeling.

entry.title: PAC: Progress-Augmented Advantage Curriculum for Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning of LLMs

author.name: Yuanqiang Yu, Yanzhao Zheng, Zhentao Zhang, Tianze Xu, Chao Ma, Jihuai Zhu, Jiashun Liu, Xinle Deng, Baohua Dong, Hangcheng Zhu, Ruohui Huang

entry.summary: Introduces PAC, a progress-augmented advantage curriculum for multi-task RL post-training of LLMs, combining advantage-derived learnability with recent reward gains to allocate rollout budget toward tasks that actually improve reward rather than merely producing large updates. It targets a real inefficiency in RL post-training pipelines. Relevant to the growing practice of multi-task RL for LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Brain-Language-Action (BLA) Models: Language-Conditioned EEG for Robotics Control

author.name: Alexandr Plashchinsky

entry.summary: Brain-Language-Action (BLA) models condition EEG interpretation on language for robotic control, letting a small set of reliably distinguishable brain states map dynamically onto a larger action space via language-defined control mappings. This sidesteps the poor separability of direct EEG-to-action classification.

entry.title: Kathleen Remembers: Length-Invariant One-Shot Recall Without Attention

author.name: George Fountzoulas

entry.summary: Formulates compression-aware abstention as a learning problem for KV-cache-compressed LLMs: a small LoRA adapter trained on compressor survival masks learns to answer when answer-bearing evidence survives eviction and abstain when it is removed. First work to treat KV-compression-induced evidence loss behaviorally.

entry.title: Arabic Safety Alignment as Selective Refusal: An Empirical Study of SFT, DPO, and Guard Calibration

author.name: Mohamad Zbib, Ammar Mohanna

entry.summary: Empirically studies Arabic safety alignment using separate benign-refusal and harmful-refusal metrics across five models and 130 runs on the AraSafe set. Shows refusal-only SFT collapses toward blanket refusal while selected mixed-SFT configurations reach H=90-93% at B=14-23%, with DPO and guards behaving inconsistently across models.

entry.title: CoCoA: Context-Conditional Cultural Alignment for Large Language Models

author.name: Kyungdon Lee, Wei Xu, Alan Ritter, Dong-Ho Lee, JinYeong Bak

entry.summary: Introduces VocalAffectBench, a test-only benchmark of 273 human-recorded English clips across seven emotion labels for evaluating vocal emotion recognition from raw audio. Baseline performance is weak, with the best model (Gemini 3.5 Flash variant) at 46.5% versus 14.3% chance.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Boundaries: Rethinking Scene Segmentation for Movie RAG

author.name: Dong-Hee Kim, Seonwoo Choi, Changbeen Kim, Jungmyung Wi, Juyeon Ko, Youngju Choi, Il Hyeon Mun, Hyunwoo J. Kim, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: Investigates scene segmentation as the retrieval-unit choice for movie RAG, showing that retrieval quality for story-level reasoning over hours of content critically depends on semantically coherent segmentation rather than default shot- or time-based units. Important systems insight for long-video understanding.

entry.title: ClearText-Video: A Large-Scale Text-Centric Video Dataset Bridging Video Restoration and Scene-Text Enhancement

author.name: Jinlong Li, Jiaming Ding, Dingfu Lu, Malcolm Hsiu, Chuang Ke, Kangning Yang, Bochen Guan, Lan Fu, Jie Cai, Huiming Sun, Zibo Meng

entry.summary: ClearText-Video is a large-scale scene-text-aware benchmark of 4,639 real-world egocentric videos under controlled quality variation, studying whether MLLMs can robustly read and reason over real-world text amid blur, noise, and compression. Bridges video restoration and scene-text understanding. Timely given MLLM sensitivity to input quality.

entry.title: RoSe-SLAM: Robust Semantic-Aware Gaussian Splatting SLAM from Dynamic Monocular Videos

author.name: Wenting Wang, Jiaxin Guo, Wenzhen Dong, Yun-Hui Liu, Charlie C. L. Wang, Yeung Yam

entry.summary: RoSe-SLAM achieves robust semantic-aware Gaussian splatting SLAM from uncalibrated monocular video in dynamic environments, distilling 2D foundation-model semantic features into Gaussian fields to identify dynamic distractors for tracking and mapping. Strong integration of foundation models into dynamic SLAM.

entry.title: Background-Free Objectness Learning for Class-Agnostic Detection

author.name: Dania Batool, Liliana Lo Presti, Marco La Cascia, Filippo Vella

entry.summary: B-FOR learns class-agnostic objectness without explicit background supervision on unlabeled regions, addressing the objectness bias that arises when incomplete annotations treat unlabeled objects as negatives. It predicts dense multi-scale object-center and scale fields from which hypotheses are derived. Useful for open-world detection under partial annotation.

entry.title: Credo: Reusable Declarative Primitives for Agentic Workflows

author.name: Duo Lu, Andrew Crotty, U\u{g}ur \c{C}etintemel

entry.summary: Observes that harnesses discovered by coding-agent search are opaque imperative programs whose logical steps, runtime signals, execution decisions, and prompt strategies remain implicit and task-specific, and proposes Credo, reusable declarative primitives that make that harness knowledge explicit and recomposable across tasks. Tackles harness reuse, an increasingly important systems problem for agents. An interesting systems-abstraction contribution.

entry.title: KLOD: Locality-Preserving Knowledge Editing via Non-Target Distribution Preservation

author.name: Hojun Jeong, Gyunyeop Kim, Sangwoo Kang

entry.summary: Identifies that cross-entropy knowledge editing amplifies the target without constraining non-target redistribution, causing cumulative distribution drift and locality degradation across sequential edits, and proposes KLOD, a bounded distribution-preserving objective that halts target amplification at a threshold while preserving non-target and prefix-position distributions. A principled fix for a known editing pathology. Incremental but useful.

entry.title: When Evidence Shapes Collaboration: Knowledge-Conditioned Topology Generation for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yangxiao Jiang, Jiarun Fan, Mingcong Xu, Yanxi Guo, Jiwen Feng, Shanqing Xu, Mengchen Qian, Wei Chen, Xiaojin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes K-GAT, a neuro-symbolic framework that formulates multi-agent collaboration topology design as knowledge-conditioned structure learning, integrating external retrieved evidence directly into topology generation rather than using retrieval reactively, to fix structure-knowledge misalignment in knowledge-intensive tasks. An interesting direction in the active topology-generation area. Moderately novel.

entry.title: String: An Agentic OS Where Every App Is a Markdown File

author.name: Jookyung Song, Nojun Kwak, Simyung Chang

entry.summary: Proposes String, an open-source runtime treating agent-facing software as an operating-systems problem in which each application is a single Markdown document declaring views, typed actions, navigation, and credentials, moving tool knowledge out of the agent context into a common layer rendered one view at a time. A provocative interface redesign aimed at token efficiency and agent-native UX. Interesting design vision with an open release.

entry.title: WeAgent-MMSearch: Native Text-Vision Interaction for Multimodal Search Agents

author.name: Zongkai Liu, Hui Zhang, Liqiang Niu, Zhen Cao, Han Li, Juntao Liu, Wenchao Chen, Chengduo Zhao, Chao Yu, Fandong Meng

entry.summary: Introduces a multimodal agentic harness for search that keeps retrieved images as persistent, inspectable context alongside text rather than collapsing trajectories to text-only reasoning, plus runtime recovery that salvages trajectories from tool-call, timeout, and budget failures during long-horizon search. Practical harness improvements from a Meituan-affiliated team. Useful for the emerging multimodal search-agent area.

entry.title: Learning PDE Time-Stepping with Neural Cellular Automata

author.name: Esha Saha, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a Neural Cellular Automata surrogate for PDE time-stepping that learns a small local update rule applied at every grid cell, mirroring the locality of differential operators. Benchmarked against PDE-Net, PINNs, and FNOs on canonical PDEs, it offers a parameter-efficient alternative to one-shot trajectory mapping. The locality-matching inductive bias is an elegant fit for PDE dynamics.

entry.title: Measuring Memory and Generalization as Separable Geometric Channels: The Topo^2 Framework

author.name: Zhanbo Zhang, Ming Liu, Qing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Topo-squared, a framework using persistent homology to causally separate memorization of noisy labels from generalization as distinct geometric channels in representation space. It introduces an FM0 intervention (zero loss on flipped samples from epoch 0) that reaches generalization ceilings while memorizing almost nothing. An ambitious measurement framework with graded-evidence laws.

entry.title: Moving the Mean Toward the Known Good, Not Beyond It: What Inference-Time Interventions and Weight Consolidation Buy in Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Roberto I. Ono Filho

entry.summary: This single-author study examines what self-training on verified successes does to open-ended generation, using generate-verify-select-LoRA-consolidate loops on online bin packing. With a confirmation battery of three replications and a held-out set read once, it finds mean shift toward value improves modestly while best-candidate performance converges to the classic heuristic and no further.

entry.title: MA-RAG: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Query-Driven Summarization of Longitudinal Parkinson's Disease Assessments

author.name: Sana Alamgeera, Denise Goberta, Muhammad Irshad, Anne H. H. Ngu

entry.summary: Proposes MA-RAG, a multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation framework that decomposes clinical reasoning into domain-specialized agents for summarizing single-visit and longitudinal Parkinson's disease assessments. Includes fact extraction and a verification stage for temporal consistency.

entry.title: Whose Assessment of Distress? Community Perspectives and LLM Alignment on Well-Being Posts

author.name: Andrew Aquilina, Xiang Lorraine Li, Yu-Ru Li

entry.summary: Conducts a perspectivist annotation study with 321 participants providing 9,587 judgments on 1,198 Reddit posts across six identity-based communities to test whether LLM distress detection aligns with community-specific norms. Finds in-group raters modestly agree more with their community, challenging single-standard alignment.

entry.title: CARD: Calibration via Agreement in Reverse Diffusion for Out-of-Domain MRI Segmentation

author.name: Jiaheng Dai, Weidong Guo, Qingbiao Li, Jie Xu, Yi Guo, Yuanyuan Wang, Zeju Li

entry.summary: CARD proposes calibration for out-of-domain MRI segmentation via agreement between a categorical diffusion model's generative shape prior and the primary segmentor, providing reliability evidence beyond the corrupted terminal prediction. A principled approach to confident errors under domain shift in medical imaging.

entry.title: Beyond Representation Learning: A Systematic Study of Joint-Embedding Predictive Generation for 3D Brain MRI

author.name: Meng Zhou, Wenhao You, Yuxing Chen, Yueying Tian

entry.summary: Med-D-JEPA systematically adapts denoising JEPA (joint-embedding predictive generation) to 3D brain MRI, combining masked context prediction, latent alignment, per-token diffusion, and next-token-set sampling. First systematic study of generative JEPA in 3D medical imaging. Extends a hot architecture family to a new domain.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Anti-UAV Detection via Evidential Fusion and Conflict-Discounted Belief Aggregation

author.name: Sharanda Suttorp, Seyed Sahand Mohammadi Ziabari, Ali Mohammed Mansour Alsahag

entry.summary: Extends evidential deep learning for thermal-only anti-UAV detection to multimodal RGB-thermal fusion via Discounted Belief Fusion, which converts inter-modal conflict into uncertainty mass before aggregating opinions. This lets the system express doubt when sensor streams disagree under occlusion or modality failure. Bounding boxes are resolved with selective strategies.

entry.title: GSPotential: Camera Potential Field for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zeyuan An, Yanghang Xiao, Zhiying Leng, Yijun Feng, Xiaohui Liang

entry.summary: GSPotential quantifies supervision imbalance across viewing directions in sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting using a Camera Potential Field, identifying supervision valleys where photometric guidance fails. Prior-guided control is then concentrated where it is actually needed. Offers a principled lens on why external-prior regularization is unevenly effective.

entry.title: openJiuwen: Beyond Static Harnesses for Long-Horizon Coding Agents

author.name: openJiuwen Team, Tao Yu, Xinyu Zhang, Qianqian Chen, Xiaoneng Xiang, Chia Kwangyang, Xingchen Huang, Ran Chen, Yangkai Ding, Zheng Wang, Yeo Boon Hong, Bingzheng Gan, Enrui Hu, Shuo Cheng, Deyang Li, Ruifeng Shi, Hongbo Wang, Qi Ye, Xuefeng Jin, Zhangchun Zhao

entry.summary: Presents openJiuwen, an open-source agent harness for long-horizon coding agents that addresses structural composability of heterogeneous capabilities and runtime adaptivity to streaming evidence such as semantic diagnostics, execution outcomes, and context relevance. Systems infrastructure responding to real trends in delegated, multi-agent coding. Valuable if adopted; the contribution is architectural.

entry.title: RECAST: Recent & Context-Aware Sampling for Test-Time Adaptation in Streaming Biosignals

author.name: Yong-Yeon Jo, Junho Song, Joon-myoung Kwon

entry.summary: Proposes RECAST, a lightweight sampling module for buffered test-time adaptation of streaming biosignal models that builds each adaptation batch from recent, context-aligned, and reliable segments rather than all-buffered or latest-only selection, addressing subject drift in long-term monitoring.
