A clean, practical answer to an under-asked question in test-time adaptation. Good niche contribution on real clinical data.

entry.title: Real-Valued Hyperdimensional Sequence Representations with Hadamard Product Binding and Shift Equivariance

author.name: Kenny Schlegel, Dmitri A. Rachkovskij, Denis Kleyko, Amy Loutfi, Stefan Streif, Evgeny Osipov

entry.summary: This paper develops real-valued position encodings for hyperdimensional computing that retain the shift-equivariant properties of Fractional Power Encoding while remaining compatible with Hadamard product binding. The construction is motivated by Random Fourier Features and targets sequence representations. It closes a compatibility gap in the vector symbolic architecture toolbox.

entry.title: AGENT-O: A Semantic Agent Card Framework for Interoperable and Governed Healthcare AI Agents

author.name: Pengze Li, Cui Tao

entry.summary: AGENT-O defines a semantic Agent Card ontology (OWL 2/RDF) for describing healthcare AI agent systems across runtime, governance, provenance, and evaluation dimensions, and supports assessing reporting completeness in publications. It was evaluated with reasoning tests, SHACL validation, competency queries, and a model-assisted assessment of 279 papers. It addresses the growing need for standardized, governable descriptions of clinical agents.

entry.title: Learning to Use Tools: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Integrated Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Minghui Xu, Zi Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies calculator tool-calling for mathematical reasoning on the Countdown task, constructing SFT datasets for tool-use patterns and then applying on-policy RL methods including RLOO, GRPO, and DAPO with verifiable final-answer rewards. It quantifies how calculation errors drive incorrect responses. A solid but incremental study of tool-integrated reasoning.

entry.title: COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing

author.name: Raghul Sugumar, Amrit Gopinath

entry.summary: COVER introduces an evaluation contract for multi-agent coalition routing that fixes the information boundary, downstream stack, and legal team family before outcomes are generated, enabling identifiable comparisons of routing policies. It shows that end-to-end accuracy gaps do not by themselves identify routing effects and derives minimal assumption-free support conditions for policy contrasts. It brings rigorous experimental-design principles to multi-agent evaluation.

entry.title: PACE: Publisher-Adaptive Content Extraction via Agentic Automation

author.name: Zhanlin Liu, Munirathnam Srikanth

entry.summary: PACE is an agentic framework that learns publisher-specific web content extraction configurations from representative pages and user requirements, aiming to combine the accuracy of hand-built parsers with the scalability of general extractors. It targets reliable data pipelines for LLMs at reasonable cost and latency. A pragmatic middle ground in a well-known trade-off.

entry.title: Marginal Coverage Credit Reduces Redundant Exploration in Parallel State-Entropy Optimization

author.name: Junhao Cao, Hongyi Xia, Jianian Wu, Xiaopeng Yi, Lixia Huang, Ping Guo

entry.summary: MCC-PGPSE improves parallel state-entropy exploration by estimating policy-specific marginal coverage credit via leave-one-policy-out analysis and state-owner specialization, redistributing non-negative intrinsic rewards without changing their total. This discourages redundant visitation across independently parameterized policies. A focused refinement of parallel exploration in RL.

entry.title: Destroy Me: Automatic Artifact Generation for Histopathology Images

author.name: Zuzanna Krawczyk-Borysiak, Adam Krawczyk, Mateusz Miller, Gabriela Kaczmarek, S{\l}awomir Paku{\l}o, Ma{\l}gorzata Sok\'o{\l}, \.Zaneta Swiderska-Chadaj

entry.summary: Destroy Me takes the opposite of the usual data-cleaning approach for computational pathology: it synthesizes six realistic artifact types (folds, precipitates, blur, stitching errors, dust) by combining fine-tuned Stable Diffusion with physics-based procedural modeling, then trains models to be robust to imperfect data. This preserves diagnostic context that filtering would discard. Practical robustness improvement for deployed pathology models.

entry.title: Self-Explainable Multi-Label Graph Neural Network for Correlated Evidence Attribution

author.name: Yingqi Feng, Yufei Tang, Min Shi, Xingquan Zhu

entry.summary: SEMGNN is an end-to-end self-explainable multi-label graph neural network that models how evidence is shared or separated across labels during training, including weakly or negatively associated label pairs that post-hoc explainers miss. It integrates correlated evidence attribution directly into the learning objective. A solid architecture-plus-explainability contribution for multi-label graph learning.

entry.title: Antipatterns in AI-assisted Qualitative Data Analysis: A Catalog of Temptations and Pitfalls for Software Engineering Researchers

author.name: Rashina Hoda, Carolyn Seaman, Victoria Gomes, Rodrigo Spinola

entry.summary: This paper catalogs antipatterns in AI-assisted qualitative data analysis for software engineering researchers, identifying assumptions and practices that appear advantageous but compromise analytical rigor as LLM tools accelerate low-quality research production. It offers strategic guidance from decades of qualitative research expertise. A timely, field-level intervention on AI use in research methodology.

entry.title: Optimal Adversarial Testing: Extracting Honest Test Results from Dishonest Test Takers

author.name: Owen Cox, April Xu, Weiyu Xu

entry.summary: Proposes optimal adversarial testing strategies that recover reliable test results even when test takers (including AI-assisted cheaters) corrupt outcomes, via optimally scheduled re-testing of selected groups.

entry.title: ARC-CT: Anatomy-Routed Contrastive Vision-Language Learning for 3D Chest CT

author.name: Huseyin Umut Isik, Mehmet Alp Ozaydin, Sila Kurugol, \c{S}eyda Ertekin

entry.summary: ARC-CT proposes anatomy-routed contrastive vision-language learning for 3D chest CT, using region-aware learning to avoid diluting localized abnormalities and to fix false-negative issues from co-positive scans in standard contrastive objectives.

entry.title: NL2AGBench: Benchmarking LLM Auto-Formalization for AlphaGeometry

author.name: Samuel Xiao, Judy Song, Rory Hu, Ziliang Zong

entry.summary: NL2AGBench benchmarks LLM auto-formalization of natural-language geometry problems into AlphaGeometry's domain-specific language, addressing the usability bottleneck between informal problems and neuro-symbolic theorem provers.

entry.title: Learning-Theoretic Foundation for General Coded Computing: The Straggler Setting

author.name: Parsa Moradi, Behrooz Tahmasebi, Mohammad Ali Maddah-Ali

entry.summary: Rebuilds coded computing for straggler mitigation from a learning-theoretic foundation, handling approximate recovery and unstructured ML workloads (like DNNs) where strict algebraic recovery thresholds of classical schemes do not apply.

entry.title: Continuity-Free Near-Minimax Leading-Order Regret for CVaR-UCBVI

author.name: Yuanlong Chen

entry.summary: Proves that the Bernstein CVaR-UCBVI algorithm achieves near-minimax leading-order regret for tabular CVaR reinforcement learning without continuity assumptions, via a selected-budget self-bound on shortfall conditional variance.

entry.title: Sparse Koopman Autoencoders Identify Local Dynamical Regimes in Multibasin Systems

author.name: Aidan Li, Uday Kiran Reddy Tadipatri, Mahan Fathi, Sarath Chandar, Ross Goroshin

entry.summary: Sparse Koopman Autoencoders use sparsity-inducing latent objectives so that latent supports act as inspectable basin indicators in multibasin dynamical systems, without regime labels, where a single global Koopman embedding provably cannot suffice.

entry.title: PathBridger: Subgoal Bridges for Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Soohyun Choi, Seonvin Cho, Songnam Hong

entry.summary: PathBridger improves offline goal-conditioned RL on long horizons by making intervening state-space paths explicit between selected subgoals, rather than leaving them implicit in endpoint-conditioned low-level policies.

entry.title: MEL: Coordinate-Preserving EEG Tokenization for fMRI Translation

author.name: Xiangyu Liu, Zeting Yan, Zhitong Yin, Boyang Li, Xi Zhang

entry.summary: MEL proposes coordinate-preserving multi-band EEG tokenization that disentangles temporal lag, channel identity, and frequency-band structure to improve EEG-to-fMRI translation, targeting the representation-interface mismatch with hemodynamic signals.

entry.title: Unlearning on Spatio-Temporal Graphs through Subgraph Virtual Edge Reconstruction

author.name: Qiming Guo, Wenbo Sun, Chen Pan, Ye Wang, Wenlu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CallosumNet, a spatio-temporal graph unlearning framework using subgraph virtual edge reconstruction to erase a single node without near-full-retraining cost. Targets the same GDPR/CCPA-driven problem as IsleNet by the same first author.

entry.title: Scalable Clinical Data Infrastructure and Comparative ML Evaluation for Hospitalisation Risk Prediction in Elderly Patients with Multiple Long-Term Conditions using CPRD

author.name: Asra Aslam, Volodymyr Chapman, Maurice M. O'Connell, Aseel S. Abuzour, Michael Abaho, Danushka Bollegala, Gary Leeming, Eduard Shantsila, Andrew Clegg, Lauren E. Walker, Iain Edward Buchan, Samuel D. Relton

entry.summary: Builds a large-scale clinical pipeline on CPRD Aurum with 260 coded conditions and benchmarks a temporal graph CNN against LASSO logistic regression and random forests for 12-month emergency hospitalization risk in elderly patients. Findings speak to whether deep learning beats simpler interpretable models on real EHR data.

entry.title: Adversarial Online Classification with a Preview

author.name: Roi Livni, Sahil Singla

entry.summary: Studies adversarial online classification with a preview, where a random fraction of a fixed adversarial sequence is revealed before prediction, characterizing optimal excess loss as Theta(d/p + sqrt(dT)) for VC dimension d. Bridges Littlestone-dimension hardness with sample-reveal settings.

entry.title: Unsupervised Multi-Scale Gromov-Wasserstein Hypergraph Alignment

author.name: Lutz Oettershagen, Honglian Wang, Aristides Gionis

entry.summary: Introduces FALCON, a filtration-based multi-scale Gromov-Wasserstein method for unsupervised hypergraph alignment using only structure, avoiding the costs of clique or bipartite expansions for non-uniform hypergraphs.

entry.title: Designing for the Next Click: Bandits for Real-Time Page Layout

author.name: Bhavtosh Rath, Harshith Narasimhamurthy, Bob Eisinger, Cole Stiegler, Adnan Awow, Amit Pande

entry.summary: Presents a LinUCB-based contextual bandit system deployed on an e-commerce platform for real-time product page layout optimization, balancing exploration-exploitation while preserving human design control, tested first offline then live.

entry.title: INTERVenE: Temporal-Abstraction-Interval Based Transformers for Short-Horizon Medical Event Prediction

author.name: Shahar Oded, Yuval Shahar

entry.summary: Presents INTERVenE, Transformer architectures over knowledge-based temporal abstraction tokens of named clinical concepts for ICU event prediction, making per-token attributions resolve to clinical concepts by construction.

entry.title: Tracing Generated Samples to Training-Data Clusters in Flow-Matching Models

author.name: Rania Briq, Ohad Fried, Michael Kamp, Stefan Kesselheim

entry.summary: Develops trajectory-based attribution for flow-matching models, tracing generated images to training-data clusters through velocity-field influence, and shows local velocity changes do not predict final counterfactual effects.

entry.title: TPR-Attention for Combinatorial Generalization

author.name: Melisa Civeleko\u{g}lu, Isabeau Pr\'emont-Schwarz

entry.summary: Introduces TPR-Attention, an attention mechanism over tensor-product representations embedding structured inductive bias, showing improved combinatorial generalization on controlled compositional tasks.

entry.title: Context Staircase: Signature-Aligned Dynamics of Token Embeddings under Small Initialization

author.name: Junjie Yao, Liangkai Hang, Zhi-Qin John Xu

entry.summary: Identifies a Context Staircase dynamic in which token embeddings under small initialization first align with low-order probability signatures (label, then contextual distributions) before high-order ones, formalizing embedding formation in language model training.

entry.title: Coarse composition suffices: tabular in-context learning for multi-activity antimicrobial peptide profiling

author.name: Raunak Kumar, Anuj Pal, Dhruvi Solanki, Parikshit Pareek, Juhi Singh, Jitin Singla

entry.summary: Shows that a simple sequence-only pipeline combining interpretable descriptors with TabPFN in-context prediction matches or beats multimodal deep models on the ESCAPE antimicrobial peptide multi-label benchmark. This challenges the assumption that expensive structure-conditioned architectures are necessary for this task. The result has practical value for low-cost peptide screening.

entry.title: Mode Connectivity Beyond Classifiers: Evidence from Generative and Contrastive Models

author.name: Chengzheyi Yao, Yongzhao Zhang, Yongding Tian

entry.summary: Extends mode connectivity research, traditionally limited to classifiers, to generative and contrastive models, specifically DDPM and NanoCLIP, via an architecture-aware connection-building algorithm. It provides evidence that low-loss paths between independently trained modes exist beyond the classifier setting. This broadens the empirical foundation of loss-landscape geometry.

entry.title: Uncertainty of Vision Medical Foundation Models

author.name: Haoxu Huang, Narges Razavian

entry.summary: Evaluates point and region-level uncertainty quantification, including conformal prediction with finite-sample validity guarantees, for vision-based medical foundation models across pretraining approaches, dataset scales, and domains. It provides evidence on when prediction sets are reliable in high-stakes medical settings. Useful for deployment decisions in clinical ML.

entry.title: Propensity Straight-Through Gradients for Discrete Stochastic Systems

author.name: Jose M. G. Vilar, Leonor Saiz

entry.summary: The authors propose the propensity straight-through (PST) estimator, which differentiates normalized reaction propensities to get exact one-step conditional-mean sensitivities for continuous-time Markov chains, bridging Gillespie-style simulation with gradient-based learning. They also characterize bias arising when one-step sensitivities compose across trajectory events.

entry.title: From Extraction to Governed Memory: Multi-Agent Knowledge Graph Construction with Domain-Expert Review

author.name: Pranav Bykampadi, Neel Mokaria, Vishesh Narayan, Faizan Wajid, Ashok Agrawala

entry.summary: MAGG is a multi-agent framework for building Governed Knowledge Graphs, adding explicit governance decisions (ownership, provenance, review by domain experts) to agentic knowledge construction. It argues that flat triple stores are insufficient for reliable knowledge sharing in agentic systems.

entry.title: ORDDAR: Observation-Driven Reasoning for Distortion-Resilient Decision, Action, and Cognitive Recovery

author.name: Deblina Kar, Anant Nawalgaria, Shyamal Kumar Das Mandal

entry.summary: ORDDAR models agent reasoning as cognitive state transitions and performs targeted recovery: it localizes distorted intermediate states, retrieves related prior reasoning, and repairs only affected states. This selective repair contrasts with wholesale re-planning or self-reflection loops.

entry.title: A rigor-matched audit of periodic-step layer skipping for efficient llm inference: conflayers versus swift, with a supplemental analysis of trained routing alternatives

author.name: Prateek Kumar Sikdar, Arpan Ghosh

entry.summary: The authors run a rigor-matched, three-seed audit comparing periodic-step layer-skipping methods (confidence-gated early exit versus SWIFT self-speculative decoding) for efficient LLM inference across two Qwen2.5 scales and two tasks. SWIFT wins on accuracy in three of four settings while ConfLayers is dominated throughout.

entry.title: From Location Phrases to Geographic Entities: Task-Adapted Retrieval for People Search

author.name: Yanbo Li, Chujie Zheng, Jiahao Xu, Chetan Bhole, Lingyu Zhang, Puneet Singh Ahluwalia, Kevin Nguyen, Raghavan Muthuregunathan, Santhosh Sachindran, Sachin Ahuja, Fedor Borisyuk

entry.summary: This paper from LinkedIn formulates mapping free-form location phrases to geographic entities for people search as graded, set-valued entity retrieval over a fixed ontology. It solves three coupled requirements via a prompt-asymmetric bi-encoder with calibrated alias support, ambiguity-aware negatives, and editable entity documents.

entry.title: Clustering as Approximation by Constrained Projectors: Theory and Guarantees

author.name: Angshul Majumdar

entry.summary: Develops a unified framework showing that k-means, fuzzy c-means, kernel variants, and spectral clustering can all be expressed as constrained low-rank projectors on a signal-derived matrix, deriving geodesic convexity, perturbation stability, and exact recovery results within a common optimization template.

entry.title: Subtraction-Based Tumor Segmentation and Lesion-Centered pCR Prediction for the MAMA-MIA Challenge

author.name: Kai Geissler, Raphael Sch\"afer

entry.summary: Describes a second-place submission to the MAMA-MIA challenge for breast MRI tumor segmentation and pathological complete response prediction, using a subtraction-based nnU-Net ensemble for segmentation and an ensemble of 25 pretrained 3D video classifiers on lesion-centered crops for pCR prediction, ranked on performance-fairness metrics across a multi-country cohort.

entry.title: A-MADiff: Attention-Guided Multi-Agent DRL with Diffusion Policies for Memory-Aware Task Orchestration in Mobile AIGC Networks

author.name: Chongzhi Wu, Zhengtao Li, Jiawen Kang, Jinbo Wen, Xiaohuan Li, Maomao Zhang, Ekram Hossain

entry.summary: Presents A-MADiff, a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework with diffusion policies for orchestrating AIGC tasks across edge nodes, explicitly modeling GPU memory feasibility so that serving providers avoid out-of-memory failures rather than just latency spikes.

entry.title: Spectral Analysis for Sparse Matrix Computation: Insights and Potential

author.name: Ruifeng Zhang, Xipeng Shen

entry.summary: First exploration connecting sparse matrix computation to spectral analysis by treating sparse matrices as 2D signals and analyzing FFT-derived frequency signatures, showing they capture global structural characteristics that spatial statistics miss and that are relevant to cache reuse, coalescing, and load balancing.

entry.title: Forward-Deployed Full-Stack Engineering for Autonomous Cloud MLOps

author.name: Sagar Srinivas Sakhinana, Venkataramana Runkana

entry.summary: Presents an evidence-gated multi-agent framework that converts natural-language MLOps cloud engineering tasks into verified repositories and operational cloud deployments, using a stateful graph orchestrator coordinating agents for generation, review, execution, verification, release, monitoring, and rollback.

entry.title: Towards Continual Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models in Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Chandler Timm C. Doloriel, Yunbei Zhang, Sarthak Kumar Maharana, Muhammad Salman Siddiqui, Tor Kristian Stevik, Fadi Al Machot, Kristian Hovde Liland, Habib Ullah

entry.summary: Studies continual test-time adaptation of vision-language models for open-vocabulary segmentation, diagnosing patch-level class collapse and erosion of vision-language alignment under entropy minimization. Proposes DAF, combining a marginal diversity loss, cross-modal anchoring to a frozen source model, and salience filtering to skip low-value gradients.

entry.title: PAUSE: Editable Strategy Artifacts for Long-Form Cultural Story Adaptation

author.name: Taaha Kazi, Vasu Sharma, Mohammad Saifullah, Abdur Rahman

entry.summary: Introduces PAUSE, an editable strategy artifact that gives humans a control surface over cultural decisions in long-form story adaptation, tested on two Chinese serialized novels. Human edits to the strategy propagated into chapter-level prose, with judges preferring edited outputs in all nine comparisons.

entry.title: Attribute-Based Activation Steering of LLMs for Group-Specific Explanation Generation

author.name: Leandra Fichtel, Janek Prange, Henning Wachsmuth

entry.summary: Proposes attribute-based activation steering for LLM explanation generation, computing group-specific steering vectors from explanatory style and knowledge attributes to tailor explanations to audiences, going beyond prompting alone.

entry.title: Detecting and Repairing Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Sai Krishna Reddy Mulakkayala, Niki van Stein, Aske Plaat

entry.summary: Goes beyond hallucination detection in RAG to repair, splitting flagged answers into individual factual claims, checking each against retrieved sources, and comparing repair strategies on RAGTruth. Addresses the underexplored question of what action should follow detection.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs on Conversational Text-to-SQL under Chain Ambiguity and Intent Drift

author.name: Yujia Liu, Jiayan Lin, Zijin Hong, Zheng Yuan, Shengyuan Chen, Hao Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Xiao Huang, Feiran Huang

entry.summary: Introduces TIDE-Bench, a conversational text-to-SQL benchmark built on 514 annotated dialogues targeting chain ambiguity (layered clarification with conditional dependencies) and intent drift (retraction and replacement of committed request elements), beyond simple execution accuracy.

entry.title: PrivBench: A Holistic and Modular Benchmarking Platform for Evaluating Text-to-Text Privatization

author.name: Stephen Meisenbacher, Andreea-Elena Bodea, Ahmet Bilal Ak{\i}n, Alexandra Klymenko, Jana Diesner, Florian Matthes

entry.summary: Introduces PrivBench, a holistic and modular benchmarking platform unifying the fragmented evaluation of text-to-text privatization methods, supporting multiple metrics for privacy preservation and utility.

entry.title: TaxCE : A Framework for Automated Taxonomy Construction and Evaluation at Scale

author.name: Sandeep Sricharan Mukku, Albert Aristotle Nanda, Rohit Pyati

entry.summary: TaxCE is a fully automated framework for constructing multi-level hierarchical taxonomies from large volumes of unstructured feedback text, with corpus-grounded evaluation metrics such as Exclusivity. It targets scale and long-tail topics that existing shallow-taxonomy methods miss.

entry.title: TRIPPULSE: Multi-Agent Travel Planning with Review-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Priyanshu Karmakar, Borru Vijay Sai, Shubhojit Mallick, Abhik Jana, Shreya Ghosh, Manish Gupta

entry.summary: TRIPPULSE is a multi-agent framework for travel itinerary generation grounded in user reviews, decomposing planning into specialized agents to capture experiential factors like comfort, safety, and crowding absent from structured databases.

entry.title: When Does Predictor-Based RL Align with Human Perception? A Study of Subjective Rewards in Codec-Based Speech Language Models

author.name: Joonyong Park, Jerry Li

entry.summary: The paper studies when learned perceptual predictors can serve as RL rewards for codec-based TTS, using GRPO for anime-like style, naturalness, likability, and arousal with a character error rate zone constraint to prevent transcript drift. Single-reward runs each improve their own target metric, showing subjective predictors can be optimized without fully collapsing alignment. It compares policy optimization against Best-of-N reranking under the same reward gate.

entry.title: DIASENTINEL: An Auditable Multi-Agent System for Guideline-Grounded Diabetes Risk Screening

author.name: Yung Wei Shueh, Zhi-Jie Chen, Chia-Hsuan Hsu, Hsin-Ling Hsu, Donghua Zhang, Chenwei Wu, Jun-En Ding, Tongze Zhang, Shihao Yang, Pengfei Hu, Fang-Ming Hung, Feng Liu

entry.summary: DIASENTINEL is an on-premise multi-agent demonstration system for one-year type 2 diabetes risk screening from EHRs, combining calibrated risk prediction, deterministic signal extraction, reciprocal rank fusion over ADA guidelines, and hybrid rule-plus-LLM-entailment verification. It provides a real-time screening dashboard and cited patient reports. The emphasis is auditability and grounding of clinical recommendations.

entry.title: Distributional Validity and Calibration of a Korean Synthetic Persona Panel for Digital and AI Service Use: A Secondary-Data Validation Against the Korea Media Panel Survey

author.name: Howard Kim, Keun Tae Cho

entry.summary: This secondary-data validation study tests how well a Korean synthetic persona panel (NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas-Korea conditioned into Gemini 3.5 Flash and EXAONE) reproduces digital and AI service-use distributions from the Korea Media Panel Survey. About 8,000 stratified personas per model answered the survey items, compared against weighted survey estimates. It provides rare non-English validation of synthetic respondents.

entry.title: How Mental Health Self-Disclosure Becomes Visible: Evidence from Eight Conditions on Reddit

author.name: Renkai Ma, Lingyao Li, Shanting Chen, Chen Chen, Fan Yang, Yuanyuan Lei

entry.summary: This study analyzes 89,605 Reddit posts from 739 users across eight mental health conditions, aligning posts to each user's diagnosis disclosure to trace how language burden becomes visible. Language-visible burden peaks in the month before disclosure for six conditions, with condition-specific timing, and remains visible afterward rather than resolving. The work offers a longitudinal, within-user perspective on mental health self-disclosure.

entry.title: OASIS: Optimizing Attacker Sequences for Hard-Label Black-Box Text Attacks

author.name: Qian Chen, Shiliang Xiao, Yuzhi Liang

entry.summary: OASIS optimizes sequences of hard-label black-box text attackers, observing that different attack methods succeed on different sample subsets. It performs a one-time bi-objective search over attack chains balancing success rate and perturbation, then reuses the selected chain. It consistently outperforms strong standalone attackers and manually constructed chains.

entry.title: When Can We Work in Embedding Space? What Text Embeddings Preserve

author.name: Simon Freyaldenhoven

entry.summary: Formalizes when text embeddings can validly substitute for text in empirical analysis under a latent-topic generative model, analyzing clustering and high-dimensional control applications, demonstrated on 363 US metropolitan areas with LLM-generated economic descriptions. Bridges embeddings and econometric validity. Useful conceptual grounding for social-science use of embeddings.

entry.title: MIRAGE-CAD: Construction-Mediated Multimodal Generation of Executable CAD Programs

author.name: Jizong Zhan

entry.summary: MIRAGE-CAD maps natural language, rendered images, point clouds, and B-Rep geometry to a shared construction representation to generate executable parametric CAD programs via an explicit construction-plan interface, achieving 55-70% build success on 2,500 held-out queries per modality. Multimodal CAD program synthesis is a meaningful step for engineering automation.

entry.title: TopoAgent: A Structure-Aware Perception-to-Reasoning Framework for Diagram-to-Graph Topology Extraction with Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Bangwei Guo, Xujiang Zhao, Yanchi Liu, Wei Cheng, Shengyu Chen, Dongyue Li, Masaharu Morimoto, Takayuki Kuroda, Dimitris Metaxas, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: TopoAgent is a structure-aware perception-to-reasoning framework for diagram-to-graph topology extraction with large VLMs, accompanied by TopoBench-180, a human-verified benchmark of 180 structural diagrams with canonical graph annotations. Addresses fine-grained grounding plus global consistency requirements that current VLMs handle poorly.

entry.title: FigMirror: Ground It, Code It, Plot It

author.name: Xiaohan Zhao, Jiacheng Liu, Yaxin Luo, Zhiqiang Shen

entry.summary: FigMirror is an agentic framework that converts scientific figures into plotting code preserving the reference style for new data, using grounded coordinate measurement and executable code through computer-use-model capabilities rather than pixel-level mimicry. Practical research-workflow automation with an agentic design.

entry.title: Chat-Edit-3D++: Interactive 3D and 4D Scene Editing via Large Language Models

author.name: Shuangkang Fang, Yufeng Wang, Yi-Hsuan Tsai, Wenrui Ding, Yi Yang, Shuchang Zhou, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: Chat-Edit-3D++ reformulates interactive text-driven 3D/4D scene editing as operations on 2D atlas images via a Hash-Atlas network, decoupling editing from fixed 2D visual models and complex reconstruction pipelines. Strengthens 3D scene editing as an interactive design tool.

entry.title: Feature-Spectral Fragility in Segmentation: Dataset Dependence, Architecture-Specific Localization, and Spectral Correlates

author.name: Subhash Kashyap

entry.summary: Studies feature-spectral fragility in segmentation models by applying post-training low-pass filtering to internal representations of CNN, SSM, and transformer architectures across two datasets. Findings show dramatic cross-dataset differences in sensitivity, with CNNs most vulnerable and transformers most robust. This offers useful diagnostic insight into how frequency content in learned features drives brittleness.

entry.title: DARD: Zero-Shot Degradation-Aware Retinex-Guided Diffusion for Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Wenjie Cai, Yuezhe Yang, Jianyang Xia, Xingbo Dong, Zhe Jin

entry.summary: DARD is a zero-shot low-light enhancement framework combining test-time degradation-aware Retinex decomposition with diffusion models, extracting image-specific physical priors for structural guidance. This avoids paired supervision while reducing color drift and structural inconsistency. Combines classical physical priors with modern generative modeling in a sensible way.

entry.title: MotionSync: Non-Causal Refinement of Causal Tracker for Label-Efficient 3D Perception

author.name: Rahul Ahuja, Bala Murali Manoghar Sai Sudhakar, Shashwata Gupta, Venkatraman Narayanan, Varun Ravi Kumar, Senthil Yogamani

entry.summary: See item 20 above: compact VLM reads full PCB engineering drawings end-to-end with a localization-first curriculum.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Bridges for Spatiotemporally Aligned Image Translation and Generation

author.name: Xing Xie, Jiawei Liu, Shijun Zhou, Huijie Fan, Zhi Han, Yandong Tang, Liangqiong Qu

entry.summary: An agent-driven pipeline reconstructs LoD3 facade openings in semantic 3D city models from volunteered street-view imagery using zero-shot LLM/VLM segmentation, enforcing CityGML-conform partonomic hierarchies. Reduces annotation burden for urban digital-twin modeling.

entry.title: OPAL: Orthonormal Prototype Alignment Learning for Interpretable Image Classification

author.name: Il\'an Carretero, Gustavo Jes\'us Angulo, Roc\'io del Amor, Valery Naranjo

entry.summary: OPAL introduces a single-stage, end-to-end framework for prototypical part-based interpretable classification, anchoring latent space with orthonormal bases to prevent prototype collapse without auxiliary regularization. Simplifies training of explainable models.

entry.title: DICS: Exploring Data Intrinsic Consistency for Visual Instruction Selection

author.name: Yuyang Hong, Jinhui Guo, Jiaqi Gu, Lubin Fan, Ruixiang Wang, Kun Ding, Yue Wu, Shiming Xiang, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: DICS proposes Data Intrinsic Consistency, a self-scoring metric for visual instruction selection that quantifies alignment between visual content, instructions, and responses within individual samples. Improves data curation for vision-language model tuning.

entry.title: Amortized Anchor Refinement for Deployable Continuous-Time 4D Gaussian Reconstruction

author.name: Jingong Chen, Qingwen Zhang, Sanghyeon Jun, Chulwoo Pack, Kyle Gao, Kwanghee Won

entry.summary: Amortized Anchor Refinement combines feed-forward prediction with short per-scene optimization under a fixed compute budget for deployable continuous-time 4D Gaussian reconstruction on XR headsets, with persistent-homology pruning and scene-flow streaming. Makes 4D reconstruction practical where collapse previously occurred.

entry.title: Whole-Slide Image Analysis under Realistic Few-Shot Annotation Protocols

author.name: Tiffanie Godelaine, Maxime Zanella, Karim El Khoury, Benoit Macq, Christophe De Vleeschouwer

entry.summary: Studies few-shot transductive refinement of vision-language patch predictions for whole-slide image analysis under realistic annotation protocols that respect multi-slide structure. Corrects optimistic evaluations of prior transductive methods.

entry.title: Learning Compositional Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding with Synthetic Curriculum

author.name: Xingjian Wang, Shijian Wang, Yibo Wang, Zihao Yu, Runhao Fu, Xuelian Cheng, Zongyuan Ge

entry.summary: Introduces Text-Instructed Viewpoint Grounding (TIVG), a new task of finding a 6-DoF camera pose in a 3D Gaussian scene whose rendered frame matches a text instruction, with CapFrame solving it via geometric pseudo labels in a partially differentiable framework. New task definition with a practical solver.

entry.title: CheXGround: Anatomical Region Tokens for Grounded Longitudinal Chest X-ray Interpretation

author.name: Adonay Demewez Gebremedhin, Wessam Shehieb, Sara Alansari, Mohamad Alansari, Muzammal Naseer, Sajid Javed, Naoufel Werghi

entry.summary: CheXGround is a region-grounded longitudinal chest X-ray language model that represents paired studies through corresponding anatomical region tokens, connecting localized visual evidence with change description over time. Combines grounding and temporal reasoning for radiology.

entry.title: ChessQueries: Toward Better Chess Board Recognition

author.name: Jo\"el Seytre

entry.summary: Introduces ChessQueries (ViT encoder + DETR-style decoder) for chess board recognition, improving ChessReD state of the art from 15.3% to 99.2% and saturating both existing benchmarks, plus a harder new dataset parsed from broadcast video.

entry.title: PixelIR: Fidelity-Perception Decoupling via Pixel-Space Image-Residual Flow Matching for Efficient One-Step Real-World Super-Resolution

author.name: Bingtian Qiao, Yue Shi, Yong Guo, Wenjun Zhang, Jiezhang Cao

entry.summary: PixelIR decouples fidelity and perception in real-world super-resolution via pixel-space image-residual flow matching, modeling faithful reconstruction separately from perceptual detail synthesis for efficient one-step Real-ISR.

entry.title: A Controlled Evaluation of Model Rankings and Input Reliance in Surface Water Segmentation

author.name: Kittipat Phunjanna, Krist\'of Karacs, Chayut Ngamkhanong

entry.summary: This paper critically examines how surface-water segmentation models are ranked using aggregate IoU metrics on Sen1Floods11 and GEOID-Flood, showing that close model orderings can be unstable across seeds and that prediction reliance on inputs deserves separate analysis. It matters because it introduces a more rigorous evaluation methodology for flood-mapping systems that are deployed in real disaster response.

entry.title: Identity-Conditioned Latent Consistency Distillation for Face Synthesis

author.name: Tiago Kienen Chaves, Bernardo Biesseck, David Menotti

entry.summary: This work distills the Arc2Face diffusion teacher into an identity-conditioned latent consistency model requiring few sampling iterations, enabling cheap large-scale synthetic face dataset generation for face recognition training. It preserves quality while cutting computational cost substantially.

entry.title: BRF-GS: Hyperspectral Bidirectional Reflectance Factor Modeling and Image Generation Based on 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yiling Yao, Wenjuan Zhang, Bowen Wang, Bocheng Li, Wentao Song, Bing Zhang

entry.summary: BRF-GS extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to model bidirectional reflectance factors of terrestrial surfaces for efficient multi-angle hyperspectral reflectance image generation, overcoming the limits of low-order spherical harmonics and expensive radiative transfer solvers. It targets remote sensing applications.

entry.title: Breaking Darknet CAPTCHAs with general purpose LLM

author.name: Benjamin Fehrensen, Jens Hubler

entry.summary: The authors evaluate general-purpose multimodal LLMs on three darknet CAPTCHA types, finding systematic weaknesses in precise spatial localization and geometric transformation despite good visual structure recognition, mitigable via task reformulation or tool augmentation. It doubles as a security assessment and an MLLM spatial-reasoning probe.

entry.title: Teaching Robot Policies to Humans Using Erroneous Examples

author.name: Rithika Narayan, Suresh Kumaar Jayaraman, Henny Admoni

entry.summary: This human-robot interaction study proposes teaching robot policies to humans using erroneous examples, an education-derived method where learners reflect on flawed demonstrations to understand correct behavior. It addresses the open question of which demonstration-based explanation methods work across domains and learners.

entry.title: Agri-Sim: Agricultural Simulation Platform for Embodied Intelligence Evaluation in Greenhouse Robotics

author.name: Shuhan Shi, Zhenfeng Xue, Minghao Mei, Chao Zheng, Nan Li, Zhonghua Miao

entry.summary: Agri-Sim is a Unity-ROS2 simulation platform for greenhouse agricultural robots with a configurable tomato environment, dual-arm harvesting robot, virtual sensors, and MoveIt 2 integration for closed-loop development and evaluation. It fills a domain-specific simulation gap for embodied agricultural AI.

entry.title: SGE: Semantically-Guided Exploration for Unstructured Environments via Image-Space Waypoint Sampling

author.name: Christopher Tatsch, Yu Gu

entry.summary: SGE integrates pixel-level semantic segmentation into sampling-based exploration for ground vehicles, evaluating candidate waypoints directly in image space with a semantic-aware utility function, projecting them to 3D, and ordering via real-time TSP in a receding-horizon scheme. It targets unstructured environments.

entry.title: A Sliding Window Filter on the Galilean Group for Consistent Aided Inertial Navigation with Unknown Measurement Delays

author.name: Jonathan Kelly

entry.summary: Formulates aided inertial navigation with unknown constant measurement delays as a sliding window filter on the special Galilean group, jointly estimating delay and navigation state. The paper analyzes observability and shows an exact symmetry that makes single-delay estimation ill-posed, with process-noise assumptions resolving it.

entry.title: Module Number Adaptive Visual Shape Control for Serial Modular Soft Robots

author.name: Kyohei Akamine, Takato Horii, Yusuke Sakaue, Hiroki Ishizuka

entry.summary: Presents a visual shape control method for serial modular soft pneumatic robots that adapts to varying module counts (one to five) by decomposing whole-body camera images into local module patches processed by a shared controller and segmenter. Training uses only single-module actuation data.

entry.title: VeloBins: Learning Velocity and Its Uncertainty via Bins and Error-Conditioned Gaussian Labels for Aerial Inertial Odometry

author.name: Maulana Bisyir Azhari, Seungwook Lee, Donghun Han, Sung Jun Park, David Hyunchul Shim

entry.summary: VeloBins reformulates velocity regression for aerial inertial odometry as classification over discretized velocity bins, deriving uncertainty from the bin distribution without a separate NLL decoder. This avoids overconfident estimates and simplifies training for aggressive aerial maneuvers where vision fails.

entry.title: Data-Centric Neuromotor Interfaces for Portable Human-Machine Interaction

author.name: Jiaxuan Li, Di Wu, Jianhua Liu, Yuxin Zhao, Jinnuo Li, Xiao Zhang, Zhenzhi Ying, Changsheng Dai, Xiang Li, Liming Shu

entry.summary: Presents a data-centric paradigm for flexible neuromotor interfaces decoding movement intention from electrophysiological signals on constrained edge devices, with a wireless high-bandwidth acquisition system and muscle-signal integration for portable human-machine interaction.

entry.title: SpectraTac: A Compact Camera-Free Optical Tactile Sensor with Distributed Color Sensing

author.name: Hao Wu, Haotian Guo, Yu Feng, Yutong Wang, Yanzhe Wang, Jianshu Zhou

entry.summary: SpectraTac is a compact camera-free optical tactile sensor combining active RGB illumination with three distributed color sensors, capturing low-dimensional spatio-spectral features from elastomer deformation and avoiding cameras and high-dimensional image processing.

entry.title: Anomaly Detection on Small Industrial Components via Vision-Based Tactile Sensing

author.name: G. F. Preziosa, M. Casiglia, M. Faroni, A. M. Zanchettin, P. Rocco

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates unsupervised anomaly detection methods (SPADE, PaDiM, and other embedding approaches) on a real tactile dataset of five industrial components captured with a GelSight Mini on a collaborative robot, targeting sub-centimetre geometry-driven defects poorly resolved by cameras.

entry.title: CIG-RL: Curiosity-Driven Information-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Source Term Estimation in Uncertain Environments

author.name: Junhee Lee, Seunghwan Kim, Hongro Jang, Hyungjin Kim, Hyoungho Park, Changseung Kim, Hyondong Oh

entry.summary: CIG-RL applies curiosity-driven, information-guided reinforcement learning to source term estimation of hazardous gas releases, using belief states updated from noisy measurements and improving exploration beyond random or purely uncertainty-reducing strategies while keeping inference fast.

entry.title: Feelium: A Touchable Blimp Body for Aerial Telepresence

author.name: George Xi Wang, Henghao Li, Shan Lin, Yunge Wen, Jiaqian Hu, Yuhua Jin

entry.summary: Feelium is a blimp-based telepresence platform whose inflatable touchable skin supports visual embodiment and contact interaction: a remote person steers and views through it while co-located partners pat, press, and draw on the sensing skin, which renders touch into the wearer's VR view.

entry.title: Robust K-means Clustering using the Density Power Divergence Measure

author.name: Anirban Mondal, Paromita Banerjee, Abhijit Mandal

entry.summary: Introduces MK-means DPD, a robust K-means variant using density power divergence with Mahalanobis distance for outlier-resistant clustering of heterogeneous elliptical clusters, plus a provably convergent variant DC-MK-means DPD and new robust internal evaluation indices.

entry.title: Marginal Coordinate Test for Fr\'echet Regression with Random Objects

author.name: Jiaye Chen, Rui Qiu, Roulin Wang, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: Develops a marginal coordinate test for Frechet regression with random-object responses in metric spaces, using a semi-supervised design and a kernel conditional mean dependence U-statistic to test whether a predictor adds information conditional on others, without requiring response residuals.

entry.title: Why autonomous replicating agents are probably not an existential risk (on the contrary)

author.name: vals tutor

entry.summary: Argues that autonomous replicating agents are probably not an existential risk, presenting systemic reasons why agents operating at the fringes of society against active human mitigation would struggle to recursively self-improve at frontier rates, updating the 2024 ARA debate.

entry.title: Value generalisation Theory of Change: putting it into practice

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Stuart Armstrong lays out a practical theory of change for value generalisation research, describing how to detect value-relevant off-distribution states, decide what features matter off-distribution, and reach good decisions under such conditions, along with associated risks and mitigations. It translates an earlier theoretical argument into a concrete research program with inputs, outputs, and benchmarks.

entry.title: Time Capsule of Testable Human Knowledge: 41 Years of Jeopardy! in a Single Free Local Model

author.name: David Noever, Forrest McKee

entry.summary: Evaluates a single 9 GB 4-bit open-weight model (Qwen2.5-14B) over the complete open Jeopardy clue archive of 529,939 clues across 41 broadcast seasons, framing the artifact as a portable time capsule of queryable cultural knowledge in contrast to IBM Watson's massive 2011 infrastructure. The full-corpus run is claimed to be the first of its kind. Its main value is a striking data point on how much factual knowledge now fits on free local hardware.

entry.title: The Shape of Power: A Multilingual Framework for Social Power Reasoning in Dialogues

author.name: Farah Atif, Sougata Saha, Monojit Choudhury

entry.summary: Introduces a theoretically grounded, schema-driven framework with native-speaker annotation pipelines for studying social power in naturalistic multilingual dialogue through movie screenplays, releasing an initial corpus of 15,836 annotated instances from French and other-language scenes. Addresses demographic and relational depth gaps in computational power analysis. A valuable resource for social NLP with cross-cultural reach.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching for CT Image Reconstruction

author.name: Davide Evangelista

entry.summary: Trains a high-resolution rectified flow matching prior on low-dose chest CT and investigates physics-guided conditioning for reconstruction, positioning flow matching as a more stable and computationally efficient alternative to diffusion priors for ill-posed inverse problems. A competent medical imaging contribution. A single-site dataset and moderate resolution limit generality.

entry.title: Fidelity Is Not Enough: Dispatch-Level Instrumentation for Agentic Datasheet Extraction

author.name: Qing Ye, Meng-Hsuan Lin

entry.summary: Motivated by a model passing fidelity checks while fabricating source text (a structured-output constraint silently disabling tool use), builds dispatch-level instrumentation for agentic document extraction with failure attribution and silent-failure detectors on a hand-curated benchmark.

entry.title: Hallucination Mitigation for Large Vision-Language Models via Implicit Feature Stabilization

author.name: Aditi Sarker, Rafi Ibn Sultan, Hui Zhu, Dongxiao Zhu, Prashant Khanduri

entry.summary: Links hallucination in large vision-language models to measurable feature instability, showing hallucination rates rise with embedding variability under semantics-preserving perturbations. Proposes baking perturbation invariance into weights during fine-tuning so no inference-time intervention is needed.

entry.title: STAGEET: Stage-wise Typed Edit Tagging for Grammatical Error Correction with Arabic as a Case Study

author.name: Wenjie Lou, Alaa Mamdouh Akef

entry.summary: Analyzes 1,030 generative-AI virtual patient dialogue logs in medical education, showing coded process evidence (cue follow-up, uncertainty checks, summarization) is more teacher-interpretable than full transcripts or final scores. Bridges learning analytics and LLM-based clinical simulation.

entry.title: How You Ask Shapes What You Get: A Theory-Seeded Measurement of Articulation in Advice-Seeking LLM Conversations

author.name: Juneha Baek, Suhyeon Lee, Donghyuk Shin

entry.summary: Extracts interpretable articulation features from 16,447 advice-seeking prompts across WildChat, LMSYS, and ShareChat, recovering latent factors separable from topic that replicate across corpora and correlate with how LLMs respond. Treats how people ask as measurable structure rather than noise.

entry.title: Weaving Visual Narratives: Agentic Image Bundle Composition Beyond Atomic Visual Matching

author.name: Rong Shan, Tianyi Xu, Congmin Zheng, Wenteng Chen, Jiachen Zhu, Junjie Wu, Teng Wang, Weiwen Liu, Changwang Zhang, Weinan Zhang, Jun Wang, Jianghao Lin

entry.summary: Introduces Image Bundle Composition, shifting image retrieval from ranking individual photos to dynamically composing cohesive bundles that express structural relations in personal collections, tackling a severe combinatorial explosion with an agentic approach. A novel retrieval paradigm with product potential.

entry.title: ReconSplat: Generalizable 3D Scene Reconstruction Beyond Observed Views

author.name: Giuseppe Stracquadanio, Kevin Raj, Julia Grabinski, Stefan Roth

entry.summary: ReconSplat is a feed-forward 3D scene reconstruction model combining 3D Gaussian splatting with a multi-view latent diffusion refiner/inpainter guided by variational 3D latents, aiming to jointly achieve geometric consistency and plausible generation of unobserved regions. Addresses a known 3DGS limitation with an integrated design.

entry.title: DocIntent: Answerability-Guided Agentic Restoration for Real-World Document Visual Question Answering

author.name: Zihan Huang, Shihang Wu, Junle Liu, Peirong Zhang, Yongxin Shi, Xuhan Zheng, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: DocIntent explores answerability-guided agentic restoration for document VQA, where restoration strategies are chosen and executed to serve downstream answer quality rather than generic perceptual metrics, targeting real degradations like blur and moire. A sensible task-level reframing of document restoration.

entry.title: Multi-Scale Temporal Domain Alignment for Federated Video Domain Adaptation

author.name: Lee En-Yi Hannah, Haozhi Cao, Yuecong Xu

entry.summary: METAL tackles federated video domain adaptation by aligning temporal information at multiple scales, training per-scale transformer encoders and using knowledge voting with an L2 cross-scale consistency penalty. It enables cross-domain video action recognition with only model parameter transfers. This addresses an underexplored intersection of federated learning and video understanding.

entry.title: Not All Explanations Are Sought: Information-Seeking Psychology for Human-Centered XAI

author.name: Andrea Beretta, Salvatore Rinzivillo

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that human-centered explainable AI should incorporate the psychology of information seeking, modeling engagement with explanations through instrumental, hedonic, and cognitive expected utilities distorted by well-known cognitive biases. It identifies failure modes such as excessive or avoided information seeking. Provides useful design framing for when explanations help, though without empirical validation.

entry.title: Coverage, Not Credit: Failure-Credit Routing of Zeroth-Order Perturbation Budgets Does Not Improve On-Pool Sample Efficiency for LLM Agents

author.name: Yuxu Ge

entry.summary: Reports a rigorous null result: routing a fixed zeroth-order perturbation budget by trajectory-level failure credit across agent modules yields no statistically detectable on-pool sample-efficiency gain over uniform allocation for tool-using LLM agents, tested across three task families, six allocation schemes, multiple model sizes, and exact sign-flip tests. Negative results of this quality help steer agent-training research. Narrow setting but unusually careful methodology.

entry.title: CrabOS: An Operating System for Human-AI Co-inhabitation

author.name: Qi Yang, Yun Ma

entry.summary: Proposes CrabOS, an operating-system design for human-AI co-inhabitation in which long-running agents and people share work environments and alternate leading task execution with seamless work-state handoff, replacing brittle bridges such as screenshots or task-specific interfaces. A forward-looking systems vision for agent integration into daily computing. Interesting but early-stage.

entry.title: SNF-Bench: Separating Static Drift from Natural Flow in Long-Horizon Fixed-Camera Video Generation

author.name: Matiur Rahman Minar, Seunghun Oh, Ganghyeon Jeong, Unsang Park

entry.summary: SNF-Bench introduces an evaluation framework for long-horizon fixed-camera video generation that separates static support from dynamic flow, reporting static fidelity, flow persistence, and drift leakage as distinct metrics instead of one aggregate score. Addresses genuine metric ambiguity in video generation evaluation.

entry.title: CareGraph: An Auditable Hybrid AI Framework for Evidence-Grounded Personalized Longitudinal Health Intelligence

author.name: Pratik Ghawate, Tanvi Patil

entry.summary: Describes CareGraph, an auditable hybrid pipeline that converts heterogeneous clinical, self-reported, and wearable evidence into prioritized trends, missing-context indicators, bounded next steps, and provenance-linked explanations while explicitly avoiding diagnosis, prediction, or treatment selection. Emphasizes deterministic analysis, constrained LLM synthesis, safety controls, and release gating. Addresses provenance and auditability in health AI, but evaluation relies on synthetic cohorts only.

entry.title: Why Didn't It Check? Unsupported Final Claims and Their Repair in Two Tool-Equipped Language Models

author.name: Justin Bronder

entry.summary: Separates two quantities in tool-equipped LLM failures: occurrence of unsupported final claims despite available tool calls and explicit no-guessing instructions, and conditional repair once the missing evidence is supplied, studying one fixed Qwen3-32B setup in which 33 of 512 responses ended in unsupported claims. A focused diagnostic study of why models skip verification. Small scale but conceptually clean.

entry.title: Learning to Allocate Incentives for Incentivized Advertising via Offline Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zilin Zhao, Han Yang, Tianpei Yang, Fangsheng Huang, Yanfei Cui, Kan Peng, Yi Li, Yiming Zong, Hao Zhang, Yinsong Xue

entry.summary: Formulates incentive allocation for incentivized advertising, where platforms promise users bonuses before observing downstream ad revenue, as a sequential decision problem with delayed revenue, cost sensitivity, and carryover effects, and develops an offline model-based reinforcement learning solution filling a gap between auto-bidding and targeted promotion. An industrial-scale application with a novel problem setting. Solid applied RL.

entry.title: SEPO: Evidence-Grounded Prompt Optimization via Structural Editing

author.name: Xiaoyu Ma, Haoyue Liu, Yiwen Li, Jionghao Zhu, Zhichao Wang, Ye Chen, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: Introduces SEPO, a prompt optimizer that performs structural edits on stable typed units in a two-layer prompt schema and maintains edit-effect lineage linking each structural edit to the examples it newly fixes or breaks, carrying that record forward to guide later iterations, in contrast to opaque whole-prompt rewrites. Improves localizability and auditability of prompt optimization. A nice engineering-concept contribution in a crowded area.

entry.title: RiskBlend: A Multi-Signal Framework for Test Input Prioritization in Machine Learning Regression Testing

author.name: Madhusudan Srinivasan, Namith Nishal Raphae

entry.summary: RiskBlend is a classifier-agnostic framework for prioritizing test inputs in ML regression testing, exploiting how predictions, decision boundaries, and local neighborhoods shift between model versions rather than relying on single-model confidence. This improves detection of regression faults under a limited human-verification budget. Addresses an overlooked practical problem in ML system maintenance.

entry.title: Explainable Uncertainty Estimation for Reliable Medical AI

author.name: Li Rong Wang, Jamie Duell, Xinran Xu, Thomas C. Henderson, Yu Yue Hew, Pik Wan Erica Chiang, Xiao Wei Alstar Ang, Bingwen Eugene Fan, Xiuyi Fan

entry.summary: Qwen-GuidePlay-2B fine-tunes a 2B model for dialogue-game interaction via staged SFT (successful trajectories, weighted turn-level SFT, teacher-guided SFT), achieving the second-highest Playpen clemscore delta among challenge submissions, roughly +36 over base. It finds trajectory imitation builds playability while turn-level weighting builds quality. A small-model efficiency result with a clean staged recipe.

entry.title: Text Restoration of Ancient Documents with Language Models

author.name: Shibingfeng Zhang, Edoardo Caraffa, Annafelicia Zuffrano, Maddalena Modesti, Giovanni Colavizza

entry.summary: Evaluates language models of varying architectures for restoring missing text in damaged ancient manuscripts, proposing decoding strategies to handle lacuna boundaries misaligned with tokenization. Finds restoration cannot be fully automated but assists paleographers.

entry.title: Embedding Models for Stance-Aware Argument Retrieval

author.name: Angelo Sparacino, Francesca Toni, Adam Dejl

entry.summary: Studies dense embedding models for stance-aware argument retrieval, showing existing models strongly bias toward topical overlap while ignoring stance instructions (support vs attack). Relevant to retrieval pipelines needing dual topic and stance assessment.

entry.title: Are These Modules Worth Their Cost? A Paradigm-Level Accuracy-Cost Analysis of In-context Learning Text-to-SQL

author.name: Jiayan Lin, Yujia Liu, Zijin Hong, Zheng Yuan, Yilin Xiao, Hao Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Xiao Huang, Feiran Huang

entry.summary: Provides a paradigm-level accuracy-cost analysis of ICL text-to-SQL pipelines, instantiating 17 configurations across five recurring modules to quantify marginal contribution of each design choice rather than aggregate end-to-end accuracy.

entry.title: Temperature-Adaptive Transformed Teacher Matching

author.name: Hiroaki Aizawa, Yoshikazu Hayashi

entry.summary: Extends Transformed Teacher Matching with a sample-wise inverse-temperature update derived by locally minimizing KL between the temperature-scaled teacher and student prediction, with closed-form updates and convergence analysis.

entry.title: BEACON: Behavioral and Semantic Enrichment of AlphaEarth Embeddings through Tri-Modal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Hao Tian, Heng Cai, Yifan Yang

entry.summary: Proposes BEACON, a tri-modal contrastive framework aligning AlphaEarth embeddings with POI text and hourly visitation behavior to enrich geospatial embeddings with human activity signals absent from imagery-only training.

entry.title: On the Resilience of Text-to-Video Diffusion Models to Hardware Faults

author.name: Zachary Coalson, A M Aahad, Stella Doehring, Zane Ma, Sanghyun Hong

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic fault-injection study of text-to-video diffusion models under hardware faults across three models, finding single faults degrade performance up to 3.7%, memory faults are more damaging than compute faults, and semantic correctness is more affected than perceptual quality.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Inverse Design of Dielectric Resonator Metasurfaces for Shaping Smart Electromagnetic Environments

author.name: M. Tsukerman, K. Grotov, D. Vovchuk, P. Ginzburg

entry.summary: Applies diffusion models to the inverse design of dielectric resonator metasurfaces, generating physically realizable structures from prescribed scattering signatures for smart electromagnetic environments.

entry.title: Error Detection for PET/CT Radiology Reports: Domain-Specific vs Large Language Models

author.name: Hermione Warr, Harry Anthony, Lilli J Freischem, Yasin Ibrahim, Daniel R McGowan, Konstantinos Kamnitsas

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic evaluation of LLMs versus domain-specific BERT models for detecting clinically meaningful errors in PET/CT radiology reports, using 30,633 oncology reports over ten years with clinically motivated synthetic error injection.

entry.title: Benchmarking Peptide-Protein Affinity Prediction Across Peptide and Target Shifts

author.name: Jiaxin Tian, Darren An, Jun Li

entry.summary: Benchmarks ten peptide representations, ESM-2 embeddings, and six regressors for peptide-protein affinity prediction under peptide-similarity, within-target, and leave-target-out splits across 11,349 pairs, showing large performance differences across shift types.

entry.title: Locally-Guided Actor-Critic: Training a Goal-conditioned Actor with a Subgoal-aware Critic

author.name: Olivier Serris, St\'ephane Doncieux, Olivier Sigaud

entry.summary: Proposes locally-guided actor-critic for goal-conditioned RL with sparse rewards, training a subgoal-aware critic so the policy stays conditioned only on the final goal, enabling planner-free deployment. It fixes goal-chaining issues in RIS by building on potential-based reward shaping. A thoughtful contribution to long-horizon RL.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Pretext Tasks for Infant Cry Analysis: A Controlled Comparison and a Cautionary Result on Donateacry

author.name: Luigi Simeone

entry.summary: Compares six self-supervised pretext tasks for infant cry analysis under a fixed compute and data budget, finding that reconstructive objectives dominate cry detection (0.988 AUC) but that all encoders perform at chance on cry-reason classification over the Donateacry benchmark. It provides strong evidence the de facto benchmark does not support meaningful learning. A valuable cautionary result on benchmark validity.

entry.title: ToxLens: A Reproducible Graph-Learning Framework for Leakage-Aware, Uncertainty-Calibrated Molecular Toxicity Prediction

author.name: Magnus H. Str{\o}mme, Alex G. C. de S\'a, David B. Ascher

entry.summary: Presents ToxLens, a reproducible graph-learning framework for 11 molecular toxicity endpoints combining leakage-aware splits, uncertainty calibration via Monte Carlo dropout and conformal sets, and applicability-domain analysis. It emphasizes that conventional benchmarks overstate utility when structurally similar molecules leak across folds. A rigor-minded contribution to computational toxicology.

entry.title: When the Martingale Never Stops Firing: Anytime-Valid Gating on Real Forecast Streams

author.name: Weijia Han, Lisha Qu

entry.summary: Examines when conformal test martingales and anytime-valid change detection retain their guarantees on real forecast streams, showing the exchangeability premise is hardest to satisfy exactly where monitors are most useful, in dependent data and closed loops where the monitor modifies the learner. It develops gating mechanisms for this setting. Conceptually important for trustworthy online monitoring of deployed ML.

entry.title: Representation Learning with Quantum Signal Processing

author.name: Junqi Wang, Junyu Liu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper establishes quantum signal processing as a solvable model of representation learning, computing exact NTK statistics at arbitrary depth and proving sparse-data guarantees for full nonlinear gradient flow without freezing the kernel. It reveals input-dependent geometry that remains non-self-averaging even near Haar randomness.

entry.title: MERIT: Mitigating Exposure Bias in Generative XMC for User-Interest Propensity Modeling

author.name: Abhinav Mahajan, Arindam Sarkar, Prakash Mandayam Comar

entry.summary: MERIT addresses exposure bias in generative extreme multi-label classification for e-commerce user-interest propensity modeling: teacher-forced fine-tuning lets early errors steer later autoregressive predictions toward co-occurring labels. The framework mitigates this over-generation of near-correlates and missed unrelated true interests.

entry.title: Sense Once, Serve Many: Common-Trace Factorized Constrained PPO for Online Sensing-Session Consolidation in Multi-Tenant ISAC Networks

author.name: Dang-Dung Vu

entry.summary: Formulates sensing-session consolidation in multi-tenant ISAC networks as a constrained MDP and proposes CT-PPO, which shares primitive workload traces across policy replicas and uses leave-one-out Monte Carlo return contrasts for credit assignment, achieving strong results across seeds and workloads.

entry.title: APPSolver: Adaptive Patch Partitioning for Point-Wise Ship Flow Prediction on Unstructured Meshes

author.name: Wenhua Huo, Fenglei Han, Wangyuan Zhao, Xiao Peng, Chunhui Wang, Jialin Wu, Jiayi Han

entry.summary: Introduces APPSolver for ship hydrodynamics flow prediction using adaptive quadtree patch partitioning over unstructured mesh slices, and reports a corrected evaluation protocol (natural train/test pairs, reused normalization statistics, multiple seeds) under which learned tokenizers beat the APP-Transformer and a persistence baseline is surprisingly competitive.

entry.title: ButterMamba: Butterworth-Enhanced Spatial-Temporal Mamba for Efficient Traffic Flow Prediction

author.name: Limiao Zhang, Yuhui Lu, Jie Gao, Hao Jiang, Haiping Ma, Xingyi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces ButterMamba, combining Butterworth filtering with a spatial-temporal Mamba backbone for traffic flow prediction, targeting quadratic attention costs and high-frequency sensor noise in large metropolitan networks.

entry.title: Continual Test-Time Adaptation via Entropy Sensitivity-Guidance in Strict Online Setting

author.name: Chandler Timm C. Doloriel, Yunbei Zhang, Muhammad Salman Siddiqui, Tor Kristian Stevik, Fadi Al Machot, Kristian Hovde Liland, Habib Ullah

entry.summary: Introduces SEGA, a strict online continual test-time adaptation method that probes predictive entropy via structured erasures to guide recovery and sample selection under batch-size-one streams without source data. Targets drift and collapse in long-horizon adaptation on corruption streams.

entry.title: Evolutionary Soups: Evolving Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Objective LLM Alignment

author.name: Lingxiao Kong, Steffen Staab, Cong Yang, Oya Beyan, Zeyd Boukhers

entry.summary: Proposes Evolutionary Soups, a mixture-of-experts framework for multi-objective LLM alignment where per-layer gating networks produce expert-merging coefficients from hidden states and are trained via an evolutionary algorithm with greedy hypervolume contribution. Enables inference-time, prompt-conditional trade-off control without retraining.

entry.title: Gurukul AI: An Interactive AI-Driven Educational Platform for Indian Education System

author.name: Isha Narang, Sneh Gosai, Mayank Singh

entry.summary: Proposes STAGEET, a stage-wise typed edit-tagging framework for grammatical error correction that decomposes correction into ordered stages with typed label spaces, evaluated on Arabic. Improves interpretability over single-vocabulary Seq2Edit approaches.

entry.title: GreenBench: Benchmarking Energy Efficiency and Carbon Footprint of Open-Source LLM Inference on Apple Silicon

author.name: Rajeswari Kannan, Raj Firke, Shreya Bengle, Srushti Deshmukh

entry.summary: Presents GreenBench, benchmarking energy efficiency, throughput, and carbon footprint of five 3-9B open-source LLMs on an Apple M4 Pro using direct powermetrics measurement. Finds remarkably low package power draw during sustained inference, filling a gap in Green AI literature beyond datacenter GPUs.

entry.title: AI Historian: Helping historians organize and verify person-centred temporal clues from dispersed historical narratives

author.name: Yifeng Lu, Zijie Yang, Jie Li, Qingkai Min, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: Presents AI Historian, an agent system helping historians organize person-time evidence from dispersed biographical narratives, with verification of cross-text associations and traceable source citations. Evaluated on six Shiji cases concerning Liu Bang and Xiang Yu.

entry.title: Anchoring Speech with Semantics: A Multimodal Adapter Mechanism for Automatic Speech Recognition in Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Kuan-Tang Huang, Cheng-Yeh Yang, Chien-Chun Wang, Hung-Shin Lee, Hsin-Min Wang, Berlin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SAMA-ASR, a lightweight adapter mechanism for low-resource ASR that conditions decoder states on semantic anchors from auxiliary translations plus an acoustic anchor, applicable to encoder-decoder multitask speech models.

entry.title: Large Language Models Systematically Favor Popular Options: Evidence and Mitigation Across MCQs

author.name: Abdelrahman Abdallah, Mohammed Ali, Bhawna Piryani, Mahmoud Abdalla, Adam Jatowt

entry.summary: Proposes ReVA, a region-aware VQA model connecting a frozen CLIP ViT and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct through a dual bridge aligning whole-image and region-level representations with the LLM. Targets object, attribute, and spatial hallucinations from insufficient region-level grounding.

entry.title: Language-Statistical Analysis of Neural Audio Codec Tokens Across Architectures, Corpora, and Noise Conditions

author.name: Joonyong Park, Shinnosuke Takamichi, David M. Chan, Shunsuke Kando, Yuki Saito, Hiroshi Saruwatari

entry.summary: This work analyzes language-like statistics of token sequences from 13 neural audio codecs across architectures, corpora, and noise conditions, measuring Zipf and Heaps parameters, entropy, codebook occupancy, and Jensen-Shannon divergence. It finds corpus identity explains little variance while acoustic condition and quantizer meta-category dominate. The result clarifies what actually drives token distributional structure in audio codecs.

entry.title: Configurable Semantic Chunking for Biomedical Information Extraction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Riya Ahuja (Institute of Data Science in Biomedicine, TU Braunschweig, Braunschweig, Germany, Braunschweig Integrated Centre of Systems Biology, TU Braunschweig, Braunschweig, Germany), Tim Kacprowski (Institute of Data Science in Biomedicine, TU Braunschweig, Braunschweig, Germany, Braunschweig Integrated Centre of Systems Biology, TU Braunschweig, Braunschweig, Germany), Roya Shiasi Sardoabi (Institute of Data Science in Biomedicine, TU Braunschweig, Braunschweig, Germany, Braunschweig Integrated Centre of Systems Biology, TU Braunschweig, Braunschweig, Germany)

entry.summary: This paper proposes a configurable semantic chunking framework that replaces only the chunk construction stage of BioMedRAG, combining entity-preserving windows, trigger-centered chunking, proposition-first extraction, and hierarchical relation resolution. It evaluates on biomedical relation extraction benchmarks including GM-CIHT, DDI, and ChemProt. The contribution is a modular improvement over fixed-size chunking for biomedical RAG.

entry.title: RENSA: Rich Environment Metadata to Navigate Shared and Distributed Endpoints for Automated Federated SPARQL Query Generation

author.name: Victor Eiti Yamamoto, Takeda Hideaki, Yamamoto Yasunori

entry.summary: RENSA proposes a federated SPARQL query generation framework leveraging rich environment metadata to navigate shared and distributed endpoints, moving beyond basic VoID metadata and runtime ASK queries for source selection. It aims to reduce communication overhead in federated knowledge graph querying. The contribution targets an infrastructure problem in the knowledge graph ecosystem.

entry.title: EmoLASP: Emotion Recognition with Language Models and Answer Set Programming

author.name: Thao Le, Michael Thielscher

entry.summary: EmoLASP combines language models with Answer Set Programming for emotion recognition in conversations, predicting VAD scores without requiring dialogue history in prompts. Across six open-source LLMs (3B-120B) and two PLMs on IEMOCAP, the hybrid improves prediction over the model alone, with the largest gains for prompt-only LLMs. It shows declarative reasoning can substitute for context in emotion tasks.

entry.title: Conducting Stylistic Analysis of Paintings through an Art-History Agent

author.name: Marc S. Walton, Astrid Harth

entry.summary: This paper presents an art-history agent that automates stylistic analysis of paintings, training a vision transformer on a large annotated painting corpus and factorizing embeddings via sparse dictionary learning into interpretable recurring features. It aims to bridge unexplained probabilistic attribution with traditional evidence-based stylistic analysis. The work applies interpretability-style factorization to a humanities domain.

entry.title: SpanCalib-VLM: Calibrated Hallucination Span Detection in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Amanuel Gizachew Abebe, Yasmin Moslem

entry.summary: SpanCalib-VLM is a hybrid dual-system for hallucination span detection in vision-language models, combining an XLM-RoBERTa-Large tagger fused with a SigLIP vision encoder and a fine-tuned generative VLM (Qwen3.5-4B), unified through a Union-Calibrated Fusion strategy. It balances generative span recall against tagger calibration and speed. The system was built for the SHROOM-Visions shared task.

entry.title: Towards a Joint Khmer Text Recognition and Word Segmentation

author.name: Marry Kong, Rina Buoy, Sovisal Chenda, Nguonly Taing, Masakazu Iwamura, Koichi Kise

entry.summary: Proposes a unified model performing joint Khmer text recognition and word segmentation, avoiding error-prone two-stage pipelines for a language without visible word delimiters. Uses a CTC decoder for fast parallel decoding, aiding large-scale document processing and RAG for Khmer. Valuable for low-resource language NLP.

entry.title: Improving Spatial-Temporal Reasoning in Video-Language Models with Structured Video Prompting

author.name: Sadegh Mohammadian

entry.summary: Introduces structured video prompting, a training-free inference-time method that adds lightweight spatial and temporal structure to input videos to improve spatial-temporal reasoning in video-language models without changing weights. Shows gains on two benchmarks with two open VLMs. Simple, broadly applicable idea.

entry.title: FLM: Frequency-Aware Language Models for Generative Image Compression

author.name: Jiarun Chen, Kejun Wu, Li Li, Chengtao Cai, Zhengguo Li, Chia-Wen Lin

entry.summary: FLM is a frequency-aware language model for generative image compression that performs next-coefficient prediction over DCT coefficient token sequences, improving low-bitrate compression while retaining deterministic reconstruction. Interesting cross-pollination of autoregressive language modeling and image coding.

entry.title: Towards Fully Automated Medical Imaging Code Generation via Validation-based Context Engineering

author.name: Zixiao Zhao, Jing Sun, Zhe Hou, Cheng-Hao Cai, Qian Liu, Mengze Li, Zijian Zhang, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: AutoMedImg is a multi-agent framework for fully automated medical image processing code generation, orchestrating specialized agents across planning and implementation phases with validation-based context engineering to handle domain-specific correctness. Practical step toward reliable domain-specific code generation.

entry.title: NFAD: Nuisance-Filtered Anomaly Detection Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Dat Cao, Son Nghiem, Phan Nguyen, Jun Rekimoto, Jhih-Ciang Wu

entry.summary: NFAD addresses industrial anomaly detection under distribution shift by explicitly modeling nuisance variation (illumination, background, viewpoint) in feature space without anomaly labels or target-domain data, filtering nuisances to avoid false anomaly responses from real-world imaging changes. Practical robustness contribution for deployment.

entry.title: Dancing Stick Figures: An Introductory Dataset for Training Video Generation Models

author.name: Jin Hyuk Cho

entry.summary: Dancing Stick Figures is a synthetic 64x64, 64-frame video dataset designed for fast, accessible, and diagnostically clear iteration when training video generation models from scratch on a single workstation GPU. Addresses the long feedback loop, inaccessible data, and blunt scoring that hinder video-generation research. Valuable community resource, especially for education and low-resource labs.

entry.title: RLG-TPV: Radar- and LiDAR-Guided Tri-Perspective View Fusion for Camera-Radar 3D Object Detection

author.name: Ahmet Mete Dokgoz, A. Enes Doruk, Hasan F. Ates

entry.summary: RLG-TPV fuses radar and LiDAR guidance into tri-perspective view representations for camera-radar 3D object detection, using ray-guided deformable attention to resolve depth ambiguity along camera rays. LiDAR supervision compensates for radar's weak elevation information. This targets cost-effective automotive sensing without LiDAR at inference.

entry.title: PERSIST: Persistent-State Discrimination for Shot Boundary Detection

author.name: Tingyu Lin, Christian Stippel, Armin Dadras, Jakob Zenzmaier, Florian Kleber, Wolfgang Aigner, Robert Sablatnig

entry.summary: PERSIST reformulates shot boundary detection as boundary semantic discrimination, accepting a cut only when local change coincides with a persistent update of the video latent temporal state. A FiLM-conditioned sinusoidal state network and structured discriminator suppress false positives from shake, flicker, and damaged footage. Particularly valuable for archival video material.

entry.title: Co-Evolutionary Prompt Optimization with Cross-Category Transfer for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Sisi Zhu, Changwei Yu, Renshuai Tao, Zhenliang Ni

entry.summary: CoEvoAD performs zero-shot anomaly detection via co-evolutionary discrete prompt optimization in natural language space, preserving interpretability and cross-category transfer versus continuous prompt embeddings. An evolutionary loop generates, evaluates, and selects candidate prompts for CLIP-based detection. A sensible alternative to latent prompt tuning.

entry.title: FIS-OT: Feature-Induced Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Action Segmentation

author.name: Linxiang Peng, Xinyao Qin, Jinhan Li, Di Yang, Jiangtao Wang

entry.summary: FIS-OT improves unsupervised action segmentation with a feature-induced structured optimal transport framework that injects local consistency via triplet loss and mitigates confirmation bias from noisy pseudo-labels. Tackles a known weakness of global-constraint OT methods.

entry.title: ATGS: Anchored Temporal Gaussian Splatting for Long Volumetric Video Representation

author.name: Jiahao Wu, Jie Liang, Die Hu, Jiayu Yang, Kaiqiang Xiong, Xiang Li, Xiaoyun Zheng, Chao Wang, Ronggang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces CedarCypress3D, a manually annotated UAV-LiDAR dataset of individual trees in Japanese cedar and cypress plantations for tree segmentation. Fills a gap in publicly available annotated temperate-forest point cloud datasets.

entry.title: Motion-Saliency Complementary Masked Modeling for Point Cloud Video Understanding

author.name: Wei Wang, Yiding Sun, Yuyan Wang, Zhuoyue Zhang, Zhengqiao Li, Dongfu Yin, Chen Li

entry.summary: MoSaiC is a self-supervised masked modeling framework for point cloud video understanding combining curriculum motion-saliency masking, Lie-algebra normal-flow motion targets, and cross-view token consistency. Advances 3D dynamic scene representation.

entry.title: Learning to Restore More: Continual Capability Expansion for Pretrained Image Restoration Models

author.name: Hu Gao, Yulong Chen, Lizhuang Ma

entry.summary: RestoreMore enables continual capability expansion of pretrained image restoration models via a frozen capability anchor plus residual expansion modules with bi-level routing, avoiding joint retraining. Addresses catastrophic forgetting in restoration.
