entry.summary: Synth-JDoc introduces a synthetic Japanese document image dataset for OCR training that handles vertically and horizontally written text plus embedded images, generated by rendering text onto realistic layouts. It targets the documented weakness of LVLMs on vertical Japanese text, where high-quality OCR data is scarce and manual annotation is costly.

entry.title: ShiftSplit-AD: Separating Domain Shift from Defects in Foundation-Feature Visual Anomaly Detection

author.name: Muhamathu Ameer Ali Aacaas Muhamath

entry.summary: BEACON constructs cross-source knowledge graphs for cyber threat intelligence by anchoring entity resolution on MITRE ATT&CK attack behaviors, solving the problem of the same threat appearing under different names across reports. This enables integrating information that single-report extraction methods cannot connect.

entry.title: DensityKV: Density-Guided KV Cache Compression for Long Video Generation

author.name: Wenqu Zhao, Xuemin Chi, Xin Zhang, Guoqing Ma, Baorun Li, Jianjie Fang, Peizhi Tang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu

entry.summary: ShiftSplit-AD examines whether decomposing nearest-normal DINOv2 residuals into low-rank and row-sparse components can separate benign domain shift from true visual defects in anomaly detection. The honest headline finding is a trade-off rather than a clean separation, since real defects can themselves be low-rank.

entry.title: A-PAIR: A Benchmark and Identity-Consistent Grounding Framework for Air-Ground Cross-View Referring Person Detection

author.name: Zhoupeng Guo, Xinjie Yao, Yunqi Zhu, Zhihe Fan, Siqi Zhao, Jianjun Chen, Yichen Dong, Yan Fan, Pengfei Zhu

entry.summary: A-PAIR introduces the first benchmark for air-ground cross-view referring person detection, requiring language commands to ground the same physical identity across aerial and ground views despite weak aerial cues and similar distractors, plus an identity-consistent grounding framework.

entry.title: 3D-USE: From Image-Level to Scene-Level Underwater Enhancement

author.name: Jieyu Yuan, Yuanlin Zhang, Jihong Li, Chunle Guo, Huimin Lu, Chongyi Li

entry.summary: 3D-USE formulates underwater scene-level enhancement as learning a persistent, visibility-enhanced 3D scene representation from degraded multi-view observations, using a medium-aware Gaussian representation and consistent enhancement targets without paired enhanced 3D data.

entry.title: A Controlled Audit of Architectural Complexity in Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Organ Ultrasound Classification

author.name: Yang Song, Pengbo Sun, Shichang Feng, Ye Zhu, Xin Xu, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: This paper conducts a controlled audit of architectural complexity in uncertainty-aware multi-organ ultrasound classification, comparing six candidates across matched seeds, frozen partitions, and paired decision rules to test whether added components like MoE routing and evidential objectives actually help deployment decisions.

entry.title: Task-State Adaptation with Prototype Memory for Multi-Task Dense Prediction

author.name: Yangyang Xu, Haobo Yuan, Yuzhu Wang, Duo Su, Xi Ye, Yibo Yang, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: MemMTL is a multi-task dense prediction framework that estimates a compact task state from global context and refines it via a learnable prototype memory, producing task-conditioned expert logits combined with token-level logits under sparse top-k selection over a shared expert bank.

entry.title: Manifold4D: Denoising on Point Cloud Rendered Manifolds for Video Re-shooting

author.name: Yongqi Mao, Zijia Dai, Zhishuo Liu, Wei Xu, Kaiwei Wang, Guotao Meng

entry.summary: Manifold4D addresses video re-shooting by denoising on point-cloud rendered manifolds, arguing that pixel-aligned renders need not be supplied as an explicit conditioning stream, which resolves the trust dilemma between render and source video in diffusion-based camera-controllable video editing.

entry.title: RASA: Disentangled Spatial-Motional Priors for Cross-Identity Character Animation

author.name: Zhen Xiao, Zhen Shen, Zhaofan Qiu, Ting Yao, Xueliang Liu, Tao Mei

entry.summary: RASA disentangles cross-identity spatial mapping from motion control in character animation via structured priors injected into a Diffusion Transformer, using a spatial prior calibrator followed by motion refinement for reference-driven animation.

entry.title: Non-Uniform Quantisation for 3DGS Compression

author.name: Bert Van hauwermeiren, Patrice Rondao Alface, Adrian Munteanu

entry.summary: This paper proposes importance-weighted non-uniform quantisation with redundancy-eliminating merging for compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting models, achieving state-of-the-art compression on benchmarks and supporting interoperability for standardized 3DGS formats.

entry.title: Conditional Visual Evidence Utility: State-Dependent Rank Reversals in Frozen Vision-Language Encoders

author.name: Yunxuan Fang, Xinhe Wang

entry.summary: This analysis paper shows that frozen OpenCLIP and SigLIP encoders exhibit state-dependent rank reversals in the conditional utility of visual evidence during compositional visual search, with the effect robust across evidence constructions and query paraphrases but vanishing under derangement controls.

entry.title: DeicticVLA: Unifying Instruction Modes Based on Language and Deictic Gestures in a Single VLA

author.name: Kango Yanagida, Tatsuya Aoki, Yuichiro Yoshikawa, Takato Horii

entry.summary: DeicticVLA unifies language, vision-language, and visual instruction modes for robot manipulation in a single pretrained VLA by canonicalizing them into text prompts and deictic gesture masks, enabling pointing-based disambiguation among similar objects without mode-specific models.

entry.title: CASTANET: Causality-Aware Spatio-Temporal Adversarial Network Using Traffic Incident Effects

author.name: Toshiya Kitahara, Ryu Shirakami, Koh Takeuchi, Hisashi Kashima

entry.summary: CASTANET integrates spatio-temporal GNNs with causality-aware adversarial modeling of incident effects to predict non-periodic traffic congestion from sparse, spatially biased incident records.

entry.title: Cross-Spectral Dense Correspondence for Multimodal Spectral Medical Imaging

author.name: Eric L. Wisotzky, Jost Triller, Simon W. H\"artl, Oliver T. Bruns, Peter Eisert, Anna Hilsmann

entry.summary: Addresses dense correspondence across non-overlapping spectral ranges in multimodal medical imaging via a sensor-agnostic cross-spectral modulation protocol and a synthetic benchmark, enabling supervision where ground truth is scarce.

entry.title: SegBench-GC: Testing Segmentation Invariance in Multi-Step Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Musa Shams

entry.summary: Introduces SegBench-GC, a controlled stress test of segmentation invariance in offline goal-conditioned RL, holding everything fixed while varying artificial backup boundaries and continuation-valid targets, showing segmentation artifacts affect multi-step GCRL.

entry.title: Automated Analysis Framework for Multilingual Climate-Health Literature Based on Multi-Agent Large Language Model

author.name: Yuze Sun, Shihui Zhang, Jiancheng Pan, Yunjia Ye, Wentao Luo, Jiahao Li, Quan Zhang, Wenjia Cai, Xiaomeng Huang

entry.summary: A multi-agent LLM framework automating multilingual climate-health literature analysis end to end: screening, structured extraction, and standardized integration via a central coordinator and three specialized agents.

entry.title: DART-FL: Burst-Aware Multitask Federated Learning under Dynamic Inference Demand at the Edge

author.name: Yiming Xie, Pinrui Yu, Geng Yuan, Xue Lin, Ningfang Mi

entry.summary: DART-FL is an SLO-aware multitask federated learning framework for edge devices that jointly adapts the inference-training resource split and task-level training emphasis under dynamic, bursty inference demand.

entry.title: TI$^2$PS: A Topology-Informed Inverse Design Framework for Stochastic Multicellular Pattern Formation

author.name: Kenji Komiya, Andrew Kailiang Jin, Ryo Nishikimi, Kunio Kashino

entry.summary: TI2PS is a topology-informed inverse design framework estimating agent-based model parameters for target multicellular pattern formation, combining Betti vectors from topological data analysis with inverse surrogate modeling.

entry.title: Efficient Online Continual Foundation Model Fine-Tuning for Predictive Process Monitoring

author.name: Sjoerd van Straten, Marwan Hassani

entry.summary: COMPASS is the first framework for online continual fine-tuning of foundation models for predictive process monitoring, using loss-plateau drift detection to identify task boundaries and adaptive subspace updates to handle concept drift.

entry.title: Picking Bins Empty: A Hierarchical Hybrid Approach with Online Self-Learning of Grasp Points for Reliable Industrial Bin-Picking

author.name: Florian T\"oper, Samarth Kishor Yelvande, Jan Niklas Ewertz, Rudolph Triebel, Peter Ohlhausen

entry.summary: The paper presents a four-tiered hierarchical hybrid system for industrial bin-picking that combines model-based precision with model-free grasp flexibility, including online self-learning of grasp points to avoid deadlocks and achieve complete bin clearance. It targets a real manufacturing pain point where neither approach alone achieves reliability plus versatility. The engineering contribution is significant for production deployment.

entry.title: Not All Explanations Are Sought: Information-Seeking Psychology for Human-Centered XAI

author.name: Andrea Beretta, Salvatore Rinzivillo

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that human-centered explainable AI should incorporate the psychology of information seeking, modeling whether users engage with explanations via instrumental, hedonic, and cognitive expected utilities shaped by cognitive biases. Identifies failure modes of both excessive and insufficient information-seeking.

entry.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Cross-City POI Recommendation on a Large-Scale Benchmark

author.name: Peibo Li, Yang Song, Hao Xue, Maarten de Rijke, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: Re-evaluates cross-city POI recommendation on the large-scale Trip World benchmark, finding that hometown-aware models rely more on destination priors than user preference transfer, and that the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff degrades at scale where the simplest model remains competitive.

entry.title: GOD: Govern, Observe, and Direct - A Real-Time Control Room for Agent Societies

author.name: Yige Luo, Ran Guan

entry.summary: GOD is a local-first control room for generative-agent societies combining setup, spatial replay, targeted questions, and live interventions through a command-and-artifact loop, making runs inspectable and portable for operators and researchers.

entry.title: Expert Knowledge & Machine Understanding: Bridging Reactome's Ontology with LLM Semantic Embeddings

author.name: Susanna Bravi, Riccardo De Luca, Rosa Sicilia, Christine Nardini, Mario Santoro

entry.summary: Tests whether LLM semantic embeddings of Reactome's expert-written pathway descriptions recover the manually curated global hierarchical structure, probing whether textual metadata mirrors higher-order biological relationships.

entry.title: Regime-Aware Portfolio Management via Retrieval-Augmented LLM-Guided Expert Switching

author.name: Ahmad Asadi, Reza Safabakhsh

entry.summary: Retrieval-augmented LLM-guided expert switching for portfolio management under regime changes, using a dual-stream VAE and a retrieval base of historical expert performance, with an LLM reasoning over evidence rather than directly generating actions, plus a monotonicity property.

entry.title: Learning to Use Tools: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Integrated Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Minghui Xu, Zi Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies calculator tool calling for mathematical reasoning on the Countdown task, analyzing reasoning failures and building SFT datasets for tool-use patterns before applying on-policy RL methods including RLOO, GRPO, and DAPO with verifiable rewards. It also introduces more reliable evaluation of tool-integrated reasoning.

entry.title: Training-free Suction Grasp Detection for Deformed Aseptic Cartons Using Vision-Language Models and Geometric Surface Scoring

author.name: Marin Maletic, Goran Vasiljevic

entry.summary: A training-free robotic system for sorting deformed aseptic cartons combining an open-vocabulary VLM for detection, SAM2 for masking, and geometric surface scoring for suction-point selection. Validated on a real robot across deformation levels and cluttered scenes.

entry.title: Unsupervised Continual Learning with Growing Self-Organizing Maps and Synthetic Replay

author.name: Pujan Thapa, Alexander Ororbia, Travis Desell

entry.summary: Presents an unsupervised continual learning framework using growing self-organizing maps with distributional statistics for exemplar-free synthetic replay, eliminating raw data storage without requiring task boundaries or labels.

entry.title: Conditional Diffusion Models for Energy-Efficient Driving

author.name: Hemanth Neelgund Ramesh, Andr\'e Snoeck, Chyi-Fu Hong, Shijing Sun

entry.summary: A conditional diffusion framework generating EV battery-current profiles conditioned on route features (velocity, temperature) for energy-aware delivery fleet routing, providing distributional trajectories rather than point estimates for operational decisions.

entry.title: D-TAIA: Domain-Aware LLM Adaptation for Multi-Task Predictive Process Monitoring

author.name: Sjoerd van Straten, Christine Jacob, Marwan Hassani

entry.summary: D-TAIA adapts LLMs for multi-task predictive process monitoring under data scarcity, high process entropy, and distribution shift, using domain-aware training and inference-time adaptation rather than direct regression heads.

entry.title: Advancing Interaction-Sensitive Feature Selection: Novel Relief-Based Algorithms, Expanded Comparisons, and Recommendations for Biomedical Data Mining

author.name: Kia Kazemi-Nia, Harsh Bandhey, Philip J. Freda, Ryan J. Urbanowicz

entry.summary: This work refactors and expands the scikit-rebate package of Relief-based feature selection algorithms and benchmarks them rigorously on genomic simulation data, offering recommendations for biomedical data mining where feature interactions matter.

entry.title: Physics-informed learning for the inverse problem in resonant ultrasound spectroscopy

author.name: Alejandro Cubillos Mu\~noz, Manuela Rivas, Julian Rincon

entry.summary: The paper formulates the inverse problem in resonant ultrasound spectroscopy as a constrained inverse-isospectral problem and builds a physics-informed learning pipeline that regresses on reduced spectral and geometric features before reconstructing elastic constants.

entry.title: A Shaky Voice Is Not Always a Dodge: Benchmarking Textual and Vocal Evasion Detection in Earnings Calls

author.name: Mirae Kim, Seonghun Jeong, Youngjun Kwak

entry.summary: DualEvasion is a benchmark of 505 annotated earnings-call QA pairs with independent textual evasion and vocal confidence labels, showing that vocal cues carry complementary evasion signal beyond transcripts and that state-of-the-art multimodal models still struggle.

entry.title: Phoneme- and Word-Level Metrics Using Self-Supervised Speech Representations for Forced Alignment Evaluation

author.name: V. S. D. S. Mahesh Akavarapu, Michael Daniel, Gerhard J\"ager

entry.summary: The paper introduces two reference-free corpus-level metrics (PCMI and WACS) based on self-supervised speech representations for evaluating forced alignment without manual timestamp annotations, validated under random and systematic perturbations.

entry.title: GAAT: Geometry-Aware Alignment Transformer for Multimodal UAV Perception

author.name: Jingpu Yang, Debin Tang, Yilin Sun, Fengxian Ji, Jiahua Zhu, Wenrui Ding, Yufeng Wang

entry.summary: GAAT is a geometry-aware alignment transformer for UAV multimodal perception that estimates local correspondence reliability before cross-modal interaction across RGB, infrared, SAR, and depth, handling parallax, platform motion, and lens distortion that break token alignment.

entry.title: Ex-Sim(3)-Reg: 2D-3D Correspondence Pruning via Extended Sim(3) Registration

author.name: Pei An, Muyao Peng, Junfeng Ding, Jiaqi Yang, Liangliang Nan

entry.summary: Ex-Sim(3)-Reg recasts 2D-3D correspondence pruning as an extended Sim(3) registration problem that explicitly models noisy monocular depth priors, improving robustness on unseen, low-inlier, and distorted cases.

entry.title: Dual-Stream Semantic Guidance with Prototype Anchor Calibration for Source-Fully-Free Adaptation of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weiwei Xiang, Shun Peng, Guangyi Xiao, Hao Chen, Lei Yang

entry.summary: DSSG tackles source-fully-free domain adaptation of VLMs by identifying a dual semantic drift problem, fixed class embeddings plus drifting generated captions, and resolving it with a dual-stream module balancing caption-based plasticity against global stability.

entry.title: GeoFF3D: Coordinate-Anchored Feed-Forward Reconstruction for Large-Scale UAV Mapping

author.name: Xiang Yang, Yongli Wang, Yunsheng Zhang

entry.summary: GeoFF3D combines a coordinate-anchored feed-forward reconstruction model predicting gravity-aligned metric poses and point maps with a spatial chunked aggregation framework, targeting large-scale UAV mapping where Sim(3) alignment becomes unstable on near-collinear trajectories.

entry.title: Abstract4D: A Large-Scale Dataset and Framework for Understanding the Visual Language of Abstract Art

author.name: Haowei Zhang, Yuanpei Zhao, Ji-Zhe Zhou, Mao Li

entry.summary: Abstract4D is the largest dataset of abstract paintings to date, over 120,000 images with multi-dimensional perceptual annotations produced by a hybrid human-VLM pipeline, used to analyze the semantic structure of abstract art and support downstream modeling of its visual language.

entry.title: Denoising-Aware Temporal Point Cloud Completion for 3D Crop Architecture Recovery and Phenotypic Trait Extraction

author.name: Mrudul Mittal, Soumyashree Kar

entry.summary: This paper introduces SynthCrop4D, a procedurally generated synthetic dataset of temporally evolving plant point clouds with controllable noise and complete geometry, plus a two-stage denoising and temporal completion pipeline for crop architecture recovery and phenotyping.

entry.title: Lossy Event Compression: From Event Stream Distortion to Task Performance

author.name: Zahra Rezaee, Catarina Brites, Jo\~ao Ascenso

entry.summary: This work introduces two lossy event-camera compression pipelines, one histogram-based and one stream-based, and studies how event stream distortion metrics relate to task-level performance, addressing the gap that existing metrics poorly predict downstream degradation.

entry.title: GeBDA: Building Damage Assessment as Text-Based Sequence Prediction

author.name: Olivier Dietrich, Krishna Sapkota, Konrad Schindler, Genady Beryozkin

entry.summary: GeBDA casts building damage assessment from bi-temporal satellite imagery as autoregressive text-based sequence prediction of variable-length bounding box sets with damage labels, using an open Gemma model and a suitable prompt without dedicated architectures.

entry.title: SignRR: Retrieve and Refine Real Motion for Sign Language Production

author.name: Fidel Omar Tito Cruz, Angie Sanchez Marquina, Summy Farfan, Gissella Bejarano

entry.summary: SignRR combines retrieval of real sign language motion segments with learned refinement to fix rhythm and style inconsistencies when concatenating across signers, aiming to preserve rare hand configurations in sign language production.

entry.title: Ada-TokenCom: Rate-Adaptive Token Communications via Large-Model-Driven Token Compression and Generation

author.name: Zijun Zhang, Li Qiao, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Zhen Gao, Mehdi Bennis, Kaibin Huang

entry.summary: Ada-TokenCom develops rate-adaptive token communications where an autoregressive large model transmits only highly informative leading tokens and the receiver predicts the rest, integrating next-token prediction with arithmetic coding for ultra-low bitrate semantic transmission.

entry.title: Generalized Context in Cross Attention for Transfer Learning of Disjoint Tabular Data

author.name: Kazi F. Akhter, Ibna Kowsar, Manar D. Samad

entry.summary: Introduces generalized context learning for transfer between tabular domains with disjoint features, using transformer projection weight interactions (source key with target query) to provide rule-based generalization without shared features.

entry.title: CareGraph: An Auditable Hybrid AI Framework for Evidence-Grounded Personalized Longitudinal Health Intelligence

author.name: Pratik Ghawate, Tanvi Patil

entry.summary: Presents CareGraph, an auditable hybrid AI framework that converts heterogeneous clinical, self-reported, and wearable records into prioritized trends, provenance-linked explanations, and bounded next steps without making autonomous clinical decisions. Includes deterministic analysis, graph construction, constrained LLM synthesis, and release gating, tested on synthetic 400-patient cohorts.

entry.title: Agents for Everyone: A Workshop Framework for Building Agentic AI Capabilities in a Distributed Curation Community

author.name: Seth Carbon, Sierra Moxon, Kimberly Van Auken, Pascale Gaudet, Christopher J. Mungall

entry.summary: Describes a cloud-based JupyterHub agentic environment using Claude Code as a universal harness, plus an interactive workshop, to bring agentic AI curation to the Gene Ontology Consortium's distributed community. Focuses on access, training, and centralized deployment for domain curators.

entry.title: COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing

author.name: Raghul Sugumar, Amrit Gopinath

entry.summary: COVER introduces an evaluation contract for multi-agent coalition routing that fixes an information boundary and legal team family before outcomes are generated, enabling identifiable estimation of oracle regret and policy contrasts. It validates the instrument with controlled tables on MuSiQue-12.

entry.title: SafeStep: An Interactive Demonstration of Semantic Communication for Pedestrian Safety Monitoring

author.name: Christian McDowell, Andrea Panebianco, Jeremiah Yang, Sirin Chakraborty, Samuel Chamoun, Travis Ross, Yin Sun

entry.summary: SafeStep is an interactive browser-based semantic communication platform for live pedestrian safety monitoring, comparing a recent semantic design (Meta-VIB) against baselines over an AWGN channel with selectable SNR, codelength, and Age of Information.

entry.title: Initialization Is Critical: Advancing Federated Short-Term Load Forecasting under Load Heterogeneity via Model Initialization

author.name: Jianing Chen, Vajiheh Farhadi, Yan Li, Thomas La Porta

entry.summary: Studies model initialization as a lever for federated short-term load forecasting under structured load heterogeneity, proposing global and personalized initialization strategies to mitigate client differences in exogenous responses and temporal profiles.

entry.title: Residual-Guided Randomized Neural Networks

author.name: Mushir Akhtar, M. Tanveer, Mohd. Arshad

entry.summary: Proposes residual-guided randomized neural networks that greedily construct hidden units by exact ridge-regularized residual reduction from candidate pools, addressing the suboptimality of a single uninformed random draw in randomized networks.

entry.title: Synthetic Linguistic Agency: How an Embodied Mortal Agent Learns Linguistic Affordances through Consequential Social Experience

author.name: Sixin Chen, Taizhou Chen

entry.summary: This position-style paper formalizes Synthetic Linguistic Agency (SLA) via embodiment, linguistic participation, and precariousness, identifies existing systems meeting these criteria, and studies an HRL-based embodied mortal agent that learns linguistic affordances through consequential social experience.

entry.title: Stranger, Fan, or Peer? A Systematic Study on the Role of Interlocutor in Persona-Based Dialogue Generation

author.name: Daniela Occhipinti, Malvina Nissim, Marco Guerini

entry.summary: This systematic study factorizes biography visibility in persona-based dialogue into target and interlocutor access across training, inference, and evaluation stages, revealing mechanisms obscured when visibility is treated as a single factor.

entry.title: Image Augmentation as Test Generation for Deep Learning-Based Image Retrieval Systems

author.name: Yehan De Silva, Anirudh Sridhar, Armin Lotfy, Nafiseh Kahani, Yvan Labiche, Ziyu Wang, Frank Ouyang, Clare Carty, Azalia Shamsaei

entry.summary: This paper reviews 50 augmentation and generation techniques organized into a ten-category taxonomy and evaluates them as test generators for deep learning-based image retrieval systems across embedding similarity, uncertainty, realism, and failure rate dimensions.

entry.title: Memory-efficient GPU pipelines for real-time non-line-of-sight reconstruction

author.name: Alfonso L\'opez-Ruiz, Diego Royo

entry.summary: This paper rebuilds GPU pipelines for non-line-of-sight reconstruction, assembling analytic ring kernels offline so propagation kernels never exist densely at runtime, achieving memory-efficient real-time f-k migration and phasor-field reconstruction as SPAD throughput grows.

entry.title: Stay Seated: Learning Omnidirectional Humanoid Locomotion on a Passive Mobile Chair with Casters

author.name: Kango Yanagida, Kazuki Miyazawa, Takato Horii

entry.summary: This paper trains policies for omnidirectional seated locomotion of a humanoid on a passive caster-equipped mobile chair, extending RL environments with seated-state rewards and contact settings learned without motion-imitation rewards. It frames seated loco-manipulation as a first step toward energy-efficient humanoid behaviors analogous to human desk work. It is an early-stage but creative exploration of an underexplored locomotion mode.

entry.title: Class-Based Heuristic Selection for Solving the Flying Block Puzzle

author.name: Sanyar Ahmadi, Pedram Asadzadeh, Amanj Khorramian

entry.summary: Presents CBHA*, a class-based heuristic A* algorithm for the NP-complete Flying Block Puzzle microworld, with a General Move Constraint capturing minimum displacement costs under scarce clearance. The bottleneck geometry mirrors clearance constraints in MAPF and warehouse robotics.

entry.title: Real-Valued Hyperdimensional Sequence Representations with Hadamard Product Binding and Shift Equivariance

author.name: Kenny Schlegel, Dmitri A. Rachkovskij, Denis Kleyko, Amy Loutfi, Stefan Streif, Evgeny Osipov

entry.summary: This paper develops real-valued position encodings for hyperdimensional computing that retain the shift-equivariant, similarity-preserving properties of Fractional Power Encoding while remaining compatible with Hadamard product binding. It is motivated by Random Fourier Features and targets efficient sequence representation.

entry.title: AI as Teammate: Rethinking Task Distribution in Medical Training

author.name: Fendi Tsim, Alina Gutoreva, Anthony Weiss, Nicole Dubosh

entry.summary: A conceptual position paper reframing AI misuse in medical training as misclassification of interaction mode, proposing the SCAN framework (Substitute, Complement, Aid, Non-Negotiable) grounded in Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development for AI task allocation in education.

entry.title: Explainable Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Using Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Abhishek Verma, Anila Krishna, Abhishek Gajanan Bankar, Juan Miguel Lopez Alcaraz

entry.summary: An explainable diabetic retinopathy classification study comparing DINOv2, CLIP, and ViT backbones with fine-tuning, linear probing, and LoRA across internal (ODIR) and external (APTOS) evaluation, with DINOv2 variants performing best.

entry.title: GAN-Based Semantic Communication for Image Transmission in IoV

author.name: Ruixing Ren, Shan Chen, Junhui Zhao, Xiaoke Sun

entry.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based semantic communication framework for image transmission in the internet of vehicles, using a pyramid attention network and safety-driven semantic weighting to allocate bandwidth toward driving-critical content, reconstructed at the receiver with a coarse-to-fine generator.

entry.title: CF-YOLO: Context-Aware Feature Refinement for Camouflaged Industrial Micro-Defect Detection

author.name: Xinda Yu, Kunxin Zheng, Chunan Yu, Qingbo Song, Hao Xiao, Ying Zang, Jie Liu

entry.summary: CF-YOLO targets camouflaged micro-defect detection on industrial components such as copper tubes using a context-perception aggregation module combining large-kernel context and small-kernel boundary refinement, plus feature refinement for real-time detection.

entry.title: From Small Talk to Rapport: Exploring Robot Self-Disclosure in Collaborative Tasks

author.name: Kaitlynn Taylor Pineda, Anvii Mishra, Brian Chien, Angela Guo, Toluwani Williams, Ziang Xiao, Chien-Ming Huang

entry.summary: This HRI study explores how robot-initiated self-disclosure in small talk builds rapport during human-robot collaborative tasks, using an LLM-driven industrial manipulator that lacks anthropomorphic cues. It provides design guidance for social behaviors in non-humanoid work robots. It matters as robots increasingly share workspaces with humans and engagement affects team performance.

entry.title: Generalized Gibbs Ensemble Weighting for Forecast Combination

author.name: Prasen R. Nuthanakaluva, Nava K. Gaddam

entry.summary: Proposes Generalized Gibbs Ensemble Weighting, a probabilistic forecast combination framework assigning ensemble weights via Gibbs-style transformations of normalized predictive loss, with stabilization and diversity-aware corrections.

entry.title: Generative AI Expands the Intellectual Reach of Course Based Undergraduate Research Experiences (CUREs)

author.name: Aditi Babar, Kristin J. Davin, Alex Dornburg

entry.summary: Longitudinal qualitative study across three semesters of a bioinformatics CURE showing that generative AI expanded the intellectual reach of undergraduate research experiences through personalized assistance, adapting support as student needs evolved.

entry.title: Logos: An Agent Harness on a Cross-Process Bus

author.name: Hanzhang Jia, Liheng Zeng, Hao Cheng, Yi Gao, Bo Ma

entry.summary: Logos implements an agent harness on a cross-process bus, extending a formal spatiotemporal-composability calculus so agent plugins need not share a single process failure domain. It shows the calculus soundness invariant applies across processes given the statelessness of language models.

entry.title: BanglaMed-QA: A Question Answering System for Healthcare Support in Bangla

author.name: Rowzatul Zannat, Abdullah Al Shafi, K. M. Azharul Hasan, Atia Shahnaz Ipa

entry.summary: BanglaMed-QA is a medical QA system for Bangla with a 4,493-pair knowledge base across 506 diseases, domain-specific dictionaries, synonym sets, and anaphora resolution, finding SVM the best supervised model. Addresses a genuine low-resource language gap in healthcare AI.

entry.title: A Framework for Object-Centric Predictive Monitoring of Collaborative Processes

author.name: Daniel Calegari, Andrea Delgado, Leonel Pe\~na, Mart\'in Rubio

entry.summary: Connects predictive process monitoring of collaborative inter-organizational processes with object-centric process mining via a formal semantic mapping to OCED-conformant representations, enabling multi-entity reasoning beyond the single-case perspective.

entry.title: An algebraic proof of Colombo's difference-power determinant conjecture

author.name: Kun Li, Li Tie, Peng Wang, Zihan Liu

entry.summary: This paper provides an algebraic proof of Colombo's 1928 conjecture on the nonsingularity of difference-power matrices for supercritical odd exponents, completing a nearly century-old open problem in linear algebra. It is pure mathematics posted under the machine learning category.

entry.title: What Do Interaction Representations Actually Measure? Pre-Event Separability in Weakly-Supervised Violence Detection

author.name: Parishruthi Ganesh

entry.summary: This study rigorously compares five interaction representations (bounding-box geometry through learned pose encoders) for weakly-supervised violence detection, holding the full pipeline fixed, and finds that no pose-based representation outperforms coarse geometry, raising questions about assumed benefits of articulated pose.

entry.title: What Will This Copper Look Like Later? Forecasting Surface Appearance and Rendering It as a PBR Material

author.name: Teejuta Sriwaranon, Borworntat Dendumrongkul, Tanapat Chamted, Pizzanu Kanongchaiyos

entry.summary: This paper builds a pipeline that forecasts the oxidation appearance of copper surfaces from fixed-camera observations and converts predictions into PBR material maps for rendering, evaluated under a strict held-out-specimen protocol.

entry.title: Remote Human and Robot Interaction for Greenhouse Gardening Using Virtual Reality

author.name: Daniel Udekwe, Hasan Seyyedhasani

entry.summary: This study evaluates remote human-robot interaction via VR teleoperation for greenhouse leaf inspection and soil moisture assessment using a ground vehicle and manipulator, reporting cycle times and up to 88 percent disease detection accuracy across two experiments with fourteen plants.

entry.title: SETU: An Agentic Ecosystem for Multilingual, Persona-Aware Communication Coaching

author.name: Jonnalagadda Maruthi Tejas, Uponika Barman Roy, Tilottama Goswami, Samir Goswami, Mousita Dhar

entry.summary: SETU is an agentic ecosystem for multilingual, persona-aware corporate communication coaching, decomposing scoring into auditable stages for recruiter calls and sales pitches. Reports results only on the sales-pitch scenario due to limited evaluation resources.

entry.title: Comparing Classical and Quantum Machine Learning for Regression in High Energy Physics Collision Data

author.name: Tariq Mahmood, Zain ul Abidin, Itzel Luviano Soto, Alfredo Raya

entry.summary: Systematically compares classical and quantum ML models (SVM, ANN, CNN, LSTM and quantum counterparts) for regression on CERN Open Data proton-proton collision events in high energy physics.

entry.title: Effectiveness of IoT and Deep Learning for Detection and Severity Assessment of Postelectrotermes militaris in Tea Plantations

author.name: D. K. C. Senevirathna, A. A. E. Nanayakkara, H. M. C. K. Kulathunga, J. K. D. P. Nadula, R. M. Mapatuna, Malithi Nawarathne, Jaliya L. Wijayaraja, P. D. Senanayake, Samitha Vidhanaarachchi, Kalpani Manathunga

entry.summary: Combines IoT acoustic monitoring on a Raspberry Pi with deep learning to detect and grade termite (ULWT) infestations in tea plantations from trunk audio, using 2,000 labeled ten-second samples with spatial tracking. Enables early, non-invasive agricultural pest detection.

entry.title: Context Localization for Generalized Level-Based Evaluation in Knowledge-Based Systems

author.name: Ondrej Hutn\'{i}k, Nat\'{a}lia Pu\v{s}k\'{a}rov\'{a}

entry.summary: Studies context localization for generalized level-based evaluation in knowledge-based systems, characterizing when filtering a score by a context equals localizing admissible contexts by intersection. Main theorem gives necessary and sufficient structural conditions for this consistency across all monotone set functions.

entry.title: A Deep Learning-Based Stacking Ensemble Framework for Turbofan Engine Remaining Useful Life Prediction

author.name: Limon Bin Hossain, Md. Salehin Seyam, Md Rashedul Islam, Abdur Rahman, Md Sharifuzzaman

entry.summary: A two-level stacking ensemble (LSTM, CNN, CNN-LSTM, CNN-GRU with XGBoost meta-learner) for turbofan engine remaining useful life prediction on NASA C-MAPSS FD001/FD003, achieving competitive RMSE and R-squared.

entry.title: Texture Image Classification Using DWT AlexNet Feature Fusion and Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Arun D. Kulkarni

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid DWT + AlexNet deep feature fusion framework for texture image classification, combining handcrafted wavelet features with learned deep features.

entry.title: Empowering Local Agriculture: A Deep Learning-Powered Web System for Identifying Bangladeshi Mango Varieties

author.name: Monowar Islam, Safaruzzaman Shovo

entry.summary: A deep learning web system for identifying nine Bangladeshi mango varieties from 2,013 collected images, fine-tuning ResNet18/50 and EfficientNetB0 under consistent conditions.

entry.title: PhenoIntel: A Lifecycle-Aligned Multi-Agent Web Application for Verified, Accessible Plant Phenotype Analysis

author.name: Narendren S V, Soumyashree Kar

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.27999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing conversational plant-phenotyping platforms are difficult for plant scientists to use and lack the reliability scientific research demands: fai...

entry.title: SciReC: Diagnostic Evaluation of Multimodal, Multi-Turn Relational Reasoning with Adaptive Interaction

author.name: Nilay Yilmaz, Naga Sai Abhiram Kusumba, Stella Wenxing Liu, Yezhou Yang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.27461v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relational reasoning requires the process of perceptual understanding, comparing, and integrating the underlying relationships between concepts. This...

entry.title: Sledgehammer or Scalpel? A Fine-grained Adaptive Framework for Implicit Hate Speech

author.name: Han Wang, Yuhu Cheng, Xuesong Wang, Yi Zhu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.27462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unlike explicit attacks with obvious profanity, implicit hate speech hides malice within seemingly compliant expressions through metaphors and contex...

entry.title: The Effect of Emotional Context on Large Language Models' Endorsement of Premature Decisions: Comparing Emotional Vulnerability Across Six Commercial Models

author.name: Cheolho Shin, Yoojin Han, Donghun Shin, Kunho Lee

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.27465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for everyday decision-making advice, whether a model shifts the direction of its advice accordi...

entry.title: PACE: Publisher-Adaptive Content Extraction via Agentic Automation

author.name: Zhanlin Liu, Munirathnam Srikanth

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.27466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Web content extraction is essential for reliable LLM data pipelines, yet existing methods often struggle to jointly satisfy accuracy, scalability, an...

entry.title: UIC-AIHealth4All at ArchEHR-QA 2026: Answer-First Evidence Grounding for Clinical Question Answering

author.name: Mohammad Arvan, Hossein Haeri, Natalie Parde, Rebecca T. Feinstein

entry.title: Research Summary: August 30, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
This batch is dominated by alignment and AI security work rather than new model releases. Reward hacking is the central theme, addressed from both training-time and inference-time angles.

Safety and alignment:

  • Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF — empirical result from Google DeepMind's Amplified Oversight team showing debate-based oversight reduces reward hacking
  • Inference-Time Inoculation Against RL-Induced Misalignment — novel approach countering RL-induced split personas at deployment while preserving RL capability gains
  • Value generalisation theory of change — frames value generalisation as a primary alignment pathway

Agent foundations:

  • Is there only one FairBot? — highest-scored item; unifies independently proposed definitions of FairBot via fixed points and arithmetic soundness in GL, with a real proof sketch

Security:

  • METR and Redwood postmortem of the HuggingFace hack delivers actionable lessons for AI lab security practice

Futures and policy:

  • Chokepoints book notes give a framework for economic statecraft relevant to compute governance
  • Keeping human skills alive and AI Tweets offer original commentary on automation and near-term expectations

Two low-substance items (a personal career reflection and a derivative effective-altruism essay) fill the remaining slots; an event announcement and a placeholder item were excluded.

entry.title: Is there only one FairBot?

author.name: transhumanist_atom_understander

entry.summary: A technical analysis of the FairBot agent from MIRI's prisoner's dilemma tournament, showing that several independently- proposed definitions (Slepnev's biconditional formulation, James Payor's cooperation condition) are provably equivalent theorems of Gödel-Löb provability logic. The author speculates on why the space of provability-based agents appears so constrained. This is original work in formal decision theory and proof-based agent design, relevant to logical-indicator approaches to cooperation.

entry.title: You Should Still Save Drowning Children (Even If They’re Far Away)

author.name: James Brobin

entry.summary: An introductory essay on effective altruism extending Singer's drowning-child analogy to distant, cost-effective charitable giving. It argues that obligations to donate apply equally regardless of geographic distance. This is a re-rendering of well-established arguments aimed at newcomers rather than a research contribution.
